News.title: How underworld ‘fixer’ behind £3m drugs ring built secret life in Costa del Crime before web of lies came crashing down
News.content:
COCAINE KING How underworld ‘fixer’ behind £3m drugs ring built secret life in Costa del Crime before web of lies came crashing down

AS gangster Craig Bennett swaggered into a posh hotel in Barcelona he must have thought himself untouchable.

But his reign as a top criminal broker for Britain’s criminal underground was about to come to a crashing end after five years hiding out in luxury apartments on Spain’s Costa del Sol.



As he walked into the hotel bar, cops swooped in to arrest Bennett who helped flood the UK with cocaine and ketamine and supplied firearms to crooks in a £3.75million operation.

In a sinister twist, police also discovered he was trying to offload a deadly gun with a silencer that he bought from a thug in south-east London.



A top cop told The Sun: “It was like an assassin’s weapon.”

Bennett, 41, originally from Uxbridge, west London, lived the high life in Spain with a contacts book stuffed with criminals who he helped supply drugs, firearms and money laundering services.



He was a fixer who brokered handovers between thugs and clients, exchanging passwords, locations, timings and car details in exchange for a slice of the profits.

He also had a gang of couriers in Britain who helped distribute 91 kilos of drugs and illicit cash.



Bennett directed Gerald Tohill, 60, from Bracknell, Berkshire, and Lucien Robinson, 38, from Wokingham to collect and distribute illicit cash and drugs on numerous occasions.

Lucien’s father, 75-year-old Peter Robinson was also involved in hiding cash for the enterprise.

Cops had no idea Bennett was such a big player in the drug and weapons world until 2020 when French police hacked into the secret phone network EncroChat, used by criminals to communicate.

Even his family were shocked by his secret life. They believed he was a legitimate businessman, although it’s not know what he told them he did.

Bennett was back home in Britain seeing a girlfriend when news broke of the Encrochat breakthrough and he quickly fled back to his villa in Spain, which boasted sweeping views of the Costa del Sol.



Messages on Bennett’s phone between March and June 2020 revealed his role in supplying 91.8kilos of drugs with the help of a criminal gang back home in the UK.

He was also trying to flog two guns, including one with a silencer he bought for £5,000 in Mottingham, London.

Senior investigating officer John Turner, of the National Crime Agency – Britain’s version of the FBI, told The Sun: “It was a loaded firearm with 50 bullets and a silencer, almost like an assassin’s weapon, very sinister.



“Bennett had some minor convictions in the UK but was good at leaving no trace of what he was up to.

“He never got his own hands dirty but was always getting a cut of the deals he brokered. You have to have good contacts to do that.

“The men who helped him worked non-stop, they were organised, their bookkeeping and communication had to be good. It’s a shame they didn’t put that effort into conventional work because they certainly put the hours in.

“We only had a tiny two month window into a small part of his operations and there were no doubt more.”

Bennett was arrested in July last year and extradited back to Britain the following month.



Sources said his partner, a woman with her own business in Kent, was “blindsided” by Bennett’s criminality as were his family.

He loved to boast of his lifestyle, sending fellow gangsters images of views from the balcony of his apartment.

John Turner added: “Had it not been for Encrochat he might never have got caught.

“The encrypted platform allowed criminals to grow networks and they became extremely confident in their interactions. They thought they were beyond the reach of the law.

How cops brought down EncroChat EncroChat was a company which sold encrypted phones, which were used for illegal business. It was one of the largest providers of encrypted communications, used by 60,000 users worldwide, and around 10,000 users in the UK and offered a secure mobile phone instant messaging service. The sole use was for coordinating and planning the distribution of illicit commodities, money laundering and plotting to kill rival criminals. The phones cost up approximately £1,600 to buy and were modified Android devices. The encrypted phone industry generally advertises its phones as capable of resisting lawful attempts to gain access to their contents – either in the face of attacks or through police monitoring. What’s more, EncroChat users could enter a PIN, which would immediately delete all messages on the device. From 2016, the National Crime Agency (NCA) had been working with international law enforcement to target EncroChat, and in 2020, they managed to infiltrate the platform. A breakthrough in the operation came in January 2020 when the French developed a hack, whereby a software update – actually spyware – would be sent to all phones on the platform. Once updated, the gangs unknowingly gave agencies unprecedented access to organised crime gangs’ secret communications. In 2020, authorities arrested 746 suspected top-tier criminals who are believed to be involved in murder, gun smuggling and drug trafficking crimes, and seized £54m in cash and 1.5 tonnes of cocaine. Investigations and arrests have been ongoing ever since.



“Bennett was out in Spain living the good life and there was no real profile on him but that came to an end when EncroChat was cracked.

“He was the lynchpin of this conspiracy to bring harmful drugs into the UK and directed the movements of members of his gang.”

Bennett was jailed 14 years last month for conspiracy to supply drugs including cannabis, cocaine and ketamine as well as conspiracy to sell a weapon and ammo.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

His accomplice Tohil was earlier given nine years for conspiracy to supply drugs and conspiracy to conceal, convert or transfer criminal property. Lucien Robinson was caged for five years on drug charges while his dad Peter, of Bracknell, Berks, was given a 12 month suspended sentence for conspiracy to conceal criminal property.

News.title: Developer’s plans to turn 19ft garage into Sandbanks mansion rejected for FOURTH time – as he launches scathing attack
News.content:
PLOT TWIST Developer’s plans to turn 19ft garage into Sandbanks mansion rejected for FOURTH time – as he launches scathing attack

A DEVELOPER’S plans to turn a 19ft-wide garage into a mansion on Millionaire’s Row have been rejected for a fourth time.

Peter Mullins launched a scathing attack on officials after spending five years seeking permission to transform the £600,000 site on the exclusive resort of Sandbanks in Poole, Dorset.



After his plans to flip the tiny garage on the peninsula were rejected a fourth time, Peter appealed the decision.

In the appeal, his planning consultant Colin Henry accused officials of a “personal attack” against his client.



In a blistering letter to the planning inspector, Colin claimed the council’s decision was “emotionally charged” and the requirements being suggested were “unreasonably complex”.

He also suggested the council was unfairly singling out Peter’s development, stating new build homes in the surrounding area had been approved without the same kind of scrutiny.

The tirade fell on deaf ears as the inspector dismissed the appeal, sending Peter back to the drawing board.

In 2021, the property developer bought the garage on the sought-after strip where a home could be worth more than £1million.



After failing to get permission for a pair of slim semi-detached houses and then for two flats, he put a pitched roof on the garage, claiming the leaky flat one had reached the end of its life.

But once the work was done, he applied for a change of use to turn the garage into a two-bed pad with most of the living space in the new roof he had created.

Both attempts were refused by planning officers, with Bournemouth, Christchurch and Poole (BCP) council citing the main reason as flood risk.



The council’s flood expert, Richard Gazzard, said the developer has had “ample opportunity” to show they have a working water drainage system but have “failed to do so”.

He believed the evidence found that drainage changes had actually increased the risk of surface water on neighbouring properties since Peter bought the site.

Richard also said the flood warning and evacuation plan was “poorly written” and clearly done “to simply pass planning” and would “likely put occupants at substantial risk of harm”.

Colin replied by stating: “This is an emotionally charged and unreasonably complex set of requirements for a simple change of use.

“They are not proportional to the development proposed, often straying into detailed design and building regulations territory.



“Has the inspector, in their career, witnessed such a high level of scrutiny over an existing soakaway or a flood warning and evacuation plan?

“To penalise an existing structural footprint while actively approving large new-build dwellings all around it violates the principles of rational decision-making and reasonableness.”

He added that Richard’s statement relied “heavily on emotive language, unverified assumptions, and AI generated misinformation to discredit an existing, functioning drainage system”.

“Ignoring the personal attack, which seems wholly inappropriate and disproportionate in the course of a planning appeal, the LLPA officer’s statement does not answer the question asked,” he said.

But planning inspector Sylvia Leonard said she agreed with the previous inspectors that the proposal was not suitable due to the flood risk.



She said: “I am not persuaded that this would be a safe evacuation option for future occupiers.

“I am not satisfied, based on the information before me, that residual risks can be safely managed or that there is an appropriate emergency plan in place that provides for safe access and escape routes.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“As such, I cannot be certain that future occupiers of the proposed dwelling would be safe during a flood event.”

Peter and Collin have not responded to requests for comment, and The Sun has reached out to the council.

News.title: ‘Truth’ about Jimmy Hoffa’s disappearance revealed in prison confession – FBI could have it solved in days, expert says
News.content:
A PRISON confession and old Mafia dump site could be the key to solving the decades-long mystery of crooked labor union boss Jimmy Hoffa’s disappearance, a veteran investigative journalist has said.

The case of Hoffa has remained unsolved for over 50 years since the former president of the International Brotherhood of Teamsters vanished from a restaurant in Michigan on July 30, 1975.



Hoffa, who was 62 years old at the time, was scheduled to meet with two mafia figures at the Machus Red Fox Restaurant, north of Detroit, that afternoon, but was believed to have been stood up.

He was last heard from when he called his wife to inform her that the meeting had been a bust and that he’d be home at 4pm for dinner.



However, Hoffa never made it for dinner and his car was later found abandoned in the parking lot of the restaurant he’d called from.

What happened to Hoffa in those final moments has remained a mystery over the last 51 years since he was last seen.

Read more in The U.S. Sun LAW GONE WRONG Ex-cop 'kills 3 before trying to sneak back over US border with son, 3'

Dan Moldea, an author and independent investigative journalist, believes he’s solved the case and has pinpointed Hoffa’s final resting place to an infamous landfill in New Jersey once linked to the Genovese crime family.

Through hours of interviews with FBI officials, Teamsters members, and key Mafia figures from both the Genovese and Detroit factions, Moldea has pieced together the most detailed account of Hoffa’s final hours.



And it all began with a prison confession a week after Hoffa’s disappearance between two Genovese associates, Steve Andretta and Ralph Picardo, who was serving a 20-year sentence for manslaughter.

Andretta visited Picardo, the mobster turned FBI informant, in prison in early August 1975 and disclosed the details of Hoffa’s grim murder and where his body was taken.

Picardo then relayed Andretta’s alleged confession to the FBI, which Moldea claims he was later able to firm up in several interviews with Philip “Brother” Moscato, the co-owner of PJP landfill in Jersey City and Genovese associate, beginning in 2007.

Evidence and alleged confessions collected by Moldea suggest Hoffa was whacked shortly after he was stood up at the Red Fox Restaurant.



That afternoon, Hoffa was scheduled to meet with Anthony “Tony Jack” Giacalone, a Detroit mobster, and Anthony “Tony Pro” Provenzano, the head of a Teamsters association in Union City, New Jersey, and a capo in the Genovese crime family.

For years, Hoffa was suspected of colluding with the mob and in 1967 was charged and convicted of jury tampering, landing him a four-year prison sentence.

The July 30 meeting was Hoffa’s latest effort in his attempt to regain his old title as the Teamsters president – a reinstatement the Mafia opposed.

Moldea claims that after being stood up, Hoffa was picked up by Vito “Billy Jack” Giacalone, the brother of Anthony Giacalone and another made man in the Detroit Mafia, and taken to the house of mob associate Lenny Schultz.



There Hoffa was allegedly killed by Salvatore “Sally Bugs” Briguglio, a capo with the Genovese crime family.

“Hoffa was murdered in Detroit, stuffed into a 55 gallon drum, loaded onto a gateway transportation truck, and shipped to New Jersey,” Moldea told The U.S. Sun.

The steel drum allegedly containing Hoffa’s body was shipped to PJP landfill and received by Paul Cappola, the co-owner of the Jersey City dump site, and on the orders of Moscato, his business partner and Genovese associate, buried the remains.

But instead of burying the drum on the landfill site as instructed by Moscato, Cappola allegedly buried Hoffa adjacent to the dump, under the Pulaski Skyway.

“He takes a hole about 15 feet deep with a ramp. He created a ramp for himself because it’s so deep, he puts off his body at the bottom of this hole,” Moldea said.



“And then he puts 15 to 30 steel barrels on top of them, which are filled with toxic waste, adhesives specifically.

“[Cappola] then bulldozers the whole thing flat, [but] instead of burying a body where Moscato told him to bury it at the dump, he buried it off site, not on the dump, but in an alcove under the Pulaski Skyway, which is controlled by the state of New Jersey,” Moldea said.

“There should be nothing buried there. Nothing. It’s adjacent to the dump, but it’s not part of the dump. And there’s nothing buried there.”



Moldea claims he was able to determine why the mob transported Hoffa’s body more than 600 miles from Detroit to the Jersey City landfill.

Genovese capo Anthony Provenzano wanted Hoffa close-by as insurance for any potential deal with the FBI, Moldea said.

“There was a murder charge against Tony Provenzano and he was guilty of that murder,” Moldea told The U.S. Sun.

“They needed something to bargain with. And so the bargaining chip became Hoffa’s body. They needed it close by. They needed it accessible.”

Through interviews with Cappola’s sons, Frank and Paul Jr., Moldea said he was able to tour the PJP landfill site in October 2019 and was shown the exact location Hoffa’s remains were buried.



Moldea described the site as the size of a little league infield and with the help of forensic engineers investigated the alcove on two separate visits.

During two visits to the site in November 2021 and April 2022, the group used sophisticated ground-penetrating radar (GPR) technology to scan the area, both scans identified an underground anomaly, Moldea said.

“You could see the scans where there appears to be a bunch of barrels and then there’s one barrel at the very bottom,” he told The U.S. Sun.

Moldea shared the findings with the FBI, who executed two search warrants at the location in late 2021 and in June 2022.

The FBI’s initial search with subterranean radar technology yielded no trace of Hoffa’s remains.



When the federal agency returned in June 2022, Moldea claims the FBI botched the excavation due to a mix of bad weather and searching in the wrong location.

“The one place that was detected by ground penetrating radar was not looked at, was not even examined,” Moldea said.

“They didn’t even stick a shovel in anything. Nothing. It was pristine ground.”



The FBI officially ruled that the excavations yielded nothing of evidentiary value related to Hoffa’s body or any other human remains.

Moldea said he’s sent letters to the FBI, including director Kash Patel, about conducting another excavation at the alcove, but his requests have largely been ignored.

“We’ve been trying to get the FBI to dig in that spot since. [But] unfortunately, there has been repair work going on on the bridge and that alcove has been completely and totally worked on,” he added.

“‘I’ve sent open letters to both Kash Patel and Pam Bondi, when she was AG, saying this is an easy one for you guys.

“Just go down. You don’t even have to make a big deal about it. Just go down and with the ground penetrating radar we’ll show you exactly where it is.



“But we can’t seem to get these people to do the right thing.”

Moldea said he was advised against conducting an independent excavation by environmentalists due to the toxic filled steel drums on top of what he believes are Hoffa’s remains.

“The reason why we can’t go up there and just do it ourselves is that there’s 15 to 30 steel drums filled with toxic waste on top of Hoffa that’s been there for 51 years under pressure,” he said.

“That’s what we’ve been advised by environmental people, that if you crack that ground under all that pressure.

“There could be an explosion, there could be a plume of gas that comes out of the ground because those steel drums probably have cracked open, and there must be a lot of pressure there.



“So we need an environmental specialist team to come in and do this excavation.”

Moldea continued, “You know, I’m 76 years old. I want this to be my swan song. I want this to be my final act, and I don’t know if that’s going to happen or not.

“I’m hoping the FBI decide to do something, do the right thing and pick up the phone and call me and say, ‘Dan, you’ve been right. Congratulations. Come on up.'”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Hoffa was legally declared dead in December 1982.

The FBI’s investigation into Hoffa’s disappearance remains open.

News.title: Teen rapist, 19, behind huge fire that tore through 150-year-old mill used in Peaky Blinders & Downton Abbey faces jail
News.content:
A VILE teen rapist behind a huge fire that tore through a 150-year-old mill used to film Peaky Blinders and Downton Abbey faces jail.

Keaton Greenman, 19, was convicted of causing a devastating fire at Dalton Mills, in Bradford, West Yorkshire, back in August 2024.



He was found guilty of arson alongside McKenzie Mottran, now 20, at Bradford Youth Court – but Greenman could not be sentenced due to a then-looming separate trial for serious sexual offences.

On Friday (August 7) he was found guilty of three counts of rape against the same victim following a trial at Bradford Crown Court.



The 19-year-old, formerly of Shelby Grange, Shipley, faced four counts of rape and five counts of sexual assault dating back to 2024.

He was acquitted by a jury of one count of rape and all charges of sexual assault.

Following the sentencing, Greenman and Mottran can be sentenced for their role in the arson on the Grade II*-listed Genappe Mill – used as filming location for the hit TV show Peaky Blinders.

They were originally due to be sentenced in January, but Recorder Mark Giuliani adjourned the sentencing of both until Greenman’s rape matters had been dealt with.



Sentencing has been adjourned for at least eight weeks.

Videos on the pair’s mobile phones showed them exploring the mill and finding a small fire, which Greenman fed using pieces of a polystyrene gargoyle which may have been left behind by a film crew.

The resulting fire, which quickly spread through the building, involved more than 100 firefighters, 20 fire engines and other specialist equipment and took three days to put out.

Damage to the mill was estimated to be £15million.

Once the largest textile mill in Yorkshire – employing more than 2,000 workers – it was built by Joseph Craven in 1869, replacing the original mill from the 1780s.



As well as Peaky Blinders, it has been used for The Great Train Robbery, Downton Abbey and 2016 film The Limehouse Golem, starring Bill Nighy.

News.title: Student, 21, dies after plunging from window while on hiking trail as tributes flood in for ‘kind beloved sister’
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

FREAK ACCIDENT Student, 21, dies after plunging from window while on hiking trail as tributes flood in for ‘kind beloved sister’

A STUDENT has died in a freak accident after falling from a window while hiking on a popular trail.

Dayanara Nicole Urbina Ruiz, 21, suffered multiple blunt force injuries in the fall and was tragically pronounced dead at the scene.



The UCLA student plunged from a window overlooking the popular Burke-Gilman Trail in King County, Washington on July 30.

Her death has since been ruled accidental.



Just moments beforehand, a friend reportedly phoned 911 to say that Dayanara was “extremely” drunk and running around in the street.

However, her family have denied these claims.



Dayanara’s sister, Catherine, told The California Post: “My sister was not like that.

“She was on the other side of the world last year on an internship. She went to a music festival. She had fun and like I said, she was very responsible.



“She’s not one to get, like she described her, sloppy or too drunk. No, that’s not my sister.”

Catherine continued: “My sister is the kind of woman that always puts her priorities first. She was not like that. She was absolutely not like that,”

Dayanara was studying communications at the prestigious California university and had been working as a summer marketing intern at Amazon Web Services in Seattle.

The 21-year-old was the co-president of UCLA’s first fashion club and a beloved member of the Phi Lambda Rho sorority.

Her family, the Urbina and Ruiz family, has since launched a GoFundMe to help cover her funeral costs.



The fundraiser set a goal of $28,000 and has already raised around $25,000 in just over a week.

The description reads: “She was a bright light and a gentle soul.

“God bless all who keep Dayanara in their prayers.”

Dayanara’s sorority has also paid tribute to the 21-year-old student.

A spokesperson for Phi Lambda Rho said: “Omega Chapter gained a new angel.



“It is with profound sadness that we share the passing of our beloved sister, Dayanara Nicole Urbina Ruiz.

“Dayanara was a bright light, a gentle soul, and someone whose kindness touched everyone around her.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“She was always there for those in need, offering support, hope, and compassion without hesitation.

“Her memory will forever remain a part of our sisterhood, and her impact will continue to live on through the lives she touched.”

News.title: Desperate new plea in hunt for killer after woman, 23, strangled to death before naked body dumped in field 32 years ago
News.content:
COLD CASE MYSTERY Desperate new plea in hunt for killer after woman, 23, strangled to death before naked body dumped in field 32 years ago

POLICE have launched a fresh appeal for information about a woman who was strangled to death 32 years ago.

The naked body of Julie Finley, 23, was abandoned in a carrot field in 1994, but the killer still hasn’t been brought to justice.



Now cops have launched a new bid for information about her brutal murder

Her body was discovered by a cyclist in a field near the Rainford bypass, north-west of St Helens in Merseyside in 1994.



Julie was last seen in Liverpool city centre on Friday, August 5, 1994, talking to a white man believed to be in his 20s or 30s at approximately 11pm behind Royal Liverpool University Hospital.

Then, another witness saw someone matching Julie’s description in the early hours of the next morning at around 2:30am on Saturday, August 6.



The witness claimed he saw a young woman arguing with a man outside the Wheatsheaf Public House, close to where Julie’s body was found.

He also said the man was trying to force the young woman into a white transit van.

Detective Inspector Sam Davies from the major incident team said: “It is 32 years since Julie was murdered but the investigation into her death remains ongoing.



“We know that back in 1994 people may have had information about Julie’s death which, either through loyalty or fear, they didn’t bring to our attention.

“My message would be it is never too late to do the right thing and tell us what you know, no matter how small. One piece of information could be key to solving the case and bringing the person responsible to justice.”

Ten months after Julie’s murder, on Friday, July 21, 1995, a man picked up a hitchhiker at the junction of East Lancashire Road and Rainford Bypass.

The lead detective at the time, DCI Francis Youell, later told BBC’s Crimewatch that the hitchhiker had become extremely agitated when they approached the site where Julie was found.

He told the driver of the vehicle that ten months before, his motorcycle had broken down in the lay-by close to where Julie’s body was found.



He said that while he was fixing his bike, he heard bangs and screams coming from a van and, when he approached the van and opened the doors, he saw a young woman.

She was naked and said, ‘help me, help me, for god’s sake, help me’, before a man appeared and told him to get on his way.

The hitchhiker said the man told him the woman was his girlfriend and then the hitchhiker drove off.

The man was in his mid-20s, about 5ft 8 with clean-cut, blond short hair and was believed to be from St Helens and en route to Ainsdale in Merseyside to see his grandfather.

He has never been traced.



In 2014, Miss Finley’s elderly parents released photographs from her childhood in a bid to shake someone’s conscience and provide new information.

At that time, Miss Finley’s mother said: “Albie and I have been put through 20 years of hell and torment and Julie’s sudden and tragic loss has affected the whole family.

“It’s difficult to explain what the last 20 years have been like, but for me I still feel like it’s 1994 and I’m constantly waiting for Julie to come through the door, but she never does and never will.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Police have said they “remain committed” to helping Miss Finley’s family get justice.

Anyone with information about her death has been asked to message @MerPolCC, call 101 or contact Crimestoppers anonymously by calling 0800 555 111.

News.title: Woman’s body discovered in suitcase by side of road as cops launch probe in Australia
News.content:
A WOMAN’S body has been found stuffed in a suitcase on the side of a rural road in Australia.

Police rushed to the crime scene after a horrified member of the public made the grim discovery.



The suitcase has been seized for a forensic exam and detectives have launched a probe.

Cops are yet to release details about how long the body had been abandoned in the quiet New South Wales area.



Officers in high-vis cordoned off the scene on Wolgon Road at Oallen, just over an hour’s drive north-east of the Australian capital Canberra.

They were forced to hold umbrellas over their equipment as rain made it difficult to photograph the scene.



A NSW police spokesperson said: “The body is yet to be formally identified; however, it is believed to be female.”

It may have been left at the site for quite some time.

The discovery comes as the case of a Brit woman who was found stuffed in a suitcase in Athens has made global headlines.

Scottish aid worker Elisabeth Ross, 38, was found dumped in a derelict building near the city centre on July 18.



After her body was identified 11 days later, cops zeroed in on Afghan boxer Sharif Ahmadzai, 26, who has since been charged with her murder.

Ahmadzai’s US-born wife Alaina Hall allegedly reported her husband to cops after she became suspicious he was involved in Elisabeth’s death.

The couple had met the Brit through their shared charity work and developed a friendship.

On July 15, Alaina says she saw a text message sent from Elisabeth, known as Lisa, to him which read: “Thank you for your intention to come with me.”

Later that night, Alaina claimed in her testimony that she woke up and found her husband had left their home without any warning.



She said: “I checked his location on my cell phone. I saw that he was inside [Lisa’s rental] apartment on Rethymno Street.

“I was surprised because there was no particular reason for him to be there at that time.”

Later that night, Alaina claimed in her testimony that she woke up and found her husband had left their home without any warning.

She said: “I checked his location on my cell phone. I saw that he was inside the apartment on Rethymno Street.

“I was surprised because there was no particular reason for him to be there at that time.”



Ahmadzai looks set to spend the next 18 months with terrorists, rapists and murderers in Greece’s toughest prison as he awaits his trial.

Elisabeth’s devastated family paid tribute to her on Thursday – describing her as “kind, principled and selfless”.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

They said: “Her integrity was absolute, and she dedicated her life to helping others in need.

“We are in deep pain, and we ask for time and privacy as we come to terms with our loss.”

News.title: Andy Burnham mulls Railcard changes in plan to cut high train ticket prices
News.content:
Andy Burnham mulls Railcard changes in plan to cut high train ticket prices

EXCLUSIVE: New Prime Minister Andy Burnham is considering extending access to railcards as part of early discussions on how to cut train ticket prices, The Mirror understands

View 2 Images The Prime Minister has said cutting rail fares is in his 'sights' (Image: POOL/AFP via Getty Images)

Andy Burnham is considering extending access to railcards as part of early discussions on how to cut train ticket prices, The Mirror understands.

‌



The Prime Minister has said cutting rail fares is in his “sights”, with some prices “outrageously” high at the moment.

‌



In a signal of intent last week, he announced plans to extend the 16-17 Saver Railcard so youngsters can access it up until the day before their 19th birthday, instead of it expiring when they turn 18. The change will come into force on August 17, benefitting thousands of students with 50% off rail tickets.

‌



Government sources said discussions are taking place on extending other railcards, with talks at a “very early stage”. Officials are looking at a range of options around how to tackle the high cost of prices that go further than the rail freeze introduced this year, the Mirror has been told.

Two influential left-wing think tanks are now urging Mr Burnham to expand the network south east railcard into a national railcard.

Andy Burnham says more cost of living help on its way as struggling families in his sights READ MORE :

View 2 Images In a signal of intent last week, Andy Burnham announced plans to extend the 16-17 Saver Railcard (Image: POOL/AFP via Getty Images)

‌



The railcard, which costs £35 a year, gives train users a third off most rail fares for journeys in London and the south east. Anyone 16 years and above can buy one.

Elsewhere in the country, railcards exist for particular age groups including adults aged up to 30 or those over 60, or groups including disabled people or veterans, but there is not a universal discount card. It means adults aged 31 to 59 are unable to access this discount outside the south east.

Zoë Billingham, director of IPPR North, who informally advised Mr Burnham on an unpaid sabbatical this summer, said it is not “coherent” that the universal railcard only exists in one part of the country.

‌



She told The Mirror: “I do think there would be a sensible question at this stage that says, well, given the kind of unfairness from the passengers' perspective, from the public's perspective of just having a network railcard that covers the south east, why shouldn't that be something that's offered more broadly?

“So I would be very supportive of the government looking at that for the country as a whole. Fundamentally, transport is about jobs, it's about connecting people socially.

“But it also helps the government with its climate goals, getting people off cars and onto more green modes of transport. So it ticks a lot of boxes and so I'd be really supportive of the government moving in that direction.”

‌



Ms Billingham added that as the network railcard is already an established scheme, an extension of it could be “mobilised quickly”. This compares to longer term structural fare reforms that are likely to be looked at as part of rail nationalisation under Great British Railways.

Hannah Peaton, deputy chief executive at the New Economics Foundation (NEF), echoed that an extension of the southeast railcard is an “obvious opportunity” to make the system more equal across the country.

She told The Mirror: “If you take an off-peak, non-advanced journey from London to Milton Keynes, it costs around £23/24, and that's similar to the cost of a trip from Manchester to Leeds.

‌



“But for no real reason, the Milton Keynes trip is eligible for the one third discount, and the Manchester/Leeds one isn't. Which, if you take that in the context of Burnham being very specific that he really wants to ensure equivalent living standards in all parts of the UK, it just feels like an obvious opportunity to equalise it.”

NEF, which last month produced a report looking at bus and rail fares, estimates the policy would generate £425million in consumer savings.

Its modelling suggests it would have a net cost of £270m in the first year, falling to £120m over the long-term, however it said new ticket sales and card sales would to a large extent offset the costs of the scheme.

‌



Ms Peaton added: “I suppose the other really exciting thing about the policy is it effectively pays for itself…So it feels like a no-brainer. It's a chance to take an existing benefit that, for no real reason, only applies to the south east.”

In an interview with The Mirror earlier this month, Mr Burnham said the cost of living is at the top of his priorities list. "I think rail fares are too high, outrageously so in some instances,” he added. “So that's something that's in my sights.”

Mr Burnham used his first days in Downing Street to roll out a rapid-fire list of cost of living announcements. VAT will be slashed from electricity bills from October, bus fares will be capped at £2 and pubs, social clubs and live music venues will get a 20% cut to business rates from April.

Article continues below

At last year’s Budget, former Chancellor Rachel Reeves announced a freeze on rail fares for the first time in 30 years, though prices of tickets still remain high.

Announcing the 16-17 Saver Railcard extension last week, Rail Minister Lord Peter Hendy said: "This kind of common-sense change is exactly what passengers should expect from the railway.”

News.title: 'I worked for Royal Family and had to make bizarre check in case Princess Anne was jailed'
News.content:
'I worked for Royal Family and had to make bizarre check in case Princess Anne was jailed'

A former royal aide has revealed the unusual preparations that were made before Princess Anne faced court over an incident involving one of her dogs

View 3 Images The Princess Royal (Image: PA)

A former royal aide has revealed an extraordinary security precaution that had to be taken before Princess Anne appeared in court.

‌



Ailsa Anderson, who served as Press Secretary to Queen Elizabeth II, was speaking to The Sun’s Royal Exclusive host Matt Wilkinson and royal journalist Phil Dampier when she recalled the remarkable preparations surrounding the case.

‌



It came after Princess Anne pleaded guilty to an offence involving one of her dogs — but behind the scenes, royal officials had to prepare for an outcome nobody wanted to see.

‌



Ailsa explained that she had been present at Slough Magistrates’ Court in 2002, where the Princess Royal faced the charge after her English bull terrier, known as Dotty, attacked two children.

The former royal staff member said: “I was there in Slough Magistrates’ Court. She lost control of her dogs. She pleaded guilty.”

But the conversation then took an unexpected turn.

‌



View 3 Images Princess Anne (Image: 2026 Getty Images)

“Yeah. Again, we had to recce the courts beforehand and look at the jails downstairs just in case they pushed her down.”

Phil initially remembered the incident as involving a cyclist, before Anderson clarified: “No, it was children. It was a child in Windsor Great Park.”

‌



Matt then asked: “Sorry, sorry. You had to check the cells?”

Ailsa replied: “Yes, just in case she was sent down.” Matt then asked: “That could have happened?” before Ailsa confirmed: “We checked the cells.”

The extraordinary preparations were carried out for security reasons, with Ailsa explaining that officials needed to know what was inside the cells and who might be there.

‌



“There were a few,” she said when asked whether there were criminals downstairs.

Asked whether the cells were suitable for a member of the royal family, she replied: “They were basic, Matt. They were basic. Not quite what she was used to, right? But she didn’t have to go to any of these cells.”

Princess Anne ultimately avoided prison, receiving a £500 fine and being ordered to pay £500 compensation. She was also ordered to pay £148 in court costs, while Dotty had to be kept on a lead in public and undergo training.

‌



View 3 Images Princess Anne (Image: WireImage)

The case was particularly significant as it marked the first time a senior member of the Royal Family had been convicted of a criminal offence. No other senior royal had attended court for around a century.

The case against Anne’s husband, Commodore Tim Laurence, was dropped shortly after the hearing began.

‌



The Princess Royal’s punishment was criticised by members of the victims’ families, who were angry that Dotty was not ordered to be put down.

District Judge Penelope Hewitt said the couple were experienced dog owners, but warned that another incident could result in the animal being destroyed.

Despite the preparations made in case Anne was sent to prison, Anderson confirmed the Princess never actually saw the cells herself.

Article continues below

Matt then asked: “Did she go to look at them herself?”

“No. No,” Ailsa replied.

News.title: Banksy in pictures - guerrilla artists' best-known works as bills to remove pieces soar
News.content:
Iconic pieces of street art by the elusive artist Banksy have cost the taxpayer around £150,000 in security and removal fees.

A mural on the side of the Royal Courts of Justice has cost the Department of Justice £85,000 so far in security fees and clean up efforts.

A painting of a judge wielding a gavel at a protester lying on the floor with a bloodied placard appeared on the side of the Grade II-listed London building, in September 2025. The artwork was quickly covered with large plastic sheets and metal barriers while clean up efforts started.

The MoJ has spent £50,000 so far trying to remove the mural while an extra £35,300 had gone towards security fees and overtime, according to a Freedom of Information request by the BBC.

Other works of art that resulted in big bills for the taxpayer include a statue of a man carrying a flag which covered his face, on a plinth in Waterloo Place, near Trafalgar Square. £60,000 was spent by Westminster City Council on security guard & admin.

Another costly piece of art was a police sentry box in the City of London, which was sprayed with images of piranhas in 2024. This set back the City of London Police £2,200 to remove the box.

News.title: Met Office maps show solar eclipse will be most visible in 42 counties – full list
News.content:
Met Office maps show solar eclipse will be most visible in 42 counties – full list

New weather maps have revealed the best spots to catch a glimpse of the solar eclipse in the UK on Wednesday - where dozens of counties will enjoy clear skies

View 5 Images The solar eclipse is due to take place on Wednesday (Image: Getty Images)

The UK is bracing for a historic solar eclipse on Wednesday, considered to be the most significant in decades.

‌



On August 12, more than 90% of the sun will be blocked by the moon between 6.17pm and 8.06pm, leaving a narrow slip of the earth covered in darkness.

‌



While parts of Europe will get to see the eclipse in its totality, the UK will get just a glimpse - but still comes as the most the sun has ever been covered above our skies since the total eclipse witnessed in 1999.

‌



View 5 Images It'll be a major event for the UK (Image: Getty Images)

The next time the moon will cover this much of the sun for Brits will be decades away, in 2081, so many will be wanting to make the most of the occasion this Wednesday.

The Met Office has shared a lit of the best spots to capture the event, with Devon, Cornwall and the westernmost parts of Pembrokeshire, where a range of 94% to 96% of the sun will be obscured by the moon, tipped as the top viewing locations.

‌



Birmingham is expected to seen 91.79% coverage at 7.12pm, 91.41% in London at 7.13pm, 90.74% in Inverness at 7.03pm, 90.71% in Edinburgh at 7.06pm and 90.22% in Newcastle at 7.07pm.

View 5 Images Planetarium Astronomer Dr Carys Herbert demonstrates wearing Celestron solar eclipse glasses (Image: Jordan Pettitt/PA Wire)

Skygazers really keen to catch a sight of the fullest possible solar eclipse should avoid the easternmost parts of the UK, where only 88% to 90% of coverage is expected. These area include the coasts of Norfolk, Yorkshire and Aberdeenshire, as well as the Orkney and Shetland Islands.

‌



The forecast also shows which patches across the country is likely to fall under cloud cover, blocking keen skygazers from catching a glimpse of the eclipse.

View 5 Images The map shows huge parts of the UK will be covered by cloud during the solar eclipse

The cloud cover map at 7pm shows most of Scotland and Northern Ireland will fall under coverage, with only clear night skies predicted for most of the midlands and south of England.

‌



Patches of the north could have some cloud-free spots, like Newcastle, Preston and Sheffield, but Greater Manchester, Leeds Liverpool appear blanketed by cloud.

View 5 Images The map shows clear skies for most of the midlands down to the south

However, it's good news for most of the Midlands downwards, where the east, south and west is almost entirely clear without a cloud in sight, including London.

News.title: Rules if an NHS dentist removes you from their patient list
News.content:
Rules if an NHS dentist removes you from their patient list

Healthwatch England has warned that millions of people are unaware of the rules around NHS dental registration

View 3 Images Patients are free to visit any NHS dentist willing to take them on (Image: Olena Miroshnichenko via Getty Images)

Millions of patients are mistakenly under the impression they hold a permanent place with their NHS dentist once they sign up.

‌



Healthwatch England has cautioned that the reality is far different, warning that surgeries can stop seeing patients once their treatment concludes and they may even remove them following repeated missed appointments. The watchdog's own research revealed that 68% of people wrongly believe they can permanently register with an NHS dentist in the same way they do with a GP.

‌



However, since reforms to the NHS dental contract in 2006, there has been no formal registration system for NHS dentists in England. Instead, patients are taken on for a course of treatment. Once that treatment concludes, the formal arrangement comes to an end, although many practices opt to maintain informal lists of regular patients and invite them back for routine check-ups.

‌



View 3 Images Healthwatch England is supporting calls for a return to GP-style registration (Image: mediaphotos via Getty Images)

Patients are free to visit any NHS dentist willing to take them on, regardless of where they live, as long as the practice is accepting NHS patients. These findings emerge against the backdrop of an ongoing shortage of NHS dental appointments, with increasing numbers of patients either unable to find a dentist or left with no option but to go private.

Healthwatch's polling revealed:.

‌



33% of people said they had waited longer than they wanted for NHS dental treatment.

16% said they had been unable to find an NHS dentist willing to treat them.

27% said they had paid for private dental care during the past two years because they could not access NHS treatment.

The problems stem in part from the way dentists are paid under the NHS contract introduced in 2006. Rather than receiving payment based on the number of registered patients, dentists are remunerated using "Units of Dental Activity" (UDAs) for completing treatments.

Many dentists contend that the system fails to provide adequate funding, prompting growing numbers to cut back their NHS work or move to private practice. According to the British Dental Association, despite the overall number of dentists rising by around 3%, only 23% now say the majority of their work is for the NHS, down from 40% before the pandemic.

‌



You could lose NHS treatment after missed appointments

Patients should also be aware that many NHS dental practices operate "failed to attend" policies. While policies differ between practices, surgeries may refuse to continue providing NHS treatment if patients repeatedly fail to turn up to appointments or regularly cancel at short notice.

For instance, some practices state they may stop treating an NHS patient after two missed appointments within two years, four short-notice cancellations, or a combination of both. Patients are ordinarily warned before this occurs, and practices typically request at least 24 to 48 hours' notice if an appointment needs to be cancelled.

View 3 Images Many practices keep informal patient lists (Image: miljko via Getty Images)

‌



Calls for reform

Healthwatch England is supporting calls for a return to GP-style registration, arguing that patients should once again have the right to remain permanently registered with an NHS dental practice for both routine and urgent care.

The Government is currently in talks with the British Dental Association over reforms to the NHS dental contract, and has launched a recruitment drive designed to boost the number of NHS dentists in areas where access to appointments is most limited.

In the meantime, Healthwatch is calling on dental practices to be more transparent with patients about the fact that they are not permanently registered with an NHS dentist, and to clearly outline what steps are needed to remain a regular NHS patient.

Article continues below

Your NHS dentist rights

You cannot formally register with an NHS dentist in England as you do with a GP.

You can attend any NHS practice that is accepting new NHS patients.

Your NHS arrangement usually ends once your course of treatment has been completed.

Many practices keep informal patient lists, but they are not legally required to do so. Repeated missed appointments or short-notice cancellations may result in a practice deciding not to offer you further NHS treatment, in line with its policy.

News.title: Tommy Fury under fire as he blasts Kim Kardashian for using nannies to raise kids
News.content:
Tommy Fury under fire as he blasts Kim Kardashian for using nannies to raise kids

Kim revealed she has a large team of nannies helping to care for the four children she shares with ex-husband Kanye West and Tommy was not impressed

View 6 Images Tommy was blasted for his views on Kim Kardashian's parenting

Tommy Fury has taken aim at Kim Kardashian over her reported use of nannies – but his comments quickly came back to bite him. The boxer, who shares two children with Molly-Mae Hague, discussed the reality star's parenting arrangements during an episode of his What The Fury podcast with dad, John Fury.

‌



The pair were discussing reports that Kim has a large team of nannies helping to care for the four children she shares with ex-husband Kanye West – North, Saint, Chicago and Psalm.

‌



Reading out a reference to "10 nannies and mannies raising Kim Kardashian's kids", Tommy's dad John didn't hold back. "If you can’t look after these kids yourself, don’t have them," he declared.

‌



6 View 6 Images Kim Kardashian said she has a team of nannies to look after her children 6 View 6 Images Tommy and Molly-Mae have a nanny to help with their kids

Tommy initially acknowledged that they didn't "know the full story", but went on to question parents who rely heavily on childcare.

"I don’t understand people who just dump the kids with nannies and mannies all day…" he said.

‌



However, the former Love Island star then revealed that he and Molly-Mae also have childcare help with their daughter Bambi, three, and baby son Midas, who was born in June.

Explaining the difference as he sees it, Tommy said: "I’m all for having some help on board and help you out – me and Molly, we have help.

View 6 Images Kim has a busy career and has help to look after her brood

‌



"But we’re with Bambi every day, all day; it’s only if I’ve got to go on a call or Molly’s on a call or we’ve got to shoot out. The baby’s looked after all the time."

His comments didn't go down particularly well with some listeners, who were quick to point out that Tommy had criticised Kim's use of childcare before admitting his own family also receives help.

One person hit back: "Leave the woman alone. I can do with 15 nannies as a busy working mother. Not easy. We need and can do with the help. Men judging a hard working business woman."

‌



View 6 Images Kim Kardashian has stated that Kanye can often go months without calling or seeing them their kids

Another branded the comments hypocritical, writing: "A man with a full time nanny judging a woman with a full time nanny!"

"Men. Mansplaining what they have no clue about," a third added.

‌



While another critic claimed: "[Tommy and Molly] have someone on call 24/7 so his argument is completely invalid. Honestly, these people are deluded!"

Kim has previously been reported to have an extensive childcare operation in place to help her balance raising her children with her huge business commitments.

View 6 Images Tommy and Molly-Mae recently welcomed their second child, a son called Midas

‌



It has been claimed her nannies work on a rotation, with childcare available seven days a week and overnight support in place.

Each member of the team is reportedly briefed on the children's individual needs, while a night nanny is said to prepare everything they might need for the following morning, including school supplies and sports kits.

Other members of the childcare team reportedly begin work from 6am and complete 12-hour shifts.
