News.title: Late own goal secures draw for Chelsea against Johor in feisty friendly
News.content:
Johor 3 Chelsea 3

Chelsea ended their Far East tour with a hard-earned, bad-tempered draw against Malaysian champions Johor.

Having played just 24 hours earlier in Jakarta – a 3-0 win over AC Milan – it was no surprise to see Xabi Alonso name a fresh XI, a mixture of players who may well be offloaded before the end of the transfer window, those needing to prove themselves, and youngsters given much-needed game time.

And considering Johor are one game away from setting a new world record of 109 matches unbeaten in the top flight – a run that would surpass the current mark set by Ivorian side Asec Mimosas in the early 1990s – it was also no shock to see the Malaysian powerhouses offer a stern, pre-season test for the west Londoners.

After a good start Chelsea were second best in a first half that should have seen Johor at least two goals to the good. The Malaysian powerhouses controlled the first 45 minutes and were 1-0 up after 14 minutes – a low cross from the left side footed home by Arif Aiman.

The hosts caused the young, inexperienced Chelsea backline a torrid time, especially on the flanks, and Óscar Arribas was guilty of not capitalising on a great chance to double Johor’s lead, his shot, after cutting in from the right, going wide.

While they looked vulnerable at the back Chelsea also struggled to keep possession in attack. But they got an equaliser they scarcely deserved after Liam Delap was manhandled to the ground in the box by Kevin Medina. The striker, who may well leave Stamford Bridge before the transfer window slams shut, fired home the spot kick allowing the visitors to go into the break on level terms.

News.title: Borussia Dortmund beat Arsenal 3-2 to win Emirates Cup
News.content:
Arsenal 2 Borussia Dortmund 3

Arsenal suffered back-to-back pre-season defeats as they lost 3-2 to Borussia Dortmund, who got their hands on the Emirates Cup. A 3-1 loss to Real Betis on Wednesday night in Dublin was followed up by a loss at home to the German outfit.

Borussia Dortmund took the lead at the Emirates inside the opening ten minutes. Felix Nmecha’s incisive pass into the penalty area was met by the run of Samuele Inacio, who made no mistake with a clinical finish into the far corner. Dortmund then doubled their lead just before the half-hour mark as 18-year-old Greek international Konstantinos Karetsas curled one in from the edge of the box.

10 minutes after half-time, Arsenal got a goal back through Ethan Nwaneri, who slotted home from Christos Tzolis’ cross. However, moments after the hosts got themselves back in the game, Dortmund restored their two-goal advantage as Joane Gadou smashed home from a corner. Arsenal kept their hopes alive through Viktor Gyokeres, who converted a penalty after Tzolis was brought down inside the Dortmund penalty area. Dortmund though were able to hold on to claim victory the Emirates Cup. After the full-time whistle, there was a penalty shootout, which Arsenal won 5-4 having not missed a spot kick.

Ahead of kick-off, Bruno Guimaraes was unveiled to the home faithful at the Emirates after completing his £75m move from Newcastle on Saturday. Arsenal still have a number of players yet to return to action following their World Cup exploits, including the likes of Declan Rice, Bukayo Saka and Noni Madueke. England and Real Madrid midfielder Jude Bellingham was in attendance at the Emirates to watch his younger brother Jobe in action for Dortmund.

Arsenal play Cesc Fabregas’ Como on Wednesday before taking on Manchester City in the Community Shield next weekend. Mikel Arteta’s side then start the defence of their Premier League crown at home against newly-promoted Coventry City in just under two weeks. Meanwhile Borussia Dortmund take on arch-rivals Bayern Munich in the DFL-Supercup in a couple of weeks before starting their Bundesliga campaign at home against Hamburg at the end of the month.

News.title: Israel’s mental health time bomb
News.content:
This month alone, three Israeli soldiers are reported to have died by suicide, two of them young women. It takes to 17 the number who have taken their own lives since the start of the year, a rate higher than at any point in the last 15 years.

The month was made worse by the news last week that the boyfriend of Liron Barda, who was murdered at the Nova music festival during the October 7 massacre, had died beside the grave of his sweetheart.

Bar Asraf, 30, was having trouble coping. He had recently told his mother he was struggling without his girlfriend, reportedly saying, “there’s no one who can replace her, no one to cheer me up”.

These high profile tragedies are but the tip of a mental health crisis that is sweeping Israel, according to data collected by Clalit, the country’s largest health provider.

The study found post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) in the general population had increased by 70 per cent in the wake of the October 7 attacks and subsequent conflict.

News.title: I’m a professional cleaner and I swear by this three-ingredient carpet stain remover
News.content:
However effective your vacuum cleaner, there will always be those unfortunate spills and baked-in stains that need closer attention. I run a commercial cleaning business and rely on a homemade paste to remove the most stubborn marks from my carpets (and deploy it after any accidents). It’s inexpensive and you will probably have the ingredients in your cupboards already.

It won’t achieve a deep clean, though. If you’re looking to tackle bigger areas and own – or can hire – a carpet cleaner, I also have some fail-safe advice to ensure a pristine finish.

Spot clean stains with a homemade paste

For small stains, this quick concoction is all you need. Simply mix the following ingredients together slowly until they form a paste:

Half a cup bicarbonate of soda

1 tbsp mild washing up liquid

1-2 tbsp of warm water

Avoid brightly coloured washing up liquids, especially if you have lighter-coloured carpets, as the dye may transfer onto the fibres. Before you start, there’s one step that applies to any carpet cleaning; always test your cleaning solution (homemade or otherwise) on a small, hidden area of flooring to check for colour-fastness and compatibility.

News.title: Wildfire forces thousands to evacuate in Canada
News.content:
A fast-moving wildfire in western Canada forced more than 20,000 people to evacuate on Saturday.

The fire in Bald Range, British Columbia, doubled in size on Friday night as Canadian officials declared a state of emergency.

It spread rapidly to cover about 23,500 acres, prompting evacuation orders across the province, including the districts of Summerland, Peachland and other areas to the west of Okanagan Lake.

David Eby, the British Columbia premier, told a press conference on Saturday that one fire official had compared the blaze to a “bomb going off”.

News.title: Argentina rugby fans display Falklands banner in defeat by South Africa
News.content:
Back-to-back world champions South Africa have travelled to Buenos Aires to take on Argentina. Argentina have beaten South Africa just four times in 40 meetings between the nations, with their last win over the Springboks coming in September 2024 when they won 29-28 in Santiago del Estero.

Argentina’s Nations Championship games on home soil last month did not exactly go to plan. They fell to defeats to Scotland and England, with their only win coming against Wales. The loss to England was a particularly fiery affair, a few days after Argentina beat England in the Fifa World Cup semi-finals. Argentina were denied a late try which could have earned them a draw and led to chaos at the full-time whistle at the end of an ill-tempered match. After today, Argentina have two home games against Australia in a few weeks’ time, which will be their final games before the second half of the Nations Championship takes place in the northern hemisphere in November.

South Africa won all three games in the first half of the inaugural Nations Championship, beating England, Scotland and Wales on home soil. The Springboks have a four-match series coming up against New Zealand over the next couple of months. They have welcomed back a number of key players from injury including captain Siya Kolisi, Lood de Jager, Eben Etzebeth and Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu. Head coach Rassie Erasmus has decided though to rest a number of players and keep them back in South Africa to prepare for the Greatest Rivalry Tour against New Zealand, including Cheslin Kolbe, Damian Willemse and Jesse Kriel.

“We tried to get the balance right between giving some guys who are returning from injury and who have not had too much game time in our last four matches a valuable run against Argentina, while at the same time managing the players who have played a lot of rugby this year,” said Erasmus. “The guys who have recovered from their injuries have been training hard and are ready to go, so it will be great for them to get a tough Test match under the belt before we face New Zealand.

“The Argentineans are very similar to South Africans in many ways. Their passion and patriotism for their country and people, and the way they give everything on the field and keep fighting is a testament to the type of Test match we are expecting this weekend. They have beaten us twice in Argentina before and they delivered brave performances in their Nations Championship matches, and will have a point to prove on Saturday, so we are fully aware of the challenge ahead.

“They have a strong forward pack and dangerous backs, and they will have a very passionate crowd behind them, so we will have to be at our best to win this match. We have had to grind out results against them on several occasions in the past, so it will take a proper 80-minute effort this weekend, and we are looking forward to the challenge.”

Kick-off from Buenos Aires is at 8pm BST.

News.title: Man Utd impress in draw against PSG but injury worries mount
News.content:
Manchester United continue their Sweden sojourn with match against Paris St-Germain in Gothenburg.

Clearly a clash against the back-to-back Champions League winners is a step up from their previous two pre-season friendlies (victories against Rosenborg and Atletico Madrid), but at the same time this is more a chance for players to get miles in the legs and see how new signings and possibly some young guns fit in.

One of those new signings is Youri Tielemans, and the Belgian international is in line to make his debut after his move from Aston Villa. Other team news is that Bruno Fernandes is back and ready to captain the team.

Michael Carrick has also been boosted by the returns of Matheus Cunha, Diogo Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui after their post-World Cup breaks.

Cunha, however, will not play a part in today’s match because of a “minor illness” according to the MUTV website. He is expected to link up with the squad in Ireland, where they face Leeds United at Croke Park, after the match.

This will be Man Utd’s first outing since the 2-1 win over Atletico, a performance and result that pleased Carrick.

“I enjoyed it, I thought there was a lot of good in things that we are looking to improve on,” the United manager said. “Building on what we did for the last seven months, I think there is a lot of good signs for us, it’s never going to be the exact stage we want to be at. But I thought there was really a lot of positives to take out of the game, individual, collectively as a team, senior players looking strong and fit, and the younger players doing really well.

“The spirit and the camaraderie is so important for the team, it’s great to see the boys getting on so naturally and enjoying each other’s company. Collectively we looked strong as a team, which is always the most important thing, and individual performances seeing the young players come on to have an impact.”

Kick-off is set for 4pm so stay here for the build up, team news and action.

News.title: Joao Pedro double and Caicedo stunner give Chelsea win over AC Milan
News.content:
Chelsea 3 AC Milan 0

Chelsea cruised to victory over Ruben Amorim’s AC Milan in Jakarta, Indonesia, on Saturday. Goals from Moises Caicedo and a double from João Pedro either side of half-time led Xabi Alonso’s side to their second win on their Far East tour.

The game was fairly even in the first half and looked set to head into the break level at 0-0 but Pedro’s header from Moises Caicedo’s corner put Chelsea in front.

The west London side then doubled their advantage seconds into the second half as Pedro scored his second, assisted by Pedro Neto.

Just minutes later, Chelsea had their third courtesy of a well-worked corner routine. Romeo Lavia’s delivery was met by Caicedo on the volley, with the Ecuadorian’s finish with the outside of the boot finding the bottom corner.

Sports.title: Arsenal player ratings: Wing wizard Christos Tzolis continues fine start but Cristhian Mosquera flat-footed in defence
Sports.content:
ARSENAL suffered another pre-season defeat as they missed out on the chance to lift the Emirates Cup.

The Gunners lost 3-2 at their home stadium to Borussia Dortmund.



Samuele Inacio and Konstantinos Karetsas gave the Germans a 2-0 lead at half-time.

Ethan Nwaneri tucked home nine minutes after the break but Dortmund restored their two-goal advantage four minutes later through Joane Gadou.



Viktor Gyokeres fired home a penalty on 69 minutes but Mikel Arteta’s side could not find the equaliser.

Arsenal then won a practice penalty shootout after full-time, with Nwaneri grabbing the decisive effort.

Here’s how SunSport’s Arsenal reporter Joshua Hall rated the Arsenal players…

KEPA ARRIZABALAGA – 5

The Spaniard looked shaky against Real Betis in midweek and has been fighting to remain Arteta’s No2 after the arrival of Illan Meslier this summer.

This performance did nothing to try and claim that place as his own.

BEN WHITE – 6

White will have to play a big part of the start of Arsenal’s season, given Jurrien Timber’s ongoing groin issue.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

A solid showing from the right-back, but nothing to write home about.

CRISTHIAN MOSQUERA – 4

Given William Saliba’s injury issues are expected to see him out for a significant period, Mosquera can expect to be called upon a fair bit if Arsenal don’t bring in a new centre-back before the end of the window.

There were some positive moments, but the Spaniard switched off to allow Samuele Inacio to ghost in behind and open the scoring for Dortmund.

GABRIEL MAGALHAES – 6

A first pre-season start for the Brazilian after he got just 30 minutes of action off the bench against Real Betis last time out.



A decent enough performance, but he will have been disappointed with his role in Dortmund’s opener.

RICCARDO CALAFIORI – 4

The Italian had little to no impact on the game and was replaced after 60 minutes.

MYLES LEWIS-SKELLY – 6

Arteta is persisting with Lewis-Skelly in midfield, especially with Declan Rice and Martin Zubimendi yet to return to training after the World Cup.

However, the arrival of Bruno Guimaraes means the 19-year-old has another top-class midfielder to fight for his place in the squad against.

This performance showed he can do well on the ball, but he will welcome the return of some experienced midfielders alongside him.



KAI HAVERTZ – 6

Started in midfield alongside Martin Odegaard in a technically sound attack-minded lineup.

The German found himself in some threatening positions down the channels but lacked the final ball at times.

Perhaps most noticeably when he tried to square a golden chance to Viktor Gyokeres and played it straight into Alexander Meyer’s grasp.



MARTIN ODEGAARD – 7

The first we have seen of the Gunners captain since the World Cup, where he shone as Norway exceeded the expectations of the masses.

He was only given 30 minutes of action, but looked strong on the ball and keen to pull the strings from midfield.

MAX DOWMAN – 7

It has been no surprise to anyone, but Dowman has been one of the brightest sparks in Arsenal’s pre-season preparations this summer.

He was always trying to make things happen and had some bright moments down the right flank. With Bukayo Saka yet to return, Dowman could be a big part of Arsenal’s start to the season.

CHRISTOS TZOLIS – 8

The £34m summer arrival might have a bigger part to play on the left wing this season now that Arsenal’s pursuit of Vinicius Junior has come to a crashing halt.



But that might not be a bad thing, as Tzolis has impressed every time he has taken to the pitch during pre-season.

This was another good performance, with some more promising set-piece deliveries and an assist to boot.

VIKTOR GYOKERES – 7

The striker finally got his pre-season goal with a second-half penalty.

His first half was less than ideal, as he smashed a free kick miles over, clattered the crossbar from close range and flopped to the floor instead of taking a shot in the box.

However, his second half was much improved as he drove the team forward in search of a comeback.



SUBSTITIUTES

ETHAN NWANERI (for Odegaard, 32min) – 8

Nwaneri is effectively playing for his Arsenal career this summer.

Last season’s failed loan to Marseille showed where Mikel Arteta views him in the pecking order at the club, and the youngster needs to impress if he wants first-team action this term.

His second-half performance might go some way to giving Arteta something to think about, including a well-taken goal and some dangerous play.



ILLAN MESLIER (for Kepa, 45 mins) – 5

Meslier had a chance to stake a claim as the No2, but struggled with a routine corner at the first sign of danger.

Arsenal need David Raya back as quickly as possible.

PIERO HINCAPIE (for Gabriel, 60 mins) – 6

A solid substitute cameo from the versatile defender.

MARLI SALMON (for Calafiori, 60 mins) – 7

The youngster made a brilliant last-ditch tackle to prevent Dortmund from running away with the game.

Sports.title: Man Utd flop Antony and England star both sent off in farcical friendly scenes after Brazilian boots ball at opponent
Sports.content:
MANCHESTER UNITED flop Antony brawled with Bournemouth star Alex Scott in farcical scenes during a friendly as both men were dismissed.

Real Betis drew 2-2 with the Cherries on Saturday in an action packed four-goal thriller.



Marco Rose’s Bournemouth twice took the lead through Marcus Tavernier and Evanilson before being pegged back by Cucho Hernandez and Pablo Fornals.

And there was even more drama in the closing stages of half time during the pre-season clash.



Betis striker Nelson Deossa whacked a ball at Bafode Diakite at point blank range after the defender fouled him by the touchline.

Deossa was given a yellow card but some Bournemouth players weren’t happy and rushed over to confront him.

That triggered a brawl as former United star Antony got involved and started shoving a couple of Bournemouth players.

Scott then raged at the winger and pushed him back before pointing a finger at him.

Antony was fuming with the England Under-21 international and tried to engage before Scott walked away.



Eventually tensions are eased as the referee told both sets of players to cool down.

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

But even though it was a friendly, Scott and Antony didn’t escape punishment after their behaviour.

The official opted to dish out reds for both players as they were sent down the tunnel just before the half time whistle.

Bournemouth were leading 1-0 at the time after Tavernier opened the scoring just minutes earlier.



But with both teams playing with ten men in the second half, Hernandez drew level before Evanilson made it 2-1 moments later.

Fornals then struck the equaliser with ten minutes to play as both sides ended the game with a draw.

Antony will be remembered by United fans for his disappointing spell at Old Trafford after joining from Ajax for £85m in 2022.

He only played 96 times for the club after falling out of favour with both Erik ten Hag and Ruben Amorim.

He spent the 2024-25 season on loan at Betis and became a hit as he scored nine times in his first season.



Those performances were enough for Betis to turn his move permanent and he joined in a £25m deal – before scoring 14 in all competitions last season.

Sports.title: Xabi Alonso forced to drag Austin MacPhee away from furious row as new Chelsea set-piece coach clashes with rival
Sports.content:
AUSTIN MACPHEE was involved in a heated row following a poor challenge on Chelsea striker Liam Delap.

The Blues drew 3-3 with Malaysian champions Johor Darul Ta’zim in Jakarta.

With 67 minutes on the clock, home defender Antonio Glauder needlessly went through the back of Delap with a scything tackle.



Chelsea stars were furious with the challenge, centre-back Tosin Adarabioyo leading the on-field scuffle.



The Blues’ new set piece coach MacPhee was also raging.

Following the challenge, the Scot and boss Xabi Alonso protested to the fourth official.

At this point, a member of the Johor coaching staff got into MacPhee’s face and poked his finger into his chest.

The former Aston Villa and Scotland national team coach didn’t back down, furiously bellowing into his rival’s face, with Alonso intervening.

Chelsea fans loved the passion of their new set piece guru.

One wrote on X: “Austin MacPhee looks ready to throw hands”.

BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS



And a second joked: “Austin Macphee saying f*** off to the coach while Delap and Tosin lose their heads bruv this is the Chelsea I know”.

Another added: “Austin MacPhee, the set piece coach is ready to work for the badge”.

Delap, who scored two penalties during the match, was okay to continue and Glauder went on to score a late own goal for Chelsea to equalise at 3-3.

It had been believed that the match would go to penalties, should it finish level.

But both sets of players left the pitch following the end of 90 minutes and did not return.



The Blues will now head home from their long Far East tour.

Alonso’s men will return to action against Real Sociedad at Stamford Bridge on Saturday, with their Prem opener coming at neighbours Fulham on August 24.

Sports.title: Arsenal 2 Dortmund 3: Gunners lose second straight friendly and ship three goals AGAIN in worrying sign for Prem champs
Sports.content:
ARSENAL are just a week away from the start of their season, but they look a world away from being champions again.

The Gunners put in a lacklustre showing as they fell to a 3-2 defeat to Borussia Dortmund, just seven days out from the Community Shield.



Mikel Arteta will have hoped to have his side ticking by now, ready to attack rivals Manchester City in Cardiff and lay down a marker for the new campaign.

But if their pre-season performances are any indication of what Arsenal will be like this season, Arteta will be more than concerned.



After being thumped 3-1 by Real Betis in mid-week, the Gunners were well beaten in their own back yard by a heavily rotated Dortmund side.

Arsenal looked sleepy from the first whistle, and it took just six minutes for Dortmund to take advantage of that.

Cristhian Mosquera switched off completely and allowed Samuele Inacio to ghost in behind him and poke home a slide pass from Felix Nmecha.

Arsenal thought they would have a chance to respond just 10 minutes later when Martin Odegaard was taken down on the edge of the area.

But Viktor Gyokeres blasted the resulting free-kick over the crossbar, a reminder of how the Swede has lacked finesse since his move to the Emirates.

Before 30 minutes had passed, Arsenal found themselves in deeper trouble as their midfield seemingly disappeared, allowing Konstantinos Karetsas to carry the ball into a dangerous area and curl a beauty into the top corner.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

New signing Bruno Guimaraes, who was watching from the stands after being unveiled to the crowd before the game, will have been wishing he was playing during that moment.

The Brazilian has been brought in as another midfield option and, alongside Declan Rice and Martin Zubimendi, would be expected to clean up those types of dangerous attacks from now on.

Without Guimaraes, and a host of other World Cup stars yet to return, Arsenal look so light in midfield.

Martin Odegaard impressed during his short cameo, but was taken off after 30 minutes having only returned to training this week.

His replacement, Ethan Nwaneri, offered a glimmer of hope for Arteta as he turned home a drilled Christos Tzolis pass to pull a goal back for the Gunners 10 minutes into the second half.



But just three minutes later, Arsenal had conceded again, this time from a poor corner that was bundled around the box like a pinball before Joane Gadou poked it home.

Tzolis was trying to create again as Arsenal fought for a way back into the game and earned the Gunners a penalty when he went down under a clumsy challenge from Kaua Prates.

Gyokeres continued his impeccable record from the spot to net his first goal of pre-season and make the score 3-2.



But Arsenal were unable to use that spot-kick gift as a way back into the game and Arteta cut a frustrated figure as he watched it all unfold from the sidelines.

Substitute Gabriel Martinelli thought he has equalised in added time, but the linesman’s flag went up to prevent the blush-sparing goal.

Arsenal have the caveat of stars like Rice, Zubimendi, Bukayo Saka, Mikel Merino and Ebere Eze still missing.

As well as injured aces like Jurrien Timber and William Saliba.

But Arteta will know what he is seeing from his current crop is nowhere near the level that earned them their first league title in 22 years last term.



A dip into the transfer market could help, but there are perhaps some underlying issues that need to be addressed first.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The match was followed by a meaningless penalty shootout, which Arsenal won 5-4 after new signing Illan Meslier denied Mathis Albert.

The penalty victory means nothing for the Gunners, who still missed the chance to win their fifth consecutive Emirates Cup.

Sports.title: Chelsea player ratings: Liam Delap a rare shining light in Johor draw but Tosin Adarabioyo off the pace yet again
Sports.content:
CHELSEA were held to a 3-3 draw by Malaysian underdogs Johor Darul Ta’zim in a back-and-forth pre-season friendly on Sunday.

Xabi Alonso fielded a second-string side at the Sultan Ibrahim Stadium, with the new boss casting his eye over a selection of youngsters.



They went behind in the 14th minute but equalised before half-time when Liam Delap won and scored a penalty.

Delap notched from the spot again just after the hour mark but there was plenty more drama to come.



Oscar Arribas equalised via a deflected free-kick and Bergson gave Johor a shock lead before Antonio Glauder’s late own goal levelled up the six-goal thriller.

Here is how SunSport’s Dan King rated every Chelsea performance in Malaysia…



Teddy Sharman-Lowe – 6

Left totally exposed by his defence on multiple occasions in the first half. Looked solid enough, apart from one poor clearance that could have led to a big chance. Substituted at half time to give Slonina a run-out.

Olutayo Subuloye – 5

A late replacement after Mamadou Sarr pulled out of the game just before kick off. Was shaky in the first half, like the whole Chelsea defence.

But did better after the break as he and fellow teenager Reggie Watson carried their more experienced team-mate in the back three.

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Tosin Adarabioyo – 3

His weaknesses, especially lack of pace, were regularly exposed by JDT and he was caught out even before playing his part in conceding the first goal.



But what was more shocking was his lack of leadership as the game became spiteful. He seemed more intent on starting or getting involved in rucks than setting a calm example to his young team-mates.

Aaron Anselmino – 5

The guy cannot catch a break. Given a rare chance to start, he pulled up within half an hour after appearing to hurt himself while attempting a sharp turn deep in the JDT half.

Geovany Quenda – 4

After his fine game as an out-and-out winger against Juventus, this was not an impressive display at right wing-back.

He showed flashes of what he could do going forward, but it was down his side that JDT had a lot of their joy.

Mahdi Nicoll-Jazuli – 5

Not nearly as impressive as earlier in the tour. But he is still only 16 and did better than a lot of the older players in Alonso’s team.



Caught out once or twice and Chelsea’s midfield was over-run at times. Yet has never looked out of place on this trip and has given the manager something to ponder.

Dario Essugo – 4

Was made captain, no less, on a rare start after his own injury problems since joining Chelsea.

But was outshone by two 16-year-olds even before his poor touch gifted JDT what looked like being a late winner. His future at Stamford Bridge must be in massive doubt.



Jamie Gittens – 3

Not even earning Delap’s second penalty was enough to save him from a low mark.

To be absolutely fair, Gittens signed as a winger and has never claimed to be a wing-back.

And he will surely never be asked to play there again after being caught out time after time in his defensive duties.

Estevao – 5

Started brightly but soon faded as Chelsea lost control of the game. Also showed a streak of petulance in earning a yellow card for retaliation after being denied a penalty.

Always had the potential to do something without ever finding a final ball.



Nicolas Jackson – 6

Put himself about from the start, having an early shot well saved, and kept going even when things weren’t going for him or his touch let him down.

Linked well with Delap at times, including one brilliant through ball. Showed he has plenty to offer but will he be happy with a back-up role?

Liam Delap – 8

Showed everything that is good and bad about his game. In one seven-minute period he won and scored a penalty, then got a stupid yellow card and missed a brilliant chance to make it 2-1.

Kept his cool to score from the spot again to put Chelsea ahead, unlucky to deflect in JDT’s equaliser but arguably a bit fortunate not to be booked for a second time.

Kept making runs all evening and his faint flicked header led to the equaliser.



Substitutes

Reggie Watson – 8

What a fantastic all-round footballer this kid is. A midfielder by trade, he barely put a foot wrong as a right-sided centre back.

Still only 16, he plays like a much more experienced player and showed up plenty of his team-mates. Needs first-team chances or a really good loan this season.



Gaga Slonina – 6

Did well to stop JDT going ahead early in the second half, although Shahab Zahedi should have done better. Nothing he could do about JDT’s equaliser but may feel he should have got something on Bergson’s shot that made it 3-2.

Dastan Satpayev – 6

Did not have time to make much of an impact. Already a Kazakh international, he should be sent on loan to a challenging environment to prove he has the chops to make it at Chelsea.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Mykhailo Mudryk – 7



You want substitutes to make an impact and the Ukrainian did just that. Delap should have got more on a fine cross, but Mudryk deserved the good fortune of it going in off Antonio Glauder.

Sports.title: ‘It’s in the contract!’ – Chelsea penalty shootout chaos erupts as pre-season friendly hit by farcical row after draw
Sports.content:
CHELSEA’S penultimate pre-season friendly ended in chaos as a scheduled penalty shootout was apparently cancelled in Malaysia.

An incident-packed, bad-tempered game ended with a score of 3-3 with 11 players still on both teams.



A late own-goal by Johor Darul Ta’zim prevented the Blues losing in normal time and a shootout was expected to settle the winners.

But it never happened and that led to mass confusion on the pitch.



A member of the Chelsea backroom staff was overheard yelling, “It’s in the contract”, to the referee.

However, both teams and staff left the field, never to return and the game came to an abrupt end.



Xabi Alonso’s men were ragged for much of the pre-season friendly and deserved to fall behind in the first half.

Johor opened the scoring after just 14 minutes thanks to Arif Aiman Hanapi’s opener.

Two penalties from Liam Delap in the second half put the Blues in the driving seat.

However, JDT equalised with Oscar Arribas just three minutes after Delap completed his brace.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

And the Malaysian outfit moved ahead four minutes before full-time thanks to Bergson’s finish.

However, Chelsea’s blushes were saved just three minutes later thanks to Antonio Cristian’s own-goal.

But then an entertaining evening was denied more drama when the shootout was called off and the West Londoners were left to head back to Europe for Saturday’s final friendly against Real Sociedad.

Alonso also lost two players in Mamadou Sarr and Aaron Anselmino to injury.

Sports.title: Chelsea 3 Johor 3: Xabi Alonso set for sleepless night with second-string Blues WOEFUL against Malaysian minnows
Sports.content:
CHELSEA avoided humiliation amid farcical scenes at the end of their far-flung Far East tour.

An incident-packed, bad-tempered game ended level on the scoresheet and with 11 players still on both teams.



A late own goal by Johor Darul Ta’zim prevented the Blues from losing in normal time and a penalty shootout was expected to settle the winners.

But it never happened.



A member of the Chelsea backroom staff was overheard saying “it’s in the contract” to the referee.

Yet both teams and staff left the field, never to return.

Xabi Alonso’s side were ragged for much of the game and deserved to fall behind in the first half.

Then two penalties from Liam Delap put the Blues in the driving seat, only for JDT to equalise and then move ahead with five minutes to go.

Delap flicked on a cross from substitute Mykhailo Mudryk to force Antonio Glauder into an own goal.

But then an entertaining evening was denied more drama when the shootout was called off and the Blues were left to head back to Europe.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Defeat would have been a real embarrassment for Chelsea, despite extenuating circumstances.

Yes, it was a mainly second-string side which took the field only 15 hours after the squad touched down at 4am local time in Jakarta.

Yes, it was still 30C and humid as anything.

And JDT have won the last 12 Malaysian titles in a row.



But still there are no excuses for a Premier League team losing to such opposition.

And Chelsea should have been three down at half time yet could have been 2-1 up.

After a good start going forward, worries about the team out of position in the 3-4-2-1 formation were proved well founded.

It was far too easy for JDT to break and Marcos Guilherme outpaced Tosin Adarabioyo before crossing to the back post, where captain Arif Aiman fired home.

Aaron Anselmino should probably have done better but the Argentinian was soon forced off with injury, after Mamadou Sarr had also been a late withdrawal from the starting line-up.



The Blues were soon all over the place.

Jamie Gittens was struggling as a left wing-back and Oscar Arribas wasted a brilliant chance to make it 2-0.

JDT also fluffed yet another good break and were punished immediately.



Delap’s strength led Kevin Medina into a silly foul which conceded a penalty.

Delap scored emphatically but then showed the other side to his game.

First, the £30m signing from last summer was needlessly booked for getting involved in a scuffle with an opponent.



Then Delap was played through by Nicolas Jackson’s brilliant pass in first-half stoppage time but sent a first-time shot wide.

If Alonso’s message at the break was to tighten up at the back, no-one listened.

Shahab Zahedi ran clear for JDT but allowed half-time substitute goalkeeper Gaga Slonina to make a good save.

Chelsea continued to look open at the back, but on the hour they went ahead.

Gittens did something right at last, winning a softish penalty.



Once more, Delap was decisive from the spot.

But JDT were soon level. Arribas’s free kick took a wicked deflection off Delap’s back and it was no more than the home team deserved.

The needle in the game returned when Antonio Glauder went through the back of Delap.

Tosin led the brawl on the pitch, while set-piece coach Austin McPhee was involved in a scuffle between the two benches.

Clear-cut chances had dried up until Dario Essugo’s poor pass allowed JDT sub Bergson to put his side 3-2 up with five minutes to go.



But Alonso’s double change paid dividends immediately.

Sub Mudryk swung in a cross, Delap got a faint touch and the ball took a big deflection off Glauder to level the score.

And so to penalties.

Or not.

Sports.title: Chelsea hit by DOUBLE defensive blow as Xabi Alonso’s plans take a major injury hit in pre-season
Sports.content:
CHELSEA’S new manager Xabi Alonso has been dealt a double injury blow ahead of the new season.

Alonso, 44, has been tasked with bringing the Blues back on their feet after a chaotic season that saw three managerial changes and a tenth-place finish.



However, the Spanish tactician has endured a turbulent pre-season that has seen him dealing with a bloated squad and two friendly losses to rivals Tottenham and Juventus.

And now the ex-Real Madrid boss saw two defenders limp off during the West Londoners’ chaotic friendly against Johor Darul Ta’zim.



Mamadou Sarr pulled out injured just before kick-off after being named in Chelsea’s starting line-up.

And Aaron Anselmino was then forced off injured midway in the first half played in Malaysia.



Neither Sarr, 20, nor Anselmino, 21, have been key players for the Premier League giants.

The defensive pair were also not being primed for Chelsea’s first team ahead of the 2026/27 season.

Sarr joined the Blues from Strasbourg in 2025 but was immediately sent back to the sister club on loan until this past February when he came back to Stamford bridge.

The centre-back currently counts a mere total of six appearances with the West Londoners.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Anselmino, on the other hand, joined Chelsea in 2024 from Boca Juniors but was loaned back to the Argentinean giants before undergoing some more short stints at Borussia Dortmund and Strasbourg.

The centre-back has only managed one appearance across all competitions with the Prem outfit in which he only played three minutes.

Alonso already has a raft of options to choose from at centre-half, which includes the likes of Levi Colwill, Wesley Fofana, Tosin Adarabioyo, Josh Acheampong and summer signing Maxence Lacroix.

Benoit Badiashile, Trevoh Chalobah and Axel Disasi are also still in Chelsea’s books but look set to move away during the summer transfer window.

Alonso oversaw an intense penultimate friendly against JDT end in a 3-3 draw.



The game ended with immense confusion as a penalty shootout appeared to have been cancelled.

Sports.title: Rusty Arsenal lose again as Dortmund defeat exposes Mikel Arteta concern - 5 talking points
Sports.content:
Arsenal lost 3-2 to Borussia Dortmund in the Emirates Cup final as Mikel Arteta's men continued their preparations for the new season proper.

Samuele Inacio gave Dortmund an early lead as Arsenal were caught cold in the 7th minute, the forward ghosting in behind the home defence to finish coolly beyond Kepa Arrizabalaga.

And Konstantinos Karetsas doubled the Bundesliga outfit's lead in some style, curling a superb strike into the far corner after running half the length of the pitch as Arsenal went in with major work to do at the break.

Substitute Ethan Nwaneri halved the deficit nine minutes after the internal after fine work from Christos Tzolis, who put the ball on a plate for the Gunners academy graduate.

‌



Joane Gadou swiftly restored Dortmund's two-goal cushion before Tzolis won a penalty which was converted well by Viktor Gyokeres. But there was no equalising goal for Arsenal, who fell to a 3-2 defeat. Here are Mirror Football's talking points from the game...

Arsenal respond to Gabriel Martinelli transfer approach as Mikel Arteta lays out demands READ MORE :

PSG move could hand Marcus Rashford last-gasp Man Utd transfer with Barcelona reunion READ MORE :

1. Defensive concerns grow

Arsenal's ultra-tight defence was the bedrock of their first Premier League title win since 2004, but they have looked uncharacteristically brittle in pre-season. Yes, it's worth bearing in mind Arsenal and their first-choice stars are still easing their way back into the swing of things after the World Cup. But with William Saliba already out of the opening months of the upcoming Premier League season, there is adequate cause for concern.

Cristhian Mosquera played alongside Gabriel and allowed Nmecha to run in blindside to open the scoring. And Dortmund simply got too much joy when they probed for Arteta to be happy about.

There's no doubt Gabriel and Co will be sharper for the big kick-off in a fortnight. But you can see why Arsenal want to add another central defender with the knowledge that Saliba is some way off being able to feature.

‌



2. Tzolis warming up

View 5 Images Christos Tzolis and Ethan Nwaneri were Arsenal's two standout players vs Dortmund (Image: David Price/Arsenal FC)

While nobody expected Tzolis to start the season as first choice given Arsenal's pursuit of Morgan Rogers and Vinicius Junior, the former Norwich City man is certainly looking the part.

Signed from Club Brugge after scoring 17 goals and providing a further 23 assists in 36 league appearances, Tzolis has already been among the goal contributions in pre-season, registering one in the previous three friendlies. He made it four in four by supplying Nwaneri with the simplest of finishes after some fine, direct wing play in the early minutes of the second half. He also won the penalty which set up a grandstand finish, too.

Arsenal will, surely, still add another left attacker before the transfer window shuts. And the odds are said signing will be a biggie in terms of star power. But right now, Tzolis has the shirt. And he may not give it up without a fight.

‌



3. Karetsas proves his point

View 5 Images Konstantinos Karetsas scored a stunning goal for Borussia Dortmund (Image: Justin Setterfield)

The highlight of the game was Karetsas' spectacular goal, with the tricky winger finishing in style after being given the freedom of north London. What makes it even more intriguing is that the uber-talented 18-year-old was a player Arsenal considered signing lasts summer.

Karetsas joined Dortmund from KRC Genk for around €30million (£25.7m) last week and Sunday's outing at The Emirates was his first in the famous black and yellow. He certainly didn't disappoint - and perhaps he even left some of an Arsenal persuasion wondering "what if".

4. Gyokeres facing make or break season

View 5 Images Viktor Gyokeres scores from the penalty spot (Image: Justin Setterfield)

‌



Despite only arriving for big bucks 12 months ago, it feels like Gyokeres is facing a make-or-break season.

Arsenal have been crying out for a marquee No 9 for years to help them get over the line in the title race and Gyokeres, chosen as that signing last summer, did help them end their agonising title drought. His numbers weren't bad, either: 14 goals in the Premier League and 21 in total. Numbers which are absolutely not to be sniffed at.

And yet, rumblings that Arsenal could pursue another striker to level up their attack have been going on in the background all summer. We saw the good and the bad of the Swede here: he was a nuisance, full of running, power and some good touches. He was unfortunate with the powerful effort that lashed up and over off the crossbar after being picked out by Max Dowman. But his finishing can be wayward too and the free-kick he blazed over from a prime position in the first half was poor, as was some of his general decision-making.

Gyokeres did end the game with a goal after a well-taken penalty but the jury is definitely still out.

‌



5. More signings needed

View 5 Images Mikel Arteta looks on during the Borussia Dortmund game (Image: Carlos Jasso/AFP)

Arteta has stated that he wants to create a "dynasty" at Arsenal and level up the team after winning the title last season. Bruno Guimaraes and Christos Tzolis are the only real significant first team signings with the new season now just two weeks away.

Arsenal have missed out on priority targets in Morgan Rogers and Vinicius Junior and although not ideal, these things happen. But the time has come for Arsenal to get motoring in the market. A central defender and an elite left winger are needed at a minimum if Arsenal are to to progress as much as Arteta wants.

Sports.content:
Man Utd given Benjamin Sesko reality check after Bayern Munich transfer links

Former Manchester United striker Michael Owen has cast doubt on whether Benjamin Sesko is the right long-term centre forward for the club

View 2 Images Benjamin Sesko has been linked with a Manchester United exit this summer (Image: Carl Recine/Getty Images)

Michael Owen has explained why he has “doubts” that Benjamin Sesko could be a long-term option for Manchester United. Sesko signed for the Red Devils last summer from RB Leipzig in a deal believed to be worth around £74million.

‌



There have been reports in recent weeks providing speculation around Sesko’s future at United, with the striker scoring 12 goals during his first season at Old Trafford.

‌



Sesko was granted more minutes for United after Michael Carrick took charge at the start of the year, but did not feature in any of the final four matches of the campaign with a shin injury.

‌



Sesko's future has been a subject of discussion over the summer, with reports in recent days suggesting that Bayern Munich are considering making an approach for the United striker. Sesko is said to be viewed by Bayern as a possible long-term replacement for Harry Kane.

Former United striker Michael Owen has "doubts" that Sesko could be a long-term solution for United, and raised the possibility of the Red Devils entering the market for a new centre forward.

‌



"Well, a lot of the time, half the time he [Sesko] doesn't even play and they do quite well anyway," Owen said in an interview with Goal.

"Whether they push [Matheus] Cunha up front or [Bryan] Mbeumo or whoever, they've managed without him.

View 2 Images Benjamin Sesko of Manchester United (Image: Visionhaus/Getty Images)

‌



"Even though he's the only out and out centre forward, if it was the European Cup final next week, then I'm not sure he would start. If they had another option, a better option, I'm sure they would take that.

"However, he has surprised a few. He wasn't that convincing right at the start, but it's not easy to be convincing in the Manchester United team over the last decade or so.

"Obviously, in the second half of the season, Manchester United are playing really, really well. He's grown into the role as well.

"You'd definitely say he's going to get more game time this season and see how he does. Do I see him as the long-term Manchester United centre forward? I'd have my doubts."

Sports.title: Mason Mount injury latest as Man Utd sweat on star after pre-season blow
Sports.content:
Mason Mount injury latest as Man Utd sweat on star after pre-season blow

Mason Mount has impressed in pre-season but he gave Manchester United a scare by picking up an injury just 20 minutes into Saturday's 1-1 draw with Paris Saint-Germain

View 2 Images Mason Mount came off injured against Paris Saint-Germain (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images)

Manchester United have been given a boost after learning that Mason Mount's injury is not serious. The United midfielder came off after just 20 minutes during Saturday's 1-1 draw with Paris Saint-Germain.

‌



It left Michael Carrick sweating on the fitness of Mount, 27, with less than two weeks to go until the Red Devils start their Premier League season away to newly promoted Hull City. But the midfielder left the stadium in Gothenburg, Sweden walking freely, suggesting that his pre-season wasn't over.

‌



Mount has now flown to Ireland ahead of United's next training camp in County Kildare. He'll be joined by Marcus Rashford, Kobbie Mainoo and Lisandro Martinez, who were each given additional time off following the World Cup.

‌



Having only started two of Carrick's 17 games in charge last season, Mount has given a good account of himself in pre-season. Playing in a deeper role, the former Chelsea star has put together an encouraging run of performances.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Mount could form part of a new-look midfield against Hull. Summer signings Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans are in contention to start, while Mainoo and Bruno Fernandes will expect to play.

‌



United have been intent on signing a third midfielder throughout the transfer window, but Mount's displays could prompt them to shelve their plans and focus on recruiting for other areas. Left-back is a position which the Red Devils want to strengthen before deadline day on Tuesday, September 1.

Mount's resurgence has also seen ex-United winger Lee Sharpe label him captain material. The 27-year-old currently isn't part of United's leadership group.

What is Manchester United's best midfield three? Have your say in the comments section.

‌



View 2 Images Mason Mount remains on Manchester United's pre-season tour (Image: Michael Campanella/Getty Images)

"I think if he can stay fit and play the way he has done previous seasons, Mason Mount, with his experience, would always be in with a shout," Sharpe told Goal. "I think he would not necessarily rule by fear, but rule by example."

Mount has managed 72 appearances since signing for United in a deal worth up to £60million in the summer of 2023. His career at Old Trafford has been stunted by injuries and constant managerial changes.

Article continues below

Last season was his most productive, however, scoring three goals and providing one assist in 25 games. Carrick will be hoping to get even more out of Mount in the 2026-27 campaign.

Sports.title: Jose Mourinho takes 'low level' swipe at Bernardo Silva after Real Madrid debut
Sports.content:
Jose Mourinho takes 'low level' swipe at Bernardo Silva after Real Madrid debut

Bernardo Silva made his first appearance for Real Madrid in a pre-season friendly against Ferencvaros on Saturday and Jose Mourinho gave a typically ruthless post-match comment

View 2 Images Jose Mourinho didn't hold back (Image: Real Madrid TV)

Ruthless Jose Mourinho has told Bernardo Silva that he 'has to improve' and criticised the new Real Madrid star's 'low level' of fitness. Silva, 31, joined Mourinho's side on a free transfer after his contract with Manchester City expired in June.

‌



The Portugal international made his debut on Saturday, helping Real beat Hungarian giants Ferencvaros 2-1 in a pre-season friendly. Silva played the second half and gave fans a first glimpse of the 'incredible player' that Mourinho has described him as.

‌



But it was the rest of his manager's comments which raised eyebrows. "He is very important, but the poor guy is one of those players who benefits mentally from not doing anything during vacation, and he arrived for pre-season at a fairly low physical level," Mourinho told Real Madrid TV.

‌



"He has to improve. But he is an incredible player."

FOLLOW OUR REAL MADRID FB PAGE! Latest news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Jose Mourinho’s three things he wants from Vinicius Jr as Arsenal transfer outcome awaits READ MORE :

The Los Blancos boss then explained how he changed Silva's position during the second half to compensate for his apparent lack of sharpness. "During the game, I realised he was lacking a little physical strength, so I moved him forward to the No. 10 position," Mourinho added.

‌



"He can play there, too. He can play in three or four positions."

In addition to his criticism of Silva, Mourinho commented on Vinicius Junior'sr decision to sign a new six-year contract with Real after crunch talks over his future. Arsenal were waiting in the wings with a lucrative offer, but the Brazilian has opted to extend his stay at the Bernabeu.

Will Jose Mourinho be successful at Real Madrid? Give us your prediction in the comments section.

‌



View 2 Images Bernardo Silva came on at half-time (Image: David Balogh/Getty Images)

"The most important thing is his contract renewal," Mourinho said. "It's a joy for him and for all of us. With so few training sessions, these are players who come into a game with tired legs from training.

"I didn't expect him to run 50 meters with the ball and score. He will surely be better on Wednesday (against Deportivo La Coruna) and even better on Sunday (against Schalke)."

Article continues below

Real will begin their La Liga campaign away to Espanyol on Saturday, August 22 before Mourinho makes his grand return to the Bernabeu against Real Sociedad four days later. Mourinho's task is to bring the Spanish title back to Madrid and end Barcelona's two-year stronghold on the trophy.

Sports.title: PSG move could hand Marcus Rashford last-gasp Man Utd transfer with Barcelona reunion
Sports.content:
PSG move could hand Marcus Rashford last-gasp Man Utd transfer with Barcelona reunion

Marcus Rashford is expected to stay at Manchester United but a Paris Saint-Germain transfer approach could open the door to a permanent Barcelona move

View 2 Images Marcus Rashford could have been handed a Barcelona transfer chance by Ferran Torres (Image: (Photo by Eric Alonso/Getty Images))

Ferran Torres looks to have handed Marcus Rashford a chance of re-joining Barcelona permanently as the Spain international targets a move to Paris Saint-Germain. Personal terms have been agreed between the European champions and Torres with an official bid expected soon.

‌



The 26-year-old is fresh of a historic achievement after scoring a World Cup-winning goal for Spain. He also helped Barca lift the La Liga title with 16 goals in 33 appearances. Despite his return, Torres did not make regular starting XI's which may be a factor in his decision to look for a move elsewhere

‌



When Raphinha was fit, Rashford also played a secondary role at Barcelona but he and Torres linked up on several occasions. Robert Lewandowksi was often preferred to the latter but he has since joined MLS side Chicago Fire.

‌



Michael Carrick provides Marcus Rashford update and confirms Man Utd star's next move READ MORE :

Despite that, the former Manchester City star is not guaranteed a place with the signings of Karim Adeyemi and Anthony Gordon, which appeared to shut the door on Rashford's prospects of joining on a permanent basis, strengthening Barca's frontline.

While the new arrivals are not in direct competition with Torres, he may well be sensing that he is being sidelined. Head coach Hansi Flick also appeared open to the player departing when quizzed about his future following a 1-0 pre-season victory over Nottingham Forest.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

‌



He said: "I respect all the players, I don't know anything about the situation at the moment. I was focused on the team, and I don't know anything."

Just hours before Barca's win over the Premier League side, Manchester United played out a 1-1 draw against Torres' potential future club PSG. Rashford played no part, still enjoying his post-World Cup break.

Michael Carrick did, however, confirm that he and two other players would be joining the club's pre-season camp in the coming days as preparations ramp up ahead of fixtures against Leeds United and AC Milan.

‌



The United head coach said: "We have got a full squad this week in Dublin. We fly straight there and have a few days where we have the whole group back together. "Marcus is part of that, and Kobbie [Mainoo] and Lisandro [Martinez]. We look forward to seeing them."

View 2 Images Kobbie Mainoo and Marcus Rashford will be back at Manchester United next week (Image: Getty Images)

Rashford currently looks more likely to stay put at Old Trafford, though a departure for Torres could certainly shake things up. Barca appear to have their sights set primarily on Manchester City's Rodri for now, but may well find themselves turning their attention to more attacking targets before long.

‌



Julian Alvarez is thought to be higher up their wishlist than Rashford, with Barca pursuing his signature intensely ahead of the World Cup.

The Argentine is said to still be seeking a move away, but Diego Simeone's side have no plans to negotiate with Barca unless his eye-watering release clause is triggered - which could enhance Rashford's prospects.

Sports.title: Arsenal defend badly as Dortmund win Emirates Cup
Sports.content:
Arsenal produced more comical defending in pre-season as Borussia Dortmund won 3-2 in north London to win the Emirates Cup.

After Mikel Arteta said Arsenal's defending in Wednesday's defeat to Real Betis was "below the standard", the Gunners found themselves in trouble again as they were 2-0 down at the break thanks to goals from Samuele Inacio and 18-year-old wonderkid Konstantinos Karetsas.

Arsenal had plenty of chances throughout - with the wasteful Viktor Gyokeres hitting the bar in the first half - and while Ethan Nwaneri pulled one back after good work from Christos Tzolis, a calamitous corner allowed Joane Gadou to make it 3-1.

Tzolis then capped off a promising performance by winning a penalty which Gyokeres converted. But with seven days to go until their Community Shield game with Man City in Cardiff, Arteta has some holes to fix.

Arsenal welcomed new signing Bruno Guimaraes onto the Emirates pitch before kick-off - he is needed sooner rather than later.

7: GOAL! Inacio gives Dortmund the lead after being played through in the box by Lukas Nmecha.

15: NO PENALTY! Odegaard breaks through on goal and is brought down. Referee Chris Kavanagh points to the spot then changes his mind by giving a free-kick on the edge of the box, which Gyokeres fires over.

26: OFF THE BAR! Gyokeres strikes the bar after Odegaard's pass freed Dowman on the right wing.

29: GOAL! Karetsas doubles Dortmund's lead after Riccardo Calafiori gave the ball away on the halfway line, which sparked a solo run.

59: GOAL! Comical Arsenal defending at a corner sees Gadou score a third for Dortmund, after Illan Meslier saved when Calafiori could not clear his lines.

69: GOAL! Gyokeres pulls one back from the penalty spot after livewire Tzolis is fouled by Jobe Bellingham.

90+4: GOAL DISALLOWED! Martinelli thinks he has equalised but is caught offside from a short corner.

Sports.title: Sunrisers Leeds dominate Welsh Fire to remain in eliminator contention
Sports.content:
Sunrisers Leeds kept themselves in contention for The Hundred eliminator while dumping Welsh Fire out of the women's competition in a one-sided contest at Headingley.

The victory sets up a virtual quarter-final with Manchester Super Giants, who sit in third two points ahead of Sunrisers on 18, at Emirates Old Trafford on Tuesday afternoon.

With both sides coming off the back of two wins, Sunrisers won the toss and surprised nobody by electing to bowl. A nervy start saw Cassidy McCarthy deliver four wides in five balls before Kate Cross got rid of Sarah Bryce lbw.

Freya Kemp then joined Georgia Voll and was fluent from the off in what turned out to be a standout innings.

The economical Deepti Sharma trapped Voll in front to leave the game nicely poised at 61-2 at the halfway mark.

Hannah Baker then broke the game wide open with two quick wickets, an excellent catch by Phoebe Litchfield dismissing her compatriot Georgia Wareham, followed by a peach to bowl Orla Prendergast, both for ducks.

Annabel Sutherland, who had earlier dropped Kemp, then immediately put her down again off Baker to give the Fire a lifeline.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Annabel Sutherland dropped two catches that could have proved costly for Sunrisers Leeds

But two more wickets in six balls saw Fire's run-rate plummet as they aimed just to survive the 100 balls, Baker finishing with 2-15.

Kemp, however, had other ideas. She upped the ante with a six off Jess Jonassen and then blitzed her way to an unbeaten 72 off 45, but a total of 121-8 felt underpowered against the in-form Super Giants line-up.

And so it proved as the remarkable Litchfield continued where she left off against Birmingham Phoenix on Friday.

Shots all around the ground, including three sixes, saw her to a 23-ball 55 and when she went, the score was 92 off 52 and the game as good as done.

Sports.title: Five-time Super League winner Makinson to retire at end of 2026 campaign
Sports.content:
Tommy Makinson has announced he will retire from rugby league at the end of the current 2026 Super League campaign.

The Catalans Dragons wing, 34, spent the majority of his career with St Helens between 2011 and 2024, winning five Super League titles in 2014, 2019, 2020, 2021 and 2022 and making more than 300 appearances.

Makinson also won a World Club Challenge, a Challenge Cup and four League Leaders' Shields with Saints, and was selected in the Super League Dream Team on three occasions.

A prolific try scorer, Makinson scored over 200 tries for St Helens and has since notched 20 tries in 37 appearances for Catalans after joining the club ahead of the 2025 season. He also represented England over 20 times.

"As the 2026 season moves towards its final stages, I feel now is the right time to announce that this will be my final season as a professional rugby league player," Makinson posted on Instagram.

Image: Makinson played for St Helens between 2011 and 2024, winning five Super League titles

"Rugby league has been incredibly kind to me, and when I look back on the journey I've been on, I feel nothing but pride and gratitude. I've been very fortunate to live out a dream I had as a kid and represent some of the biggest clubs both in England and France and also the pinnacle which is representing my country.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch Makinson score a special try for St Helens with millimetres to work with against Leigh Leopards

"There have been so many highs, some difficult moments, incredible memories and friendships that will last a lifetime. I wouldn't have been able to experience any of it without the unbelievable support I've had from my family, friends, team-mates, coaches, staff, supporters and everyone who has played a part in my career. To each and every one of you, thank you.

"I've still got a few games left, and I want to enjoy every second of them. I'll be taking it all in, appreciating the moments and giving everything I have to finish this chapter of my career in the best possible way.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Makinson makes acrobatic pass to Reimis Smith who goes over for an impressive Catalans Dragons try against Hull FC

"It's hard to put into words what rugby league has given me, but I know how lucky I am to have lived this life and played the game I love for as long as I have."

Sports.title: Thorslund ends Johnson's undisputed run to become world champion again
Sports.content:
Dina Thorslund is a world champion again after ending Cherneka Johnson's undisputed run to cap an emotional return to the sport.

Just over a year after vacating her WBC and WBO bantamweight titles because she was pregnant, the undefeated Thorslund fought aggressively from the start to snatch the WBC, WBO, WBA and IBF titles from Johnson, winning every round in a unanimous decision in the main event of MVPW-5 in Orlando, Florida.

Thorslund (25-0, nine KOs) vacated her titles in June 2025, and a month later she announced on social media that she had suffered a miscarriage.

She returned to the ring in January and defeated Almudena Alvarez to capture the vacant WBC interim featherweight title. Then Thorslund, who is 32 years old and from Denmark, dropped back to bantamweight to fight for the undisputed championship.

"This has been such an emotional journey for me the last year," Thorslund said, fighting back tears.

"I'm going to take this [title belt] straight back to Raven and say thank you."

Image: Johnson (left) and Thorslund finally met in the headline act of MVPW-05 in Orlando

Thorslund was in control for the whole fight. Her aggressive combinations put Johnson on the defensive, especially early, and through three rounds, Thorslund had landed 37 punches to Johnson's 14. Johnson (19-3, eight KOs), who became undisputed champion by knocking out Shurretta Metcalf in July 2025, was unable to utilise her power against Thorslund. Practically every time she connected, Thorslund would respond by landing three or four shots in return.

The French 18th seed looked dominant early on in the Montreal contest, utilising his powerful serve well to wrap up the first set without much hassle.

Norrie stepped up a gear in the second, matching Fils' power to force a tie-break.

Despite creating two set-point opportunities, Norrie was ultimately unable to convert when it mattered and Fils sealed the win in one hour and 43 minutes.

Norrie knocked out third seed Alex de Minaur in the round prior, turning the tables from match-point down by winning 11 out of the next 13 games to beat the Australian 5-7 7-6 (7-5) 6-1 - a victory that saw him become British No 1 again in place of Arthur Fery - but he was unable to build on that win.

The 16th-seeded ​Alexandrova fought a hard battle lasting nearly two-and-a-half hours to secure her quarter-final ​berth.

Sabalenka, a four-time Grand Slam champion and ‌reigning US Open winner, recovered from a set down to force a ​decider but was unable to halt Alexandrova's aggressive shot-making in the final set.

Image: Aryna Sabalenka suffered a shock Canadian Open loss against Ekaterina Alexandrova at the last-16 stage

The Belarusian broke early in the opening set ​before Alexandrova rallied to force a tie-break, ⁠which the Russian won to ⁠move ahead.

Sabalenka responded by seizing control of the second set with a break for a ‌4-3 lead before serving out to level the match.

Alexandrova held her nerve in the decider as Sabalenka's error count rose. ‌Serving to stay in the match at 4-5, the top seed saved two match points, but a double fault on the third handed victory to the Russian.

"I just tried to play ⁠every single point as if it was ​the last one because with her, you don't [get] ​a lot of chances during the match," Alexandrova ​said in her on-court interview.

"Honestly, I was trying not ⁠to think about the score or anything. Just hit the ball, and that's it.

"I'm super happy that I could win because ⁠after the second set, I thought [the ​chance] was already past me."

Sports.title: Hogh hits hat-trick as Celtic ease past hapless Kilmarnock
Sports.content:
Record signing Kasper Hogh silenced his early critics with a first-half hat-trick as Celtic swept Kilmarnock aside on the new grass pitch at Rugby Park.

Manager Martin O'Neill was absent from the dugout as he recovers from surgery, but it did not hinder the Hoops as Hogh nodded into an empty net after just 64 seconds.

Killie have switched from plastic to grass, but any hopes Neil McCann had of it favouring his side faded with the Danish striker fired in his second after Benjamin Nygren had hit the crossbar.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Hogh runs rampant with first-half hat-trick for Celtic.

The £11m signing then headed home his third with Max Stryjek only able to watch. It then went from bad to worse for the Kilmarnock keeper when he played the ball straight out to Nygren to fire in a fourth just after the break.

Michael Schjonning-Larsen managed to pull a goal back, but Luke McCowan then volleyed in Celtic's fifth just moments after coming on to wrap up an impressive afternoon in Ayrshire.

The champions' title defence starts with back-to-back wins, while Kilmarnock have conceded nine goals in their opening two games.

The key moments from Rugby Park

2: GOAL! Hogh is off the mark. Celtic's record signing meets Engels' cross at the back post and nods into the net.

5: CLOSE! Almost an equaliser! John-Jules' shot from inside the box is blocked by Trusty.

12: SAVE! John-Jules directs his header towards goal but Sinisalo tips it over.

18: OFF THE BAR! Engels cuts the ball back to Nygren in the box but he smashes it off the woodwork.

33: GOAL! Two for Hogh. Kilmarnock fail to deal with the danger and he fires beyond Stryjek.

35: GOAL! Make that a first-half hat-trick. Duran's cross takes out Stryjek, leaving Hogh to nod into the empty net.

47: GOAL! Howler from the Kilmarnock keeper! Stryjek inexplicably passes the ball straight out to Nygren an he makes no mistake.

49: OFF THE BAR! Duran wants in on the action, but the summer signing hits the woodwork.

56: GOAL! The hosts pull one back as Schjonning-Larsen finds the bottom corner.

'A lot of cause for optimism'

The Sky Sports pundits assessed Kasper Hogh's impact at Rugby Park.

Aiden McGeady

"He's a really refreshing character. Today, I think he was fantastic.

"It wasn't just his goals and his movement in the penalty box, he could have scored four or five, it was his hold-up play and his unselfish runs as well.

"I'm absolutely delighted that he's managed to answer some critics after his first game. A lot of cause for optimism."

Image: Kasper Hogh scored the first hat-trick of his career

James McFadden

"He's new into the club. People maybe looked at him last week and said he really should have been doing better, but I'm sure he would have agreed.

"He's reading the type of cross that's coming in.

"The more they play together, the better the understanding will be and the more goals he'll score.

"There's no doubt he's going to score goals."

Kris Boyd

"His all-round game was excellent today. His hold-up play, his willingness to get in the box."

Maloney: 'We've set a bar'

Celtic assistant Shaun Maloney speaking to Sky Sports:

"We started the game the exact opposite of how we did the Dundee home game and then we never really came off it.

"I think we've seen him [Kasper Hogh] for months now, so you know the level of player he is and what he's done at his previous club and a really high level in the Champions League.

"I said before, it's the life of a striker. I think you're there, you score some, you miss some. He was really good today.

"He scored a brilliant hat-trick, but a big part of his game was when Kilmarnock went man for man. He had to hold it. It's something the boss is really, really strong on and it made a big difference.

"His all-round game was really good, Kasper.

"I thought our creativity in the final third was as good as I've seen it in a little while.

"We were really good in the final third. We've set a bar now and we have to keep trying to get there."
