Sports.title: How Trabzonspor shocked Turkish rivals to make Mohamed Salah their Black Sea saviour
Sports.content:
It began with a text sent during the World Cup. Ertugrul Dogan, the president of Trabzonspor, was watching Egypt when he picked up his phone and messaged his manager, Fatih Tekke. “Coach,” it read. “Do you want Mohamed Salah?”

Tekke’s response was immediate enthusiasm, though Trabzonspor’s initial push for Salah went under the radar with Besiktas looking most likely to land the former Liverpool striker. In Turkish football, Istanbul’s Big Three – Galatasaray, Fenerbahce and Besiktas – have long held monopoly on the Super Lig’s marquee signings.

Istanbul is not the capital but it is the undisputed financial, cultural and commercial heartbeat of the country and wider region. It came as a shock, then, when Salah opted for Trabzonspor.

The club are by no means minnows. They form part of the traditional Big Four alongside their Istanbul rivals. Yet the football-crazy port city on the eastern Black Sea coast lacks the cosmopolitan lifestyle Istanbul offers. What it possesses instead is devotion. Most Turkish cities do not have a strong local football identity, with residents supporting one of the major Istanbul sides from afar. Trabzon is one of the few exceptions. The entire region eats, sleeps and breathes for its team.

Trabzon is like the Newcastle of Turkey: a proud, working-class city in the north-east with an industrial maritime past, deeply tied to its football club and trying to forge a new identity to adapt to the modern world.

Salah’s arrival has thrust a city that often feels politically and geographically sidelined onto the global stage. This transfer is bigger than football. Trabzon wants to revitalise the city as a maritime trade, tourism and logistics hub. The arrival of the Egyptian superstar ensures an even bigger spotlight on the city.

View image in fullscreen An excited Trabzonspor fan decked in traditional claret and sky blue colours sports sunglasses decorated with new signing Mohamed Salah. Photograph: Ümit Bektaş/Reuters

The chaotic scenes at Trabzon airport on Wednesday – when supporters turned the terminal into a sea of red flares, followed by tens of thousands packing Papara Park for Salah’s signing ceremony – demonstrated their fervour.

Salah could easily have accepted lucrative proposals in the Saudi Pro League or Major League Soccer, but their fan culture pales by comparison. Crucially, the 34-year-old remains in a highly competitive league in the Uefa zone; Trabzonspor need only navigate the playoff rounds for a place in the Europa League group stage.

“I am seeing a reception like this for the first time in my life,” Salah told the roaring crowd during his unveiling. “I came here to win trophies. I am here to bring titles to this club.”

Trabzonspor have played the role of disruptors in Turkish football – the Black Sea rebels who broke Istanbul’s stranglehold in the 1970s and most recently won the league title in 2021–22. But never before has a player of this magnitude rejected Istanbul for Trabzon.

View image in fullscreen Salah takes a photo as the fans offer a hearty welcome. Photograph: Ümit Bektaş/Reuters

The Turkish top flight is experiencing a renaissance. Leandro Trossard joined Besiktas after a title-winning campaign with Arsenal; Victor Osimhen continues to spearhead Galatasaray’s attack; while Nathan Aké and Mason Greenwood now line up for Fenerbahce. The league is also developing world-class homegrown talent, with Arda Güler at Real Madrid and Ferdi Kadioglu at Brighton serving as prime examples.

Trabzonspor’s pursuit of Salah was executed in the shadows. The club deployed their former winger Mahmoud Hassan – known as Trézéguet – as their secret operative. Salah’s international teammate spoke with the Egyptian captain daily, to help convince him to consider the move.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

There was a cultural element, too: moving to a welcoming, Muslim-majority nation where Salah and his family could feel immediately at home. Trabzonspor locked him into a two-year contract through to June 2028 and disclosed the financial details on the Public Disclosure Platform (KAP). Salah will earn a base annual salary of €10m (£8.5m) alongside a guaranteed €7m annual signing bonus, netting him €17m per season (€34m net over two years).

Because wages in Turkey are paid net, with the club covering all tax liabilities, Salah in effect takes home 50% more than his final Liverpool contract. The deal also includes performance add-ons, a 5% agent’s fee on gross wages and an extraordinary image-rights agreement granting Salah a 20% royalty on all personal merchandise sold through the club’s official TS Club retail network.

The commercial return was immediate. Within 24 hours of Salah landing, Trabzonspor sold more than 17,000 season tickets, generating £11m. Dogan confirmed that total projected revenue from tickets, sponsorships and merchandise during the Salah era is expected to approach £22m, in effect self-funding the transfer.

View image in fullscreen Trabzonspor supporters unveil a banner celebrating Salah. Photograph: Nurgul Gunaydin/AFP/Getty Images

Crucially, Trabzonspor did not overextend themselves. Balanced by roughly €95m raised in player sales since last season, the transfer is manageable financially. Salah joins a side on an upward trajectory under Tekke. Languishing in 13th when Tekke took over in March 2025, the team recovered to finish eight points behind the champions, Galatasaray, in third and won the Turkish Cup.

Tekke added the Valencia defender Cenk Özkacar and the Manchester United loanee André Onana in goal and Trabzonspor are in talks with Darwin Núñez.

Taking his favoured No 10 shirt, Salah steps into a side in the ascendant. Yet the challenge remains steep. Galatasaray have won four consecutive league titles, while Besiktas and Fenerbahce have spent lavishly this summer. Trabzonspor will be hoping his arrival serves as a catalyst for a change in fortunes.

For Trabzon and the eastern region, however, Salah’s arrival is far more than a transfer story. The tide could be turning back in the favour of the Black Sea Storm.

Sports.title: Martin O’Neill absent from Celtic’s win at Kilmarnock as Høgh hits hat-trick
Sports.content:
Kasper Høgh scored a hat-trick, his first goals for Celtic, as the Scottish champions made light of the absence of their manager Martin O’Neill with a 5-1 win away to Kilmarnock on Sunday.

Victory made it two wins out of two Scottish Premiership games for Celtic, with 74-year-old boss O’Neill missing the trip to Rugby Park after what the club had said earlier this week was a “small procedure” in hospital.

No details were given about O’Neill’s operation, which came after the veteran Northern Irish boss took charge of Celtic’s win against Dundee in their first game of the season.

But the club’s assistant manager, Shaun Maloney, speaking before Sunday’s kick-off, said O’Neill was on the mend.

“He is doing better again,” Maloney told Sky Sports. “He came to the team hotel and spoke to the players but he just needs an extra few days.”

And O’Neill’s mood would doubtless have been improved by the performance of his side, with Celtic 3-0 ahead before half-time thanks to Høgh’s treble.

The Danish striker, who joined in July from Bodø/Glimt, needed less than a minute to score his first Celtic goal, heading in at the back post from a cross by Arne Engels.

Høgh doubled Celtic’s lead in the 33rd minute, with Camilo Durán seizing on Johnly Yfeko’s pass out of defence.

He combined with Benjamin Nygren to work the ball to Hogh on the left edge of the box, with the forward finishing well.

Two minutes later, Høgh had his hat-trick. Nygren slipping the ball right for Duran, whose cross took the Kilmarnock goalkeeper Max Stryjek out of play, with Høgh nodding into an empty net.

Celtic extended their lead early in the second half after they were effectively gifted a fourth goal by Stryjek.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

His pass out of defence went straight to Nygren in front of goal and his shot into the top corner made it 4-0.

Michael Schjønning-Larsen pulled a goal back for Kilmarnock in the 56th minute after finishing a well-worked move.

But Celtic went four goals ahead again when Luke McCowan, moments after coming on, volleyed in from close range 15 minutes from time after Kilmarnock made a mess of trying to clear the ball from a corner.

In Sunday’s other Scottish Premiership matches, Hearts – last season’s runners-up – are at home to Dundee United as they look to bounce back from their opening-day defeat by Aberdeen, with Motherwell hosting Falkirk and Rangers facing Hibernian at Ibrox.

Sports.title: Alexia Putellas: ‘I’m hungry to win, to fight with my teammates for victory’
Sports.content:
Momentarily, Alexia Putellas appears somewhat nervous, stepping inside the cramped conference room in a Kent hotel to see 23 reporters squeezed inside, all eager to hear from the Women’s Super League’s newest global superstar, but she quickly composes herself. Within minutes, she is into her stride, asking for tips about roast dinners and drawing laughs from the room as she jokes that her friends who play for other English clubs have told her they are going to kick her. Welcome to the WSL.

Speaking in English throughout the 20-minute session with ever-increasing proficiency, the two-time Ballon d’Or winner and four-time Champions League winner explains why she has swapped the prestige of Barcelona – where she has been idolised over a trophy-laden 14-year spell – for a team that finished 22 points adrift of the European qualification places last term.

Backed by the ambitious businesswoman Michele Kang, the independently run London City Lionesses have made eye-catching, world-class signings this summer, including the France forward Kadidiatou Diani from Lyonnes – who are also majority-owned by Kang – Putellas’s Barcelona teammate Mapi León and the former England goalkeeper Mary Earps from PSG.

Undoubtedly, though, Putellas is the biggest of them all and the signing that will have made all of women’s football take notice. As a serial winner will Putellas have to be patient for trophies here?

“Both can live together, my mentality and the moment of the project. I’m going to bring to the project whatever the project needs from me, so I’m 100% committed,” the 2023 World Cup winner says. “I’m hungry to win, to be better day after day, to fight with my teammates for the victory. I’m going to try to give my best to the team and let’s see at the end of the season how good we were.”

View image in fullscreen Barcelona made Putellas a parting gift of a photo of herself surrounded by every trophy she’d won while at the club. Photograph: Albert Gea/Reuters

London City Lionesses were promoted to the WSL in 2025, finished sixth last season in their top-flight debut and are yet to win a major trophy. Asked what her expectations are, Putellas says: “I don’t have expectations. I just want the hard work we are doing to speak for itself. It’s a hard competition. Of course, I have a competitive mind and I want to win every game. But I don’t have expectations in this sport. In my opinion, you shouldn’t. Just work in the back[ground] and give everything.”

Putellas was named as the Women’s Champions League’s player of the season after helping fire Barcelona to a fourth European title in six seasons, yet at the age of 32, she still feels she can improve – “Of course, always, day after day, I want to learn things [and] just keep going, I never stop [trying to] be as good as I can,” – but specifically she thinks the WSL can add elements to her skillset.

“It will be different, but that’s why I’m here, because I’m looking forward to improving myself,” she says. “It’s being a more complete player, as much as I can. It’s about learning new things, playing with and against other players and just trying to find where my limits are. It will take time because it’s a new beginning and a big change for me.

View image in fullscreen Alexia Putellas will be hoping to stamp her name on more than just her contract and the camera after joining London City Lionesses. Photograph: London City Lionesses

“[In the WSL] you never know what will be the result of the game; it’s a very competitive league, week after week. I imagine all the games will push you to your limits. It’s a very entertaining league.

“The first conversation [I had with London City] was about what the club wants and how ambitious the project is. I want to be part of that journey, bring the experience I have and learn as a player and make me more complete. I made the move for that and just being in other positions that I’ve never been in. In my opinion, this league can give me that.”

When asked if she had sought advice from her former Barcelona teammates, such as the England duo Keira Walsh and Lucy Bronze, about what to expect in England, she says: “Well, some of them told me that it’s a hard league and they’re going to kick me. No, I’m just joking.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

She also chuckled when asked about London’s traffic and expensive property prices, even if she was slightly hesitant reflecting on her first taste of an English fry-up: “Erm, yes. It was quite different. Not the beans, but the sausages and eggs. It was fine.”

View image in fullscreen Alexia Putellas scored twice when Spain thrashed England 4-0 in June, ending the Lionesses’ chances of automatic World Cup qualification. Photograph: Francisco Ubilla/Reuters

She will have plenty of help when it comes to settling into the London City, with six Spanish teammates and a head coach, Eder Maestre, who she says did a “really good job with Tenerife”. Maestre, yet another coaching export of the Basque Country, was at Tenerife for a year and a half, finishing sixth in his only full season and taking them to fifth by the time he left for England.

Putellas knows there will be differences tactically in the English game and thinks that can help her add even more strings to her bow.

“I really believe that moving to England can give me something more,” she says. “Like, I can control the low blocks and all this stuff; I am used to it playing in Spain. I have already controlled that, so [I want] different kind of games or box-to-box and all this stuff.”

She then apologises for her English – not that any apology was needed – and explains she is still learning the language and working hard to improve it all the time. If her footballing ability continues to enhance too, then WSL defenders had better beware.

Sports.title: ‘It’s a true art form’: Nigeria goalkeeper Maduka Okoye on high fashion and life at Udinese
Sports.content:
When Maduka Okoye visited Paris fashion week for the Jean Paul Gaultier show, taking his seat in the front row alongside rapper Cardi B, the online reaction was swift. Within hours, footage of the Udinese and Nigeria goalkeeper was all over TikTok and Instagram – where his audience now stretches to nearly two million followers – transforming the appearance into a viral cultural moment that crossed beyond the boundaries of football.

Yet ask Okoye to reflect on his sudden explosion into the fashion ecosystem, and he frames it not as a pursuit of celebrity or status, but as a genuine interest in art. “Being at the Paris fashion week was really impressive,” Okoye says. “It was my first time really coming into contact with high fashion, and it was fascinating. It’s a true art form. I enjoyed it immensely and since that moment I’ve become a much bigger fan of fashion than I was before.”

In an era where elite footballers are expected to be multi-dimensional figures – balancing performance on the pitch, personal branding, digital presence, and commercial partnerships – Okoye embodies a generation navigating this global landscape with ease. Crucially, he knows exactly where to steer the ship.

While some athletes run the danger of losing their bearings when the off-pitch spotlight intensifies, the goalkeeper draws a sharp, impenetrable line between his two realms.

“What happens off the pitch is one thing, what happens on the pitch is another,” he says. “You have to separate the two. I never let these two worlds collide. Even though marketing and personal branding are part of the business today, at the end of the day I am a goalkeeper, and my main job is to protect my team’s goal. Outside football, I pursue things that matter to me but my priority and my work remain between the posts. These two worlds don’t overlap. What I do off the pitch has zero impact on what I do on it, and those two spheres will never cross.”

Reinforcing that boundary is the daily environment in which Okoye operates. Playing for Udinese, nestled in the calm, industrious region of Friuli-Venezia Giulia, creates a vivid contrast with the flashing cameras of Paris or the hyper-fast churn of social media trends. For Okoye, who grew up in Düsseldorf, Udine offers an essential sanctuary.

View image in fullscreen Maduka Okoye arrived at Udinese after spells at Sparta Rotterdam and Watford. Photograph: Foto Petrussi/Udinese FC

“I grew up in a big city, so in my heart I am and always will be a city boy, used to the metropolitan rhythm,” he smiles. “However, as you grow older, you learn to appreciate the peaceful side of life. I really like Udine. It’s a human, quiet city. You have your peace there and you can focus 100% on your work. I’m genuinely happy to live here. The serenity in Udine is good for you as a person and makes you feel very comfortable.”

That quiet focus away from the noise is paying dividends on the pitch. Having arrived after spells with Sparta Rotterdam and Watford – where he only made two senior appearances – he has established himself as a cornerstone between the posts for Udinese. In a footballing landscape often obsessed with highlight-reel saves, Okoye is staying focused.

“I believe there is always room for improvement in every direction,” he says. “I’m very happy working here with a great goalkeeping staff. I’m on a good path, learning every day, and I can’t wait to show it on the pitch during the season.”

When asked which goalkeeper impressed him most during the recent World Cup, Okoye says: “I found Spain’s Unai Simón very impressive, especially towards the final stages. Not so much for making hundreds of saves, but for the way he remained inside the game, defending deep balls against France. For me, that was goalkeeping of the highest level.

“As I said, it’s not just about spectacular saves; it’s about managing those details. Overall it was a great World Cup, and for us young goalkeepers it was a fantastic learning opportunity.”

Okoye’s drive to absorb lessons from top-tier athletes extends beyond football. During a recent visit to the British Grand Prix at Silverstone, he met rising Italian Formula One driver Kimi Antonelli, taking the opportunity to study the mechanics of another high-level sport.

“It was fantastic. The whole Formula One experience was extraordinary,” Okoye says. “I think there’s so much an athlete can learn from other sports. Meeting the drivers, especially Kimi, was great. From the outside you only see the race on TV, but behind it there’s an immense amount of work going on. It was impressive to see how much effort and preparation go into competing at that level.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Maduka Okoye enjoyed his visit to the British Grand Prix where he presented Kimi Antonelli with his pole position award after qualifying. Photograph: David Davies/PA

Udinese enter the Serie A season with stability and ambition and, in Friuli, that means looking towards Europe. “Everything is possible,” Okoye says. “But I think we should talk about that again in February or March. First we have to get the basics right and take it game by game. Then we’ll see where we are. We certainly have the quality, the players, an excellent staff, and a solid club behind us. Udinese is a club where a player can really grow and make that leap in quality.

“For me, Serie A remains one of the best leagues in the world and I’m grateful to be part of it. The higher the level of the league, the happier and prouder I am to play in it. We’re working hard and can’t wait to compete against the best.”

There is also unfinished business with Nigeria. Watching the World Cup from his living room was far from ideal. “Obviously it would have been better to be part of it, but unfortunately we didn’t qualify,” Okoye acknowledges. “We’ll try again for the next World Cup. I still enjoyed watching it from the outside; I supported Germany, hoping they’d go a bit further. Now we look to the future, and I really hope to be there at the next edition.”

As football continues to evolve into a convergence of sport, entertainment and global culture, figures such as Okoye offer a compelling blueprint for the modern athlete. He is a player capable of sitting in the front row in Paris on Monday, studying a rival on screen on Wednesday, and commanding his penalty box on Sunday – all without losing his sporting identity.

“On a personal level, it hasn’t changed me at all. I’m still the exact same person,” Okoye says. “Of course, when it comes to business and my personal image, a lot of things have changed. Fortunately, I have a great team around me and we try to make the most of these opportunities. But I repeat: who I am hasn’t changed. It’s simply part of my professional journey.”

And what advice would Okoye offer a young footballer dreaming of putting on the gloves and following in his footsteps? The Udinese goalkeeper does not hesitate: “To work hard, believe in yourself, and have faith.”

Sports.title: Fifa defends Gianni Infantino and launches attack after ‘effort to undermine’ president
Sports.content:
Fifa last night issued a thinly-veiled attack on Uefa and other leading figures in European football in a statement which alleged there is a “concerted and ongoing effort by some to undermine Fifa and its president,” as football’s civil war escalated further.

Uefa has made it clear they regard Infantino’s continued leadership of world football as untenable following his role in the World Cup sell-off plans, while the Guardian revealed on Friday the Norwegian Football Federation has publicly called on him to resign, with Fifa responding by accusing them of attempting to subvert the organisation’s democratic processes.

Fifa’s latest defence of Infantino followed Uefa’s confirmation on Saturday that a “departure payment” was made to a female employee who is alleged to have been in a relationship with Fifa president while he was the organisation’s general secretary over a decade ago.

The Daily Telegraph had reported on Friday night that the woman received a six-figure sum following the alleged relationship with Infantino, allegations Fifa dismissed as “categorically untrue.”

Fifa went further last night by accusing Infantino’s critics of attempting to remove him from office before next March’s presidential election.

As previously reported by the Guardian, Uefa is seeking support from other confederations to call an Emergency Fifa Congress to trigger a vote of no confidence in the president, but their own members can provide the 43 votes to call a meeting it is unclear whether they would reach the threshold of 106 of the 211 Fifa members required to unseat Infantino.

North American confederation Concacaf are aligned with Uefa, while there is some support amongst the Asian Football Confederation, but the Confederation of African Football and South American confederation Conmebol have both publicly announced their backing for Infantino.

“Echoing the recent statements of Conmebol and CAF, as well as discussions with Fifa Member Associations and Confederations from around the world, Fifa will not support, facilitate or tolerate any process concerning the election of the Fifa President that is inconsistent with Fifa’s Statutes, democratic procedures and established governance framework,” a Fifa spokesperson said. “The Fifa President was democratically elected by Fifa’s Member Associations and continues to serve with their mandate.

“The Fifa president was democratically elected by Fifa’s member associations and continues to serve with their mandate. Those who do not have the support of Fifa’s member associations should not seek to achieve through allegation, insinuation or misinformation what they cannot achieve through Fifa’s established democratic processes.”

Uefa had responded to Fifa’s proposal to sell 20% of a new company controlling the World Cup’s commercial assets with a threat backed by all 55 European countries to boycott their tournaments unless the plans were abandoned, which they were less than 48 hours later.

Significantly however, Uefa released a new statement last Thursday after Fifa had confirmed that Infantino retained the organisation’s “full support” following a crisis meeting of their management board in Rabat the previous day, saying that nothing had changed and that the boycott threat remained in place.

Fifa is now convinced that Uefa is behind coordinated attempts to remove Infantino. It is unclear what further concessions Uefa is demanding to cancel the boycott, which faces its first test next month at the Under-20 Women’s World Cup in Poland.

Fifa’s statement last night also included a new attack on the media, a well-worn tactic used by Infantino.

“Recent reporting has included unsubstantiated assertions and demonstrably false claims concerning Fifa and its president,” a spokesperson said. “Speculation and insinuation should not be presented as fact, and repetition does not make an allegation true.

“Fifa welcomes legitimate scrutiny. But scrutiny is not a licence to distort facts, amplify unsubstantiated allegations or manufacture distractions designed to undermine progress.

“Where reporting is inaccurate or misleading, Fifa will challenge it directly and vigorously. Fifa’s responsibility is to its 211 member associations and to football around the world. We will not be distracted or diverted from strengthening the organisation, delivering for our member associations and continuing the work of making football truly global.”

Sports.title: Mason Mount injury overshadows Manchester United’s draw with PSG
Sports.content:
Manchester United managed a creditable 1-1 draw with the European champions, Paris Saint-Germain, in a Gothenburg friendly on Saturday but the result was overshadowed by an injury to Mason Mount.

The England midfielder, who joined United from Chelsea in 2023, has been hampered by injury problems since arriving at Old Trafford and he lasted fewer than 20 minutes after starting against PSG.

Mount, 27, appeared to suffer a foot injury in Sweden and, after discussions with coaches on the touchline, left the field to be replaced by Tyler Fletcher. Mount has been restricted to 54 league appearances – many of them as a substitute – during his first three seasons with United.

“He got kicked,” ⁠Carrick told reporters of Mount. “We just wanted to be careful and look after him. ‌We’ve been lucky with injuries so far, so we wanted to be careful.“

His side were 1-0 down to PSG at the time of his injury, having gone behind in the second minute through an Ibrahim Mbaye goal even though the French giants were missing many of their star players.

But Bryan Mbeumo equalised in the 32nd minute when Amad Diallo played him in after winning the ball back.

There were more injury concerns for United early in the second half when their 40-year-old goalkeeper Tom Heaton suffered a right hamstring problem while rushing out to make a clearance.

Mbeumo might have doubled his tally but for the fine form of PSG’s Matvey Safonov but the goalkeeper left the pitch to jeers after escaping punishment for clattering into Joshua Zirkzee way outside his area – an incident that may well have led to him being punished in a competitive match.

There were late chances for Fletcher, Shea Lacey and the captain, Bruno Fernandes, who linked up well with new arrival Youri Tielemans in an encouraging sign for the United manager, Michael Carrick.

View image in fullscreen Mason Mount (back right) started the friendly in Gothenburg but had to be removed with an apparent injury. Photograph: Ash Donelon/Manchester United/Getty Images

“I enjoyed it,” Carrick told MUTV, United’s in-house television station. “Good challenge. Slightly different with the way they play. We should’ve scored more goals.

“It’s good for the boys sometimes to have to problem-solve and find their own way and I thought we did that. That prepares them for the season as well. In that respect there were a lot of things that maybe people don’t always see that we were quite happy with. There were some good signs there.”

United have two more friendly fixtures, against bitter rivals Leeds in Dublin on Wednesday and AC Milan in Wroclaw three days later, before launching their Premier League campaign away to newly promoted Hull on 22 August.

Sports.title: Premier League managers have never been less English, title-winning or secure in their jobs
Sports.content:
Nine of the 20 Premier League clubs will begin the 2026-27 season with a different man in the dugout than the one who ended the last campaign. The only other seasons which started with so many men making their managerial debut for top flight clubs were 1888-89 and 1946-47; the inaugural season of league football and the first following the second world war. Neither occurred under normal circumstances yet the level of turnover this summer does not feel unusual. Job security has never meant less in the Premier League. Adding in the recently appointed pair of Roberto De Zerbi and Michael Carrick – confirmed in March and May respectively – means 11 teams are led by coaches with less than a year in their hotseat. The median tenure of Premier League managers at the start of each season has never been so low.

The most recent similar season was 2016-17. Heading into that campaign, 10 clubs had managers with less than one year in the role. But with respect to the current Premier League crop, the relatively new head coaches that summer included Antonio Conte, Pep Guardiola, Jürgen Klopp and José Mourinho. All had either already won the Premier League or would go on to do so.

With Arsène Wenger still at Arsenal, four of those considered the five big beasts of Premier League management were present, with the other (Alex Ferguson) having retired three years earlier. By contrast, Mikel Arteta is the only man who has won the English league who will be starting 2026-27 with the chance to do so again. There was also only one such manager two years ago, albeit it was Guardiola with his bulging trophy cabinet.

As Arteta has a single championship win, this season begins with the fewest English league titles on the division’s collective CV in the Premier League era. The previous lowest at the beginning of a campaign was three in 1995-96 (thanks to Ferguson having two and Howard Wilkinson one) and 2019-20 (Guardiola two, Manuel Pellegrini one).

This is a natural byproduct of managers being younger and less experienced. The median age of Premier League managers is 46.9 years old. It was the same heading into 2024-25 but was last younger 20 years ago. The drop in age has not led to further opportunities for Englishmen.

Eddie Howe’s departure from Newcastle means there will be three English managers when 2026-27 gets under way. The total was the same at the start of the last two campaigns, though interestingly it will be a different trio this year (Carrick, Frank Lampard and Gary O’Neil) than 12 months ago (Howe, Scott Parker and Graham Potter). The standing of the six clubs led by these men is worth considering. Two of the current coaches are at teams that have just been promoted, while two from last season’s group were with sides that went on to be relegated. Opportunities with relatively secure Premier League clubs are now rare for English managers, never mind at those with realistic title ambitions.

The top end of the division is likely to have a Spanish feel. The Basque region of Gipuzkoa is providing more head coaches to England’s top division than England, with Arsenal, Aston Villa, Chelsea and Liverpool led by men from that relatively small area of Spain. It’s plausible none of them will win the league given the presence of Manchester City (who themselves are under new management after a decade of Guardiola) but Arteta, Xabi Alonso and Andoni Iraola are in charge of three of the leading four clubs in the title betting market, with Unai Emery’s Villa seventh.

Managers from overseas lessening opportunities for English coaches in the Premier League is simply following the trend on the pitch: Just 8.6% of available minutes went to players from outside Britain or Ireland in 1992-93 yet a new high of 69.6% was reached last season. It is a truly global competition at every level, including ownership and sporting directors.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The influence of the latter on recruitment decisions has blurred the line between being a head coach and a manager. Liam Rosenior said he was “extremely humbled and honoured to be appointed head coach of Chelsea” when he was appointed by the Blues in January. “It fills me with immense pride to become manager of this great club,” was Xabi Alonso’s line when he secured essentially the same gig less than six months later. Based on the announcements clubs made to herald news of their appointments, the Premier League currently employs 14 head coaches and six managers.

Regardless of what the sign says on Alonso’s office door, he should reflect upon his new club giving him a four-year contract when they haven’t kept a manager for as long as two years since Conte left in 2018, or three years since Mourinho’s first spell in charge more than a decade earlier.

Rosenior learned this the hard way. He signed a six-and-a-half year deal yet Chelsea previously employed both Rafael Benítez and Guus Hiddink on interim bases for longer than the young Englishman lasted at the club. Head coach or manager, call it what you will. The profession has never offered shorter-term employment, or felt less English, in the Premier League.

Sports.title: Versatile Bruno Guimarães gives Mikel Arteta options to shuffle midfield pack | Ed Aarons
Sports.content:
If there was one of his many assets Newcastle supporters grew to love above all about Bruno Guimarães then it was best summed up by the man himself after being unveiled as Arsenal’s new £75m signing. “That’s a tough one,” said the Brazil midfielder when asked what fans in north London can expect from him. “I would say I can pass the ball, run a lot and play like a warrior. I’ll never give up.”

After more than four years on Tyneside and having seen Alexander Isak, Anthony Gordon and Sandro Tonali precede Eddie Howe’s departure, Guimarães – who was devastated after missing a penalty for the Seleção in their defeat against Norway in the last 16 of the World Cup – was determined to seize his opportunity.

While his emotional statement released by Newcastle as his move to Arsenal was confirmed on Saturday said they “did everything they could to keep me”, at the age of 28 he clearly felt it may never come again.

Andrea Berta’s pursuit of Vinícius Júnior came up short this week after the Brazil forward signed an improved six-year deal with Real Madrid. But at least Arsenal’s sporting director was finally able to bring in a player who was first courted by the club in the early days of Mikel Arteta’s reign, and who will add to the outstanding crop of central midfielders at his disposal.

Edu Gaspar, Berta’s predecessor, is understood to have first enquired about Guimarães when he was still at Athletico Paranaense in Brazil before he joined Lyon in the January 2020 transfer window – a few weeks after Arteta’s arrival at the Emirates.

They were also interested when Newcastle won the race to sign him in January 2022 for €40m, which came back to haunt Arsenal when he scored in a 2-0 win that went a long way to them missing out on Champions League qualification that season.

That first of nine appearances is the only time he scored against Arsenal, but Guimarães always impressed in a variety of roles whenever he came up against them, including in the Carabao Cup semi-final Newcastle won 4-0 on aggregate in 2025. He has covered more distance, won more duels and committed more fouls against Arsenal than any other side since making his Premier League debut.

It was no surprise that Declan Rice – the only player in the division to have covered more distance than Guimarães in that period and who enjoyed their fair share of battles – was one of the first to welcome him to Arsenal with a message that said “come here and please no more fights, now we’re friends”.

It is hard to argue with Guimarães that Arsenal have “one of the best midfields” in Europe because last season proved it. Yet having gone all the way to the Champions League final before spending the summer with England, after suffering with neural pain in his hamstring and lower back since December, Rice must be treated with the utmost care in the coming months. Guimarães can provide cover for him in a box-to-box role and gives Arteta options to rotate his other midfielders more frequently.

View image in fullscreen Bruno Guimarães will provide box-to-box cover for Declan Rice, rather than engage him in midfield combat. Photograph: David Price/Arsenal FC/Getty Images

He did not seem to trust Christian Nørgaard, who has joined Everton, to deputise for Martín Zubimendi in the Premier League last year, and that led to the Spain midfielder running out of steam in the spring.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Preview latest Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

It was telling that the teenager Myles Lewis-Skelly started in his preferred position at the base of midfield during the title run-in, and against Paris Saint-Germain in Budapest for the Champions League final, having begun the campaign as a left-back. Guimarães showed at Newcastle he is capable of playing in a deeper role as well and Arteta must decide how to balance his plethora of options in a crucial part of the pitch.

While he could not match Mikel Merino’s goalscoring exploits for Spain,Martin Ødegaard showed signs that he is back to his best during the World Cup after another disappointing season for Arsenal that was again interrupted by injury.

Having missed out on Morgan Rogers, the onus will be on the Norway captain, Guimarães and last summer’s big signing, Eberechi Eze, to provide some creativity to an attack that struggled to break down the low block at times last season.

Arsenal are still in the market for a defender to cover the absence of William Saliba for an extended period, while they would like to bring in another forward to add to the signing of Christos Tzolis. Atlético Madrid’s Julián Alvarez or Bradley Barcola of Paris Saint-Germain would fit the bill, although it remains to be seen if they will bring in a marquee player without offloading Gabriel Martinelli and Gabriel Jesus – who has interest from Napoli. Even if they do depart, the presence of another familiar face in the Brazil centre-back Gabriel should also help Guimarães settle into his new home.

“Big Gabi was very excited,” he told Arsenal’s website. “Every time he sent me the message: ‘We’ll wait for you, when will you come?’ I’m so excited to join them, not only the Brazilians, we have an amazing squad here. I’m so excited to meet the other players, to start training. I just want to give my best.”

Sports.title: Lionel Messi lands back in Rosario after father Jorge's death at 68... as Inter Miami teammate pays heartfelt tribute during game
Sports.content:
Lionel Messi has returned to his hometown of Rosario following the death of his father, Jorge.

Messi missed Inter Miami's Leagues Cup clash with Monterrey to fly back to Argentina where, according to reports in South America, the 39-year-old will attend a private memorial service.

Jorge Messi - who also served as his son's agent and business manager - died at the age of 68, two months on from the family revealing he had been rushed to hospital with an ongoing 'health situation'.

He reportedly passed away in a hospital in Rosario, close to the family home, at around 10pm local time on Friday August 7.

In the absence of their captain, Inter Miami players honored Jorge Messi by wearing black armbands, while fans paused for a moment of silence before kickoff. Earlier on Saturday, the team had posted a tribute which read: 'Our hearts are with our captain, Leo, and the entire Messi family.'

Against Monterrey, stand-in captain Rodrigo De Paul - Messi's international teammate - scored the opening goal and then pulled off his jersey to reveal another which read: 'Messi 10.' Unfortunately for Inter Miami, Monterrey scored late on to snatch a 2-1 win.

Lionel Messi has returned to his hometown of Rosario following the death of his father, Jorge

The soccer legend's father, pictured at the 2022 World Cup final, died at the age of 68

Rodrigo De Paul paid tribute to the Inter Miami captain during Saturday's clash with Monterrey

In the first official statement, Messi's first team Newell's Old Boys wrote in Spanish: 'Club Atletico Newell's Old Boys bids farewell with deep sorrow and grief to Jorge Messi, who passed away at the age of 68 in the city of Rosario.'

The club continued: 'Jorge was the pillar and the person who supported with vision, rigor, and affection the career of the greatest player of all time alongside his wife, Celia Cuccittini.

'His constant companionship and behind-the-scenes leadership were essential in backing every step of Lionel, from his beginnings at Malvinas to the pinnacle of world football glory. Thank you for teaching him to love these colors.'

Later on Saturday, both Barcelona and the Argentina national team added their own tributes.

'Stay strong, Leo Messi and family. We are with you in this difficult moment. We send you our most heartfelt embrace,' Argentina wrote on X.

A spokesperson for FC Barcelona, meanwhile, said in a statement: 'The President and the Board of Directors of FC Barcelona express their deepest condolences on the passing of Jorge Messi, the father of former Barca player and legend Lionel Messi, and, on behalf of the entire Barca family, extend their condolences to the Messi family.

'FC Barcelona thanks Jorge Messi for his commitment to our Club, for entrusting us with the beginnings and the most glorious years of his son Leo's football career. May he rest in peace.'

Sports.title: Manchester United interested in signing Leicester star, 18, who is already on radars of Arsenal and Aston Villa - as Man City striker enters talks with Southampton: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
Manchester United interested in signing Leicester star, 18, who is already on radars of Arsenal and Aston Villa - as Man City striker enters talks with Southampton: WINDOW WATCH

It's that time of the year again – the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period with clubs looking to make big signings ahead of next season.

Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team...

Man City striker in talks with Southampton

Manchester City striker Divin Mubama is in talks to join Southampton on loan for the season.

The former West Ham forward did well on loan at Stoke City last season up until he suffered an ankle ligament injury in January, incurred by a hefty challenge against QPR.

Manchester City striker Divin Mubama is in talks to join Southampton on loan for the season

He has bounced back to full fitness though and has impressed on City's pre-season tour scoring two goals, including a composed finish against Inter Milan, and weighing in with an assist.

The 21-year-old has had interest from a number of Championship clubs including Preston North End, Middlesbrough and Derby County.

Swedish international heads to Hull

Hull City have signed Sweden international Elliot Stroud from Swedish side Mjallby for around £3.5million.

The wing-back has joined on a four-year contract, which includes an option for a an extra year.

The 24-year-old played in all four of Sweden's matches at the World Cup.

West Ham make opening Parrott bid

West Ham have made an opening offer understood to be worth around £15million for AZ Alkmaar striker Troy Parrott

West Ham have made an opening offer understood to be worth around £15million for AZ Alkmaar striker Troy Parrott and are exploring a deal for Arsenal's Reiss Nelson.

Parrott, their leading goalscorer last season, started on the bench for Alkmaar's opening league game against Den Haag on Saturday.

The Hammers are prepared to break the Championship record of over £17.5million to get Parrott amid competition from Porto.

Nelson has been on the Hammers' radar before and has attracted interest from Fulham and Benfica in this window.

The 26-year-old had an indifferent campaign on loan at Brentford last season.

The Hammers had been pursuing a loan for Sunderland's Simon Adingra but he picked up an injury and has been wearing a protective boot on his left foot.

United keen on Page

Manchester United are interested in signing Leicester prospect Louis Page.

The 18-year-old midfielder has made 21 appearances for the Foxes and won EFL Apprentice of the Year last season.

Arsenal and Aston Villa have also expressed interest in the England Under-20 international but it is understood he wants to join United.

Charles closes on Fulham move

Fulham have agreed a £30million deal with Southampton for midfielder Shea Charles.

The 22-year-old is expected to undergo a medical in the next 24 hours and will sign a five-year contract with the option for an extra year.

Read the full story here.

Willock on Besiktas radar

Newcastle midfielder Joe Willock remains a target for Besiktas.

The Turkish side are working on an offer for the 26-year-old but believe Newcastle's current asking price is too high.

Joe Willock is a target of Turkish side Besiktas this month

Newcastle are continuing to work on a £13m deal for Marseille’s Pierre Emile Hojbjerg.

They want an experienced midfielder to work alongside new signings Sean Steur and Aladji Bamba.

Read the latest on Newcastle's summer transfer business here.

Race to sign Tuanzebe heats up

Free agent defender Axel Tuanzebe is attracting interest from Saudi Pro league and Premier League sides.

The 28-year-old centre back had an impressive World Cup on the back of a challenging season with Burnley in the top flight and is ready for a new challenge.

Axel Tuanzebe is drawing a lot of interest from both English sides and abroad

Everton and Brentford have looked at the former Manchester United academy graduate and he has drawn attention from abroad also.

He made 16 appearances and scored one goal last season and spent the two previous seasons with Ipswich Town.

Hamer closes on Cov return

Gus Hamer is due to undergo a medical after Coventry and Sheffield United agreed a £6million deal for the midfielder.

The package for the 29-year-old is worth £6m plus add-ons.

Hamer spent three years at Coventry between 2020 and 2023, becoming a real fans favourite scoring 19 goals in 132 appearances.

Blades manager Chris Wilder hinted last week that Hamer had asked to join Coventry and had already spoken to Frank Lampard. His medical is scheduled for today.

Sports.title: Marcus Rashford returns to Man United nearly TWO years after last appearance - as exiled Red Devils star prepares to link-up with Michael Carrick's squad
Sports.content:
Marcus Rashford has returned to Manchester United, almost two years after his last appearance for the club.

Rashford, 28, made 426 appearances for United after coming through the academy yet his career at Old Trafford appeared to be over after a falling out with Ruben Amorim.

That saw the former Red Devils boss freeze out the forward, with Rashford spending time away on loan at Aston Villa and Barcelona.

However, the Spanish giants declined to trigger a £26million option to buy him before their deadline in mid-June – despite head coach Hansi Flick admitting recently that he will miss the player – and no other clubs have been prepared to meet United’s £40m valuation.

And on Sunday, Rashford was seen returning to the club's Carrington training base for pre-season training, a moment many thought would never happen. He was then later pictured in Ireland ahead of their friendly against Leeds on Wednesday.

The 28-year-old, whose last game for United came on December 12, 2024 against Viktoria Plzen in the Europa League, was granted some extra time off after his exploits at the World Cup with England.

Marcus Rashford has returned to Man United, nearly two years after his last appearance

Rashford is pictured back in Manchester United's training kit on Sunday in Dublin, Ireland

Rashford spent last season on loan at Barcelona and his United career appeared to be over

As he arrived, Rashford stopped to greet adoring fans, with the forward saying 'thanks' as several of them welcomed him back.

He then posed for photos and headed on into United's base.

Michael Carrick had confirmed on Saturday that Rashford would join his squad as they head to the Republic of Ireland for the next stage of their pre-season, with Rashford set to imminently fly to Dublin to meet up with his team-mates.

Daily Mail Sport reported earlier this week that as it stands, the feeling at United and within Rashford’s camp is that he is likely to play for his boyhood club next season.

But with a month of the transfer window remaining, there is still uncertainty over his future.

Speaking after United's 1-1 draw against PSG, Carrick had been asked about Rashford's impending return.

He said: 'I've played with him. I played in the game he made his debut, so we have a history.

'We have got a full squad this week in Dublin. We fly straight there and have a few days where we have the whole group back together.

'Marcus is part of that, and Kobbie (Mainoo) and Lisandro (Martinez). We look forward to seeing them.'

Rashford posed for photos with fans and signed memorabilia as he arrived at United's base

Meanwhile, back in April, the United boss appeared to extend an olive branch to Rashford when questioned on his future.

'There's decisions to be made on certain things, and obviously Marcus is in that situation,' he added.

'But at this point in time, nothing's been decided. It will be, because it has to be at a certain point, but at this stage, there's nothing to say.'

Rashford scored 14 goals and provided as many assists at Barcelona last season and had indicated his desire to remain at the Nou Camp.

'I'm not a magician but if I was, I would stay,' he said in May. 'It's really good. I came here to win. I want to win as many things as I can.

'This team is a wonderful team. They're going to win so much in the future as well. To be a part of that would be special.'

Sports.title: Phil Foden's girlfriend puts England World Cup tops up for sale on second-hand clothing website - after Man City star was surprise omission from Thomas Tuchel's squad
Sports.content:
Phil Foden's girlfriend puts England World Cup tops up for sale on second-hand clothing website - after Man City star was surprise omission from Thomas Tuchel's squad

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Phil Foden's girlfriend Rebecca Cooke is reportedly trying to sell England World Cup shirts on resale website Vinted.

Man City star Foden was a surprise omission from Thomas Tuchel's squad for this summer's tournament, and it appears that snub also caught his partner by surprise.

According to a report in The Sun, Cooke, 25, is offering the white home and red away strip the Three Lions wore that she appeared to pick up in anticipation of Foden's involvement.

She has priced each kit at £70 on the second-hand website, although they have been slightly modified.

That adaptation was done by a clothing brand which tightened the waist, with the likes of Ellie Watkins, wife of England star Ollie, seen wearing a similar fit out in the US.

The report adds Essex-based company A Vintage Fit altered the shirts to a 'figure-hugging version' for £180.

Phil Foden's girlfriend Rebecca Cooke is reportedly trying to sell England World Cup shirts

Foden missed out on England's squad for the tournament but Cooke is trying to flog the shirts she appeared to pick up in anticipation of his inclusion

She is selling the home and away strips, although both of them have been modified slightly

Cooke is looking to flog both strips - which are 'new with tags' and in size 12-14 - for £70, cheaper than the £89.99 they will cost punters on the England website.

Cooke, who has three children with Foden, is said to have more than 100 items listed on her Vinted page, including four similarly adapted Man City tops.

Her account states: 'Selling new & used authentic items only. Account ran by management team.'

Commenting on her attempted sale of the England kits, a source told The Sun: 'Perhaps Rebecca had one foot on the plane when she got the tops.'

Foden didn't enjoy his best season in 2025-26 as Man City missed out on the title for the second year in a row, yet he still managed 12 goal contributions in the Premier League

Speaking earlier this week during Man City's pre-season tour of the Far East, the attacking midfielder opened up on his World Cup snub.

'I took some time off football, spent some good time with the family, and just rested,' he said.

'Going into this season, I just want to have a really good year, want to try and help the team as much as possible, and try and be one of the leaders, and hopefully win titles as well!'

Sports.title: Fulham agree £30million deal for Southampton's Shea Charles - after Man City decline opportunity to buy back midfielder
Sports.content:
Fulham agree £30million deal for Southampton's Shea Charles - after Man City decline opportunity to buy back midfielder

Fulham have agreed a £30million deal with Southampton for midfielder Shea Charles.

The 22-year-old is expected to undergo a medical in the next 24 hours and will sign a five-year contract with the option for an extra year.

The deal, as reported in today's Mail on Sunday, is understood to be £27m plus a further £3m and the final go-ahead for Fulham was held up as they had to wait for clearance from Manchester City who had matching rights.

Shea Charles is set to complete a £30million move to Fulham from Southampton

The Northern Ireland international has been looking to depart for a chance to play in the Premier League after Spygate cost him and his teammates a place in the play off final.

Leeds United had three offers rejected for Charles but now Fulham have been successful and he is heading to join up with new boss Alvaro Arbeloa at Craven Cottage.

Sports.title: Newcastle add former Tottenham midfielder Joao Palhinha to transfer shortlist as move for Marseille's Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg ramps up - plus fitness update on Tino Livramento and Lewis Miley
Sports.content:
Newcastle add former Tottenham midfielder Joao Palhinha to transfer shortlist as move for Marseille's Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg ramps up - plus fitness update on Tino Livramento and Lewis Miley

Newcastle have identified Joao Palhinha as an option in their search for an experienced midfielder to fill the void left by Bruno Guimaraes and Sandro Tonali.

Talks continue over a move for Marseille’s Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg and a deal in the region of £13million could accelerate over the next 48 hours.

Daily Mail Sport understands the 31-year-old has indicated he is keen on the switch and new head coach Matthias Jaissle sees the Dane as the potential organiser at the base of his young midfield.

However, there is still work to do on that transfer and alternatives have been identified, including Palhinha. Aston Villa are also interested in the Bayern Munich midfielder, 31, and he looks set to return to the Premier League this summer after spending last season on loan at Tottenham.

Newcastle like the Portugal international and he fits the profile of older head they want to complement new arrivals such as Sean Steur, 18, and Aladji Bamba, 20.

Sporting director Ross Wilson is prioritising a midfield addition and a new full-back, with signings beyond that dependent on Jaissle’s assessment of what his squad then needs.

Joao Palhinha is another experienced midfielder Newcastle are considering to fill the void left by the departures of Bruno Guimaraes and Sandro Tonali

Tino Livramento is not expected to be fit for Newcastle's season opener as he recovers from the injury he picked up on England duty at the World Cup

Midfielder Joe Willock will join Besiktas if they meet Newcastle’s asking price, and sources believe there will likely be progress on that front. Goalkeeper Nick Pope has also been told he can leave and, while no offer has yet arrived, both Ipswich and Celtic are said to be monitoring his situation.

Meanwhile, Newcastle expect midfielder Lewis Miley to be fit for the season opener against Liverpool after recovering from a broken leg, but the game will come too soon for Tino Livramento.

The England defender is currently in the United States as he continues his rehabilitation from the calf injury that ruled him out of the World Cup. He could return on the second weekend of the campaign at Tottenham.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."
