World.title: IGP Disu receives Commonwealth Games Champion Ezekiel Nathaniel
World.content:
The Inspector-General of Police, Olatunji Disu, has received the 400m Hurdles Commonwealth Games champion, Ezekiel Nathaniel, a corporal, at the Force Headquarters in Abuja.

Speaking during the reception, the IGP said the victory underscored the longstanding relationship between the Nigeria Police Force and sports.

The police boss explained that Nathaniel’s achievement is a reminder of what police personnel can accomplish when provided with the necessary platform and support to excel both in their professional duties and sporting careers.

He said: “The Nigeria Police Force and sports have always been twins, bound together by shared values of discipline, teamwork and excellence.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“This victory is a powerful reminder of that bond, and of what our personnel can achieve when given the platform and support to thrive both in service and in competition.”

The IGP assured police athletes and personnel with sporting talent that the Force would continue to invest in and support police sports, promising to identify, nurture, and celebrate talent within its ranks.

“I want Corporal Ezekiel Nathaniel, and every officer watching, to know that this Force will continue to invest in and support police sports.

“We will keep identifying, nurturing and celebrating talent within our ranks, because a Force that is strong in body and spirit is a Force that serves the nation better.”

Mr Disu, who described himself as a sportsman, said he was particularly proud of Nathaniel’s achievement.

He added that the feat had brought honour to the officer, the Nigeria Police Force and the country.

He said: “As a sportsman myself, I take particular pride in this achievement. Corporal Ezekiel Nathaniel, you have honoured your uniform, your Force and your country. Congratulations, and may this be the first of many more victories to come.”

World.title: SPECIAL REPORT: As climate change pushes fish into deeper waters, Nigerian coastal fishermen lose livelihoods
World.content:
Clouds hung heavily over the Atlantic coastline, a familiar sight at the peak of the rainy season in Nigeria’s Niger Delta. On this day in June, rain had been falling since morning, leaving the sandy pathways of Ikot Inua Eyet, a fishing community in Ibeno Local Government Area of Akwa Ibom State, slick with mud.

At their home, 52-year-old fisherman, Christian Inyang, helped his wife attend to customers at her small roadside food stall.

Moments later, as the drizzle became heavier, Mr Inyang looked toward the river that had sustained his family for decades.

He should have been on the water. Instead, like some fishermen across Nigeria’s southern coastline, he was stranded on land.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“There is a lot that has changed,” he began quietly.

“Our catch is no longer like before. If you don’t have a big boat with a powerful engine to go far into the sea, you won’t catch anything,” Mr Christian said.

For decades, the shallow creeks surrounding his community supplied enough fish to feed families and support local markets. Fishermen paddled wooden canoes into nearby waters and returned with nets overflowing with croaker, catfish and bonga.

Today, those waters have become increasingly empty. The fish, fishermen say, have moved farther offshore.

For Mr Inyang, many say it is “climate change”, but he understands well the changes affecting his source of livelihood.

“Some people came here and explained that it is climate change,” he said.

“I don’t know much about it, but what I know is that the fish have gone deeper into the ocean,” he added.

The situation has affected the livelihoods of many fishermen in the area, with some turning to other sources of income, especially when they cannot afford engines powerful enough to take them out to the open sea for a good catch.

Climate change threatens Nigeria’s coastal fisheries

Fishing has shaped life in coastal communities across Akwa Ibom, Bayelsa, Delta, Rivers and Cross River states for generations. Long before oil installations took the coastline, fishing was the primary source of income for thousands of households. Children inherited the trade from their parents, learning to paddle canoes before they could even ride bicycles.

Nigeria’s over 200 million people rely on the country’s fishing industry for much of their protein, making the sector a critical part of the economy.

Yet the sector is under growing pressure, arising from many challenges, including climate change.

According to the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC), rising ocean temperatures, changing rainfall patterns, ocean acidification and sea-level rise are altering marine ecosystems worldwide. Many fish species are moving into deeper or cooler waters as sea temperatures rise, making them harder for small-scale artisanal fishers to access.

The Food and Agriculture Organisation (FAO) has similarly warned that climate change is affecting fish distribution, breeding patterns and the productivity of coastal fisheries, particularly in developing countries where communities depend heavily on traditional fishing methods.

Nigeria ranks among the countries most vulnerable to climate change, with rising temperatures, erratic rainfall, coastal erosion, and flooding threatening livelihoods across the country — from the Niger Delta’s shrinking fish stocks to the Sahel’s advancing desertification. Millions, especially in farming and fishing communities, face growing food insecurity as a result.

On paper, the government has taken steps to respond. Nigeria submitted its third Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC 3.0) in September 2025, pledging a 32 per cent reduction in emissions by 2035 compared to 2018 levels and aiming to raise the share of renewable energy in electricity generation from 22 per cent to 52 per cent. The plan also targets net-zero emissions by 2060, backed by Nigeria’s 2023 Climate Change Act and Long-Term Low-Emissions Development Strategy.

However, implementation failures continue to undermine climate policies. Financing remains a major hurdle: Nigeria estimates it will need $337 billion between 2026 and 2035 to fully deliver on NDC 3.0, a sum far beyond current domestic and international commitments.

For fishing communities like those in Akwa Ibom and across the Niger Delta, this gap between policy ambition and action means the crisis remains largely unaddressed on the ground, leaving residents to adapt on their own, often without support.

In Nigeria’s Niger Delta, where artisanal fishers operate small wooden boats powered by paddles or low-horsepower engines, travelling farther offshore often requires equipment they cannot afford.

“If you don’t have a big boat with a powerful engine to go far into the sea, you won’t catch anything,” Christian said.

For fishermen like Mr Inyang, the changing climate is no longer an abstract scientific concept. It is measured by longer hours at sea, higher fuel costs, smaller catches, and the growing uncertainty of whether each fishing trip will provide enough to feed their families.

“Before, a fishing trip (one week) could bring me fish worth between N700,000 and N800,000. Now, we make about N150,000 or even less. When you remove the cost of fuel, paying workers and feeding the crew, what is left is very small.”

Fish production in Nigeria

According to WorldFish data, Nigeria produces around 1.2 million metric tonnes of fish annually, 90 per cent of which is consumed domestically. In 2025, the sector produced approximately 1.4 metric tonnes. Although that indicated growth, the federal government said production level remains below Nigeria’s annual consumption estimate of 3.6 million metric tonnes.

In February, the federal government raised the alarm over post-harvest losses of up to 30 per cent in Nigeria’s fish sector,

“Despite fish being one of the cheapest and most accessible sources of animal protein for Nigerian families, post-harvest losses of up to 30 per cent continue to undermine supply and affordability,” the Minister of Marine and Blue Economy, Adegboyega Oyetola, said.

Meanwhile, decades of inadequate government investment and regulation have affected the industry. Small-scale fishers, who form the backbone of the industry, struggle with outdated equipment, inadequate storage facilities, and limited access to credit and training in sustainable fishing practices.

According to Eyo Ambrose, a professor in the Department of Fisheries at the University of Uyo, climate change is worsening the challenges facing Nigeria’s fisheries, while the inability of local fishermen to operate in the high seas allows foreign vessels to exploit the country’s fish resources unchecked.

“Climate change is affecting our fisheries. Our local fishermen do not have the capacity to fish in the deep sea, so foreign vessels come with large trawlers, harvest the fish, and leave. There is little or no monitoring of their activities,” Mr Ambrose said.

Forced to abandon fishing

At Okorotip, another fishing community in the area, Aniedi Uwem said he has switched to crab harvesting.

“I have changed to crab catching,” Mr Uwem said. “The fish we used to catch in the shallow waters, where we could go with our hand-paddled canoe, have moved deep into the ocean. Only very few are left. If I go fishing now with my normal hand canoe, I usually come back with very little catch or sometimes nothing at all,” he added.

Aniefiok Edet, another fisherman, sees a spiritual connection in the development.

“In this area, we hardly see fish anymore. Instead, we hear that those who go farther into the deep sea are the ones making catches now. I don’t really know the cause, but I believe it is the will of God,” Mr Edet said.

These changes are one of the reasons fish prices keep increasing now. Fish catches are no longer enough like they used to be,” he said.

Market checks conducted by PREMIUM TIMES show that fish that used to sell at N10,000, now sells at N22,000. Quantity sold for N15,000 now sells for N25,000, and one stick of small tilapia fish that used to be N3,000 has more than doubled to N7,000 in the market.

The sea comes closer

While fish move further away, residents say the sea itself is gradually moving closer to their community. Many areas are now regularly submerged or washed away by the advancing shoreline.

Affiong Benjamin, a resident of Oborotip, pointed toward the ruins of homes damaged by water.

“The water now comes into our houses and carries away our fishing equipment. “,she added.

Many families have responded by piling sand and other materials around their homes in desperate attempts to keep floodwaters out.

Expensive adaptation

For those determined to remain fishermen, just like Mr Inyang, survival depends on larger boats and stronger engines, but those investments are beyond the reach of many.

The sharp increase in fuel prices in recent years has made longer fishing trips significantly more expensive. Each journey into deeper waters requires more petrol, more labour and greater financial risk. For small-scale fishermen, the economics no longer add up.

Despite the mounting challenges, the fishermen interviewed for this report said they have not received any government support specifically to address the effects of climate change on their livelihoods. However, they acknowledged that the government has provided other forms of assistance, including road infrastructure, electricity, and improved security.

While some hope for subsidised fishing equipment and other targeted interventions, many simply want the authorities to understand the scale of the problem before their communities lose a way of life that has sustained generations.

Effiong Akpan, one of the community leaders, said that climate change poses an existential threat to the community, saying parts of the settlement could disappear if the impacts continue unchecked.

“Some parts of this community are at risk of disappearing because of climate change,” Mr Akpan said.

“Fishing is our main source of livelihood because the land we would have used for farming has been taken over by water. If nothing is done, our community and our way of life will continue to be threatened,” Mr Akpan added.

Mr Inyang believes things can return to normal if the nearby water is dredged to deepen it. “There is too much sand now,” he explained.

“There used to be people dredging this river, but they stopped around 2018 or 2019. Since then, the river has not been deep enough for fish to survive here. If the dredging is carried out, things will be better, and fish will return to the nearby water where we can continue our work,” he added.

Expert intervenes

Brave Imiete, a marine policy analyst and director of Ocean Stewardship International in Port Harcourt, confirmed that climate change is impacting the ocean, affecting the relationships between species and their habitats.

According to Mr Imiete, there is a need for sustainable adaptation measures and greater investment in advanced marine research to understand the changes better and support the long-term health and resilience of Nigeria’s marine ecosystem.

“In the face of these challenges, it is expedient that we engage in collaborative efforts in making informed decisions to collectively adapt to these changes for the sustainability of fish stock,” he said.

“We must also lay emphasis on advanced research, innovations and adaptive management in securing the health of our oceans, preserving vital fish populations while protecting the livelihood of coastal communities,” Mr Imiete added.

This reporting was completed with the support of the Centre for Journalism Innovation and Development (CJID).

World.title: Gov Mbah honoured with transformational leadership award
World.content:
Enugu State Governor, Peter Ndubuisi Mbah‘s transformational leadership and developmental strides took centre stage again, as Enugu Media Village honoured him with an Award of Excellence for dedication to transformational leadership and outstanding governance.

This was even as the Chairman of Nsukka Local Government Area, Jude Asogwa, emerged winner of the 2025/2026 Enugu State Best Performing Local Government Chairman Award, while Isi-Uzo Council Chairman, Obiora Obeagu came second in the poll.

The awards were presented during the organisation’s 2025/2026 Best Performing Local Government Chairman Poll and Leadership Recognition Ceremony, which took place at the International Conference Centre, Enugu.

Enugu State Attorney General and Commissioner for Justice, Osinachi Nnajieze, receiving the award on behalf of Governor Peter Mbah

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Presenting the awards on behalf of the organisation, the Board of Trustees Chairman of Enugu Media Village and former Chairman of Agwu Local Government Area, Nnanna Nze, commended Governor Mbah for what he described as his remarkable transformation of the state in just three years.

Mr Nze noted that the governor’s developmental strides in critical sectors of the economy had continued to attract commendation from residents and stakeholders.

Earlier in his welcome address, state’s Attorney General and Commissioner for Justice, Osinachi Nnajieze, Mr Kelvin Uche Edeh, described the organisation as a media platform established to promote developmental governance and ensure that information about government projects reaches the grassroots. He noted that Governor Mbah had demonstrated that governance was a powerful tool for transforming communities and improving lives.

“Governor Peter Mbah has shown us that governance is about changing communities and transforming systems. We are committed to supporting developmental governance by ensuring that information reaches the grassroots across all local government areas,” Edeh said.

Receiving the award, Governor Mbah said the honour belonged to members of his team and the entire people of Enugu State for entrusting their mandate to him.

He, however, said that the people of Enugu State had only seen a tip of the iceberg, as he remained committed to exceeding expectations in delivering more dividends of democracy to the people.

Mr Mbah, who was represented by the state’s Attorney General and Commissioner for Justice, Osinachi Nnajieze, said the people of Enugu State deserved only the very best, hence his insistence on excellence, innovation and high performance from members of his administration.

Another major highlight of the event was the emergence of Jude Asogwa, as winner of the 2025/2026 Enugu State Best Performing Local Government Chairman Award.

The poll, which featured all 17 local government areas of the state, recorded Nsukka Local Government Area as the overall winner with 110,447 votes, ahead of Isi Uzo, Uzo Uwani, Igbo Eze North and Enugu South LGAs, in that order.

In his acceptance speech, Mr Asogwa, who dedicated the award to God, Governor Mbah, his family and the people of Nsukka, said the recognition reflected his Council’s commitment to delivering development to all 52 communities in the LGA.

He further reaffirmed Nsukka’s support for Governor Mbah’s re-election, citing the administration’s investments in the area such as 20 Smart Green Schools, 21 Type-2 Primary Healthcare Centres, dualization of the over 44.1-kilometre Enugu – Opi – Nsukka Road, the 52.2km Nguru – Lejja – Aku – Akpakume Nze – Egede – Affa – Eke road, and N1 billion oxygen plant, among other development projects designed to improve lives and grow Nsukka and Enugu North Zone’s economy.

“Let me just tell us that the secret of our performance is Dr Peter Ndubuisi Mbah. He is a leader that supports the local government council chairmen. He is a governor who does not tamper with the allocations of the LGAs. That is the secret of the results you are seeing. In addition, he has delivered 267 Smart Schools and 260 Type 2 Primary Healthcare Centres in the 260 wards.

“So, Nsukka is for Governor Peter Mbah. Also, we had earlier decided as a zone that come 2027, we will support and deliver not only the governor but also President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, whose administration has contributed to the growth and development of our people, including the appointment of the first indigenous Vice Chancellor of the University of Nigeria, Nsukka,” he said.

The event also featured the presentation of Awards of Excellence to distinguished public office holders and leaders in recognition of their contributions to governance, leadership and public service.

Among the awardees were Senator Osita Ngwu, representing Enugu West Senatorial District; Senator Ikeje Asogwa, representing Enugu North Senatorial District; Hon Chimaobi Sam Atu, representing Enugu North and South Federal Constituency; Osinachi Nnajieze, Attorney General and Commissioner for Justice; and Chie Chukwudi Nnaji.

World.title: Article of Faith: The blind servant of God (1), By Femi Aribisala
World.content:
The Bible reads us.

I asked a question during a Bible Study, “What will happen to the great men of the earth?” Nobody answered.

Then I said the great men are all in trouble. God is going to deal very harshly with them. I then quoted some scriptures:

“The Lord of hosts has purposed it, to bring to dishonour the pride of all glory, to bring into contempt all the honourable of the earth.” (Isaiah 23:9).

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

“It shall come to pass in that day that the Lord will punish on high the host of exalted ones, and on the earth the kings of the earth.” (Isaiah 24:21).

“(God will) execute vengeance on the nations, and punishments on the peoples; to bind their kings with chains, and their nobles with fetters of iron.” (Psalm 149:7-8).

Let me add another question, “What will happen to the rich men?” They will become poor. James says

“Come now, you rich, weep and howl for your miseries that are coming upon you! Your riches are corrupted, and your garments are moth-eaten. Your gold and silver are corroded, and their corrosion will be a witness against you and will eat your flesh like fire. You have heaped up treasure in the last days. Indeed the wages of the labourers who mowed your fields, which you kept back by fraud, cry out; and the cries of the reapers have reached the ears of the Lord of Sabaoth. You have lived on the earth in pleasure and luxury; you have fattened your hearts as in a day of slaughter. You have condemned, you have murdered the just; he does not resist you.” (James 5:1-6).

But the poor will become rich.

“The Lord makes poor and makes rich; He brings low and lifts up. He raises the poor from the dust and lifts the beggar from the ash heap, to set them among princes and make them inherit the throne of glory.” (1 Samuel 2:7-8).

“And all the trees of the field shall know that I, the Lord, have brought down the high tree and exalted the low tree, dried up the green tree and made the dry tree flourish; I, the Lord, have spoken and have done it.” (Ezekiel 17:24).

This was a bit confusing for some. A lady sought refuge in Moses. Moses says:

“You shall remember the Lord your God, for it is He who gives you power to get wealth, that He may establish His covenant which He swore to your fathers.” (Deuteronomy 8:18).

She said. “If it is God who gives the power to get wealth, how can the rich be in trouble?”

Covenant Wealth

In the first place, the wealth that Moses is talking about here is different from the wealth that the lady was thinking about. The wealth Moses is talking about is one designed to establish God’s covenant. That is different from the wealth of a classic rich man.

With the rich, God says:

“I will change their glory into shame.” (Hosea 4:7).

Jesus even declared a devastating principle:

“What is highly esteemed among men is an abomination in the sight of God.” (Luke 16:15).

Think of anything that man esteems: wealth, fame, power, position, background, education, wisdom, etcetera; they are all abominations to God.

Listen carefully: We send our children to school to get what is an abomination to God.

“Clarus: What would you like to be when you grow up?”

“I want to be an Engineer.”

Wrong answer. Say instead, “I want to be a friend of God.”

“Gringory: “Why are you studying the sciences in university?”

“I want to grow in the knowledge of the sciences.”

Wrong answer. Say instead, “I want to grow in the knowledge of God.”

Paul says:

“What things were gain to me, these I have counted loss for Christ. Yet indeed I also count all things loss for the excellence of the knowledge of Christ Jesus my Lord, for whom I have suffered the loss of all things, and count them as rubbish, that I may gain Christ.” (Philippians 3:7-8).

The Good Might Be Bad

The fact that God gives something to you does not mean what He gives is good for you. God also gives bad things. He gives diseases, and that is bad.

“The Lord will strike you with the boils of Egypt, with tumors, with the scab, and with the itch, from which you cannot be healed. The Lord will strike you with madness and blindness and confusion of heart.” (Deuteronomy 28:27-28).

He also gives us things we consider bad that are actually good for us.

God sent Moses to Pharaoh to secure the release of the Israelites from Egypt. Moses did not want to go:

“Moses said to the Lord, “O Lord, I have never been eloquent, neither in the past nor since you have spoken to your servant. I am slow of speech and tongue.” The Lord said to him, “Who gave man his mouth? Who makes him deaf or mute? Who gives him sight or makes him blind? Is it not I, the Lord?” (Exodus 4:10-12).

God says if a man is blind, He is the one who makes him blind. But why? Why does God make us blind?

Read Matthew 13:13-16

I was a new believer; I had just met the Lord. Jesus stooped beside me while I was sleeping and shouted in my left ear, “Matthew 13:13-16.”

What does it say:

“Therefore I speak to them in parables, because seeing they do not see, and hearing they do not hear, nor do they understand. And in them the prophecy of Isaiah is fulfilled, which says: ‘Hearing you will hear and shall not understand, and seeing you will see and not perceive. For the hearts of this people have grown dull. Their ears are hard of hearing, and their eyes they have closed, lest they should see with their eyes and hear with their ears, lest they should understand with their hearts and turn, so that I should heal them.’ But blessed are your eyes for they see, and your ears for they hear.” (Matthew 13:13-16).

I thank God for opening my eyes and ears 33 years ago. He did not tell me to read verse 17, but I read it anyway. It says:

“Assuredly, I say to you that many prophets and righteous men desired to see what you see, and did not see it, and to hear what you hear, and did not hear it.” (Matthew 13:17).

This says that many prophets and righteous men do not see what I see and do not hear what I hear. Why not? That is kingdom dynamics. God says:

“Who is blind but My servant, or deaf as My messenger whom I send? Who is blind as he who is perfect, and blind as the Lord’s servant? Seeing many things, but you do not observe; opening the ears, but he does not hear.” (Isaiah 42:19-20).

But why are the servants of God blind? Why are the messengers of God blind? Why is the perfect man blind?

The Bible Reads Us

We read the Bible, but it is important to realise that the Bible also reads us.

“For the word of God is living and powerful, and sharper than any two-edged sword, piercing even to the division of soul and spirit, and of joints and marrow, and is a discerner of the thoughts and intents of the heart. And there is no creature hidden from His sight, but all things are naked and open to the eyes of Him to whom we must give account.” (Hebrews 4:12-13).

So, James counsels:

“Be doers of the word, and not hearers only, deceiving yourselves. For if anyone is a hearer of the word and not a doer, he is like a man observing his natural face in a mirror; for he observes himself, goes away, and immediately forgets what kind of man he was. But he who looks into the perfect law of liberty and continues in it, and is not a forgetful hearer but a doer of the work, this one will be blessed in what he does.” (James 1:22-25).

The Bible is not just a collection of stories about what happened to some people in the past. The Bible, especially the New Testament, is a collection of stories about us. Every act of Jesus is directed at us.

We are the lepers that Jesus cleansed. We are the sick that He healed. We are the woman with the issue of blood whose faith healed her. We are Blind Bartimaeus, whose eyes Jesus opened. We are the deaf whose ears He opened. We are the dumb whom He enabled to talk. We are the paralysed who He enabled to walk.

Therefore, Paul says:

“All Scripture is given by inspiration of God, and is profitable for doctrine, for reproof, for correction, for instruction in righteousness, that the man of God may be complete, thoroughly equipped for every good work.” (2 Timothy 3:16-17).

Born Blind

God made two types of ears that can hear, and two different types of eyes that can see. Solomon says:

“The hearing ear and the seeing eye, the Lord has made them both.” (Proverbs 20:12).

The inferior eye and ear are the ones that all men have. The superior ones are exclusive. You have to ask God for them. That is why it is not a good idea to concentrate on asking God for provision, school fees, and house rent. There are many more important things to fast and pray for.

Solomon says:

“Wisdom is the principal thing; therefore get wisdom. And in all your getting, get understanding.” (Proverbs 4:7).

James also counsels:

“If any of you lacks wisdom, let him ask of God, who gives to all liberally and without reproach, and it will be given to him. But let him ask in faith, with no doubting, for he who doubts is like a wave of the sea driven and tossed by the wind. For let not that man suppose that he will receive anything from the Lord; he is a double-minded man, unstable in all his ways.” (James 1:4-8).

World.title: 2Baba, Annie Idibia follow each other on Instagram amid alleged fallout with Natasha
World.content:
Nigerian singer Innocent “2Baba” Idibia and his estranged wife, actress Annie Macaulay, have followed each other again on Instagram, fuelling reactions amid reports of tension between the singer and his partner, Natasha Osawaru, a member of the Edo State House of Assembly.

PREMIUM TIMES earlier reported that 2Baba and Annie unfollowed each other on social media days after the “African Queen” hitmaker announced their separation in January 2025.

In July, rumours that the former couple had reconciled trended on social media after a video purportedly showing them together surfaced online. They, however, dismissed the speculation, saying the footage was old.

Checks by this newspaper on Sunday showed that 2Baba and Annie now follow each other on Instagram.

Further checks showed that the singer no longer follows his partner on the platform. The development comes amid reports of an altercation involving the couple outside a nightclub in Abuja on Friday.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

Neither the renewed Instagram connection between 2Baba and Annie nor his decision to unfollow Ms Osawaru establishes the state of either relationship.

Altercation

The reported incident occurred during the opening of the “90s Lounge” in Abuja and has since generated reactions on social media. A viral video obtained by this newspaper and widely circulated online purportedly showed moments from the incident.

However, the footage does not show the events that allegedly triggered the confrontation or establish the circumstances surrounding it.

An X user identified as King, who claimed to have witnessed the incident, alleged that Ms Osawaru arrived at the venue with some men and waited for 2Baba.

He claimed that when the singer arrived, Ms Osawaru approached his vehicle and demanded to speak with him, causing a commotion outside the venue.

The video posted by King, however, does not show the alleged confrontation between Ms Osawaru and 2Baba.

He further alleged that the singer eventually took Ms Osawaru inside the venue to prevent the situation from escalating.

“Allegedly, 2Face and his latest wife, Natasha, haven’t been on good terms for months, and she hasn’t even been able to see him. She reportedly heard that the owner of Trukadero was opening a club called 90’s yesterday, so she went there and waited for 2Face.

“When he finally arrived, she rushed to his car and started making a scene, saying she wanted to see her husband and talk to him,” he wrote.

Neither 2Baba nor Ms Osawaru has publicly addressed the account of what allegedly transpired at the venue.

Previous controversies

The latest speculation follows previous controversies involving 2Baba and Ms Osawaru since their relationship became public in 2025.

Ms Osawaru publicly referred to the singer as her husband in May 2025, months after he announced his separation from Annie and subsequently proposed to the Edo lawmaker. The couple later held a traditional wedding.

They later made headlines following a clash during an Instagram Live session hosted by media personality Daddy Freeze.

2Baba and his partner also attracted public attention following reports of an altercation in the United Kingdom that allegedly led to the singer’s arrest.

In another controversy, 2Baba publicly apologised to Ms Osawaru after saying during an interview that “men are not built for one woman.”

The latest developments have renewed speculation about both his marriage to Ms Osawaru and his relationship with Annie. However, none of the parties has publicly linked 2Baba and Annie’s decision to follow each other again to the reported problems in his marriage.

World.title: Niger records 124 diphtheria cases, 17 deaths — Commissioner
World.content:
The Niger State Government has confirmed 17 deaths from diphtheria out of 124 cases recorded in three local government areas within the last seven months.

The Commissioner for Health, Murtala Bagana, disclosed this on Friday while presenting an overview of the state’s health sector at the Second Quarter Press Parley organised by the state Ministry of Information and Orientation in Minna.

Mr Bagana said 103 patients had been treated and discharged, while 17 deaths were recorded in Bida, Suleja and Shiroro local government areas.

He added that three new cases were recently identified, with one patient currently receiving treatment.

Stay Ahead with Premium Times 

The commissioner said the government was strengthening disease surveillance, case management, immunisation and public awareness to contain the spread of diphtheria.

He urged parents and caregivers to ensure that children received all recommended vaccines, stressing that routine immunisation remained critical to preventing diphtheria, measles and other vaccine-preventable diseases.

100 PHCs for completion

Mr Bagana also disclosed that the state government was targeting the completion and operationalisation of 100 out of the 274 Tier-Two Primary Healthcare Centres (PHCs) being upgraded across the state by the end of 2026.

He said the ongoing PHC upgrade was part of the government’s efforts to strengthen primary healthcare delivery and improve access to quality healthcare services, particularly in underserved communities.

According to him, the administration of Governor Mohammed Bago had continued to prioritise investment in the health sector through infrastructure development, partnerships with development partners and timely payment of counterpart funds.

The commissioner said the government was also providing several free healthcare interventions to reduce the financial burden of treatment on residents.

He said accident victims were entitled to free treatment within the first 24 hours of presentation at designated health facilities, while victims of snake bites would also receive free treatment within the same period.

He added that Caesarean Section operations were being provided free of charge at five designated centres across the state.

Vaccines, he said, were also available free of charge at all primary healthcare centres, urging parents and caregivers to ensure that their children received the recommended vaccines.

Mr Bagana said the Ministry of Health was working towards enforcing relevant provisions of the Child Rights Act and other applicable regulations to ensure that children had access to routine immunisation.

IBBU medical students’ clinical training

On clinical training for medical students of Ibrahim Badamasi Babangida University (IBBU), Lapai, Mr Bagana assured students and parents that arrangements were being made to provide clinical training facilities in Minna within the next six months to one year.

He explained that the arrangement became necessary following delays in the construction of the permanent IBBU University Teaching Hospital in Minna.

According to him, disagreements with the contractor handling the project affected its progress, but the issues had now been resolved.

“In view of that, we have lost some mileage, as there was some disagreement along the way. But finally, we are at the point where the contract would be re-awarded to another contractor who would take us to completion,” he said.

Mr Bagana said the government would not wait for the completion of the permanent teaching hospital before commencing clinical training for subsequent batches of medical students.

He said the permanent facility was projected to be completed within 18 months to two years, while interim arrangements were being made to enable students to undertake their clinical training in Minna.

“We are not waiting for the teaching hospital to be completed before we start training our students. Since the timeline for the completion of the hospital is now between 18 months and two years, in the next six months to one year, we will have our facilities ready for them,” he said.

The commissioner said Minna General Hospital was undergoing rehabilitation and would serve as a temporary clinical training facility for students of the IBBU College of Medicine.

He added that the government was also working with a contractor to establish a laboratory medicine facility at the IBB Specialist Hospital, while the IBBU Guest House in Minna would provide accommodation for the students.

Mr Bagana recalled that the first batch of 41 medical students had moved to Zaria for clinical training pending the availability of suitable facilities in Niger State.

He said the interim arrangement would enable subsequent batches of students to undertake their clinical training in Minna while the government pursued completion of the permanent teaching hospital.

Measles cases

Also speaking at the press parley, an official, Samuel Jiya, said Niger State had recorded a decline in measles infections, with 31 cases reported this year.

He said nine of the cases tested positive and were treated, while two deaths were recorded.

The officials also disclosed that the present administration had engaged no fewer than 20 consultant doctors as part of efforts to address manpower shortages and strengthen healthcare delivery in the state.

Mr Bagana further disclosed that the state had secured malaria drugs worth N2.5 billion through partnerships with development partners.

He said the government had also recently conducted a free medical outreach targeting 1.5 million people.

According to him, the outreach provided free cataract operations, 1,500 pairs of eyeglasses and 500 walking sticks to beneficiaries.

He said similar interventions would be sustained in the state.

On HIV/AIDS, the commissioner said the prevalence rate in Niger remained below one per cent, adding that the government was taking measures to sustain and strengthen its partnership with the Global Fund.

Mr Bagana attributed the improvements recorded in the state’s health sector to the commitment of Governor Bago and collaboration with development partners.

He commended the state government for creating an enabling environment for effective healthcare delivery and urged the media to continue supporting the Ministry of Health through public health advocacy and sensitisation, particularly on routine immunisation and the prevention of vaccine-preventable diseases.

World.title: OPHK air strikes neutralized scores of terrorists fighters in Borno
World.content:
By Ndahi Marama, Maiduguri

Recent air strikes conducted by the Nigerian Military have reportedly dealt a major blow to the Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP) in the Sambisa Forest, with nine fighters, including a prominent commander responsible for escorting senior terrorists, neutralised. Sources have said.

The strikes, conducted on Saturday, Aug. 8, around the Yuwe and Sabil Huda enclaves in the Sambisa Forest, were described by intelligence sources as highly effective.

According to fresh intelligence obtained by Vanguard, which was corroborated by Zagazola Makama, a Security Analyst and Counter Insurgency Expert, one of those neutralised was Qaid Abu Khalid Al Muhajir, an ISWAP commander originally from Maiduguri metropolis.

Intelligence sources identified Abu Khalid as a specialist responsible for providing escorts and coordinating the movement of senior ISWAP commanders and other high-value members of the terrorist group.

He was reportedly highly familiar with navigation routes and tactical movements connecting major ISWAP enclaves, particularly routes used to move senior commanders and special convoys.

His role reportedly made him an important facilitator of mobility within the terrorist group’s network, enabling senior members to move between enclaves while reducing the risk of interception by security forces.

The intelligence report indicated that nine ISWAP fighters were neutralised during the air strikes, while several others sustained varying degrees of injuries.

Sources said the casualties included terrorist elements linked to the group involved in the ambush of Nigerian troops along the Bita–Yamtage axis in Gwoza Local Government Area.

The latest intelligence suggests that the air strikes may have disrupted a wider network of fighters involved in terrorist operations across the Sambisa Forest and the Gwoza axis.

The neutralisation of Abu Khalid is considered significant because of his reported knowledge of the terrain, routes and movement patterns used by ISWAP commanders and special convoys.

His loss could therefore affect the group’s ability to move senior operatives between its various enclaves, particularly in areas where security forces have intensified surveillance and kinetic operations.

Security sources said the latest strikes would be followed by continued intelligence exploitation and surveillance to assess the extent of the damage and identify surviving members of the affected groups.

The development comes amid intensified military operations aimed at dismantling terrorist command structures, disrupting logistics and denying ISWAP and Boko Haram elements freedom of movement across Borno State.

The Nigerian Army and the Air Component are expected to sustain their intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance missions in support of ground troops operating across the Sambisa Forest, Gwoza and adjoining areas.

The military has also continued to place emphasis on precision targeting to disrupt terrorist leadership and specialised networks while supporting ongoing ground operations in the theatre. End

World.title: Tinubu urges religious leaders to confront extremism, misuse of faith
World.content:
By Omeiza Ajayi

ABUJA: President Bola Tinubu has called on religious and spiritual leaders to consistently raise their voices against terrorism, kidnapping, banditry and the misuse of religion to justify violence and cruelty, stressing that no genuine service to God can be advanced through the destruction of innocent human lives.

The President made the call on Sunday in Kano in a goodwill message delivered on his behalf by the Secretary to the Government of the Federation SGF, Senator George Akume, at the Grand Maulud of Sheikh Ahmad Al-Tijani, RTA.

Addressing the World Khalifa of the Tijjaniyya Order, scholars, spiritual leaders and adherents from Nigeria and other countries, Tinubu said religious leaders have an important responsibility in confronting violence, extremism and the manipulation of faith for destructive purposes.

“Your voices must be raised consistently against the murder of innocent people, against terrorism, kidnapping, banditry and the misuse of religion to justify cruelty. Your institutions and networks must become stronger in the advocacy for peace education, religious literacy, scholarship and the formation of upright young men and women.

“You must also remind political leaders of justice, responsibility and compassion, while reminding citizens that legitimate grievances must never become permission for lawlessness or violence. Above all, our spiritual fathers must continue to teach that no genuine service to Allah is advanced by destroying the innocent human life that Allah has made sacred,” the President said.

He also urged religious institutions and networks to strengthen their advocacy for peace education, religious literacy, scholarship and the moral formation of young people, while using their influence to promote justice, responsibility, compassion and peaceful resolution of grievances.

Tinubu observed that the gathering was taking place at a consequential moment in human history, with societies across the world confronted by conflicts, uncertainty, climate shocks, food and energy shocks, violent extremism, terrorism, transnational crimes and the increasingly dangerous manipulation of identity and religion.

Citing a United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees UNHCR report, he noted that 117.8 million people were forcibly displaced worldwide at the end of 2025, stressing that the scale of global challenges makes the intervention of spiritual leaders increasingly indispensable.

According to him, spiritual leaders “guard the frontiers of conscience” through their capacity to heal wounds, resolve grievances and dissolve deep-seated hatred and bitterness.

He said the Tijjaniyya community, with its extensive spiritual networks across West Africa, North Africa and beyond, possesses relationships and moral capital that could be deployed for reconciliation, countering violent extremism, youth guidance and humanitarian solidarity across the Sahel, West Africa and the wider world.

The President said the Federal Government recognises the critical roles of religious and traditional leaders in deepening tolerance, countering misinformation and identity-based division, strengthening grassroots peacebuilding and promoting peaceful coexistence.

He reaffirmed Nigeria’s commitment to regional cooperation, counter-terrorism, maritime security, economic integration and dialogue, noting that the country’s strategic location at the intersection of West Africa, the Sahel, Lake Chad Basin, Gulf of Guinea and the wider Atlantic world makes its peace and stability consequential to the wider region.

“It also means that religious communities with deep transnational connections, such as the Tijjaniyya, can be valuable partners in building an architecture of social peace that complements the work of governments and regional institutions,” he said.

Tinubu explained that such partnership should mobilise the ethical resources of religion, including truthfulness, compassion, justice, restraint, service and the sanctity of human life, for the common good.

He described Nigeria’s extraordinary diversity and plurality as among the country’s greatest strengths, assuring that the Federal Government would continue to uphold Nigerians’ freedom to practise their faith while strengthening collaboration with religious and traditional institutions to promote peace, mutual respect and national cohesion.

The President also welcomed the World Khalifa of the Tijjaniyya Order, scholars, spiritual leaders and other guests who travelled from Algeria, Morocco, Senegal, Egypt and other countries for the Maulud, describing Nigeria as a country where the Tijjaniyya tradition has established deep roots in scholarship, remembrance, service, moral instruction and peaceful community life.

He recalled recently receiving a high-level delegation of the Supreme Council of Tijjaniyya at the State House, Abuja, where prayers were offered for the peace, unity and prosperity of Nigeria as well as the enduring relationship between Nigeria and Algeria.

Tinubu also paid tributes to the late Sheikh Dahiru Usman Bauchi, whose foundation played a significant role in organising the Maulud, describing him as one of the towering figures whose absence was deeply felt at the gathering.

He recalled describing the late Islamic scholar, following his death in November 2025, as “a teacher, a father and a voice of moderation and reason, and as an advocate of peace and piety.”

According to him, the most enduring monument that could be built in his honour would be the preservation of his legacy of Qur’anic scholarship, moral instruction, devotion to Allah, respect for learning, peaceful coexistence and concern for the wellbeing of society.

World.title: Sokoto Teenager’s Death: Family demands justice, prosecution of suspects
World.content:
By Musa Ubandawaki, Sokoto

SOKOTO — The family of 15-year-old Fadimatu Abubakar Gizo, who allegedly died after being sexually assaulted in Yarume Mai Hako village, Wamakko Local Government Area of Sokoto State, has appealed to the authorities to ensure justice for the deceased.

The family also called for a thorough investigation and prosecution of the suspects currently in police custody if found culpable.

Fadimatu was reportedly attacked while she and other girls were gathering firewood in a nearby forest. She subsequently died following the alleged assault.

The incident has thrown the community into mourning, with the teenager’s parents and residents calling for a comprehensive investigation into the circumstances surrounding her death.

Fadimatu’s father, who spoke amid grief, appealed to the Federal and Sokoto State governments, the Nigeria Police Force, the National Human Rights Commission and other relevant authorities to ensure that the matter was thoroughly investigated.

“We are deeply bereaved and emotionally devastated by the death of our daughter.

“We want all the suspects arrested and currently being detained to face justice. We appeal to the authorities to come to our aid and ensure that whoever is responsible for the death of our daughter does not escape justice,” he said.

The victim’s mother, Malama Yar Buga, also called for a transparent investigation into the circumstances surrounding her daughter’s death.

She urged the authorities to prosecute anyone found to have committed an offence.

“We cannot understand how the life of our daughter could end this way. She had a future ahead of her, and preparations were being made for her marriage,” she said.

The Ward Head of Yarume Mai Hako, Alhaji Abubakar Yarume, described the incident as devastating and called for a comprehensive investigation to establish what happened.

He said the community would continue to seek justice for the deceased.

“We will not rest until justice is served. Fadimatu was an honest, disciplined and humble girl, and her life was cut short,” the traditional leader said.

Two friends of the deceased, Khadijah Buba and Faiza Bello, were also said to have provided information to investigators concerning the incident.

Meanwhile, the Sokoto State Police Command confirmed the arrest of suspects in connection with the case.

The Command’s spokesperson, DSP Ahmed Rufai, said the suspects were being detained at the State Criminal Investigation Department, CID, while investigation continued.

Rufai assured that the command would conduct a thorough investigation to establish the circumstances surrounding the teenager’s death.

The incident has renewed calls for stronger protection of children and other vulnerable persons, as well as effective investigation and prosecution of suspected perpetrators of sexual and violent crimes where evidence establishes criminal responsibility.

World.title: PANDEF hails Tinubu over 15-year gas supply deal for UTM FLNG
World.content:
By Henry Umoru

ABUJA — The Pan Niger Delta Forum, PANDEF, has commended President Bola Tinubu for approving a 15-year gas supply framework for UTM Offshore Limited to facilitate the construction of Nigeria’s first Floating Liquefied Natural Gas, FLNG, facility.

UTM Offshore Limited is an indigenous company operating in the Niger Delta.

In a statement on Sunday, National Chairman of PANDEF, Ambassador Godknows Igali, described the approval as significant to ongoing efforts to accelerate industrialisation and economic development in the Niger Delta.

The statement, titled, “Appreciation for granting of 15 years Gas Supply to UTM Offshore Limited for the purpose of building Nigeria’s first Floating LNG,” said the multi-billion-dollar project, proposed for offshore Akwa Ibom State, would contribute to economic activities in the Niger Delta and the country.

Igali said, “PANDEF considers your approval of this gas supply momentous as it will add significantly to the efforts which are at different levels to bring about the rapid industrialisation of the Niger Delta.

“In this case, the multi-billion-dollar construction of this floating LNG which is intended to be located offshore Akwa Ibom State will engender rapid economic development in the whole Niger Delta and Nigeria at large.”

He said the project would also contribute to the development of Nigeria’s gas industry, particularly through greater participation by indigenous companies.

Igali noted that the project, alongside other investments in the sector, could contribute to the development of a gas-based economy.

He also commended UTM Offshore Limited and its Managing Director, Dr Julius Rone, describing the project as an encouragement to other indigenous entrepreneurs to invest in the development and utilisation of Nigeria’s gas resources.

According to him, the construction phase of the project could generate employment opportunities and stimulate other economic activities in the region.

Igali said PANDEF also expected the project to contribute to improved access to gas and efforts to address gas flaring and its environmental impact in the Niger Delta.

He said, “Even at the social level, we are hopeful that this project and many like it which will come in the future will help to raise the standard of living of people of the area, by stemming the tide of skyrocketing domestic and industrial gas prices.

“At another level, this will also help to combat the scourge of gas flaring which has for many decades contributed to pollution in the area.”

The PANDEF chairman urged the Federal Government to continue providing the necessary support to enable the project team to meet its implementation timelines.

Igali also assured the President of PANDEF’s support for the project, particularly in mobilising stakeholders in the Niger Delta to create a conducive environment for its implementation.

“On our part, we take the opportunity to assure Mr President that PANDEF will be at the fulcrum in galvanising support of the people of the Niger Delta, in particular our people in Akwa Ibom State, to ensure that the right environment exists locally for the take-off of the project and throughout its lifespan,” he said.

World.title: Obasanjo’s allegations against Atiku will collapse, says aide
World.content:
ABUJA — Media Adviser to former Vice President Atiku Abubakar, Paul Ibe, has accused former President Olusegun Obasanjo of using political allegations against his former deputy for electoral purposes, saying the claims would not withstand scrutiny.

Ibe made the allegations in a statement posted on his Facebook account on Sunday, titled, “Obasanjo’s campaign of lies, political manipulation and orchestrated deceit falling apart like a pack of cards.”

He was reacting to comments attributed to Obasanjo alleging that Atiku had mobilised the late former Speaker of the House of Representatives, Ghali Umar Na’Abba, to initiate moves to impeach him during their time in office between 1999 and 2007.

Ibe described the allegation as baseless and accused Obasanjo of revisiting allegations against Atiku during election periods.

He argued that Na’Abba, who died in 2023, could no longer respond to the claim.

However, Ibe cited former member of the House of Representatives, Abubakar Bawa Bwari, who served as Chief Whip during the period, as disputing Obasanjo’s account.

According to Ibe, Bwari had said Na’Abba did not seek Obasanjo’s removal and that Atiku acted as an emissary to lawmakers on behalf of the former President.

Ibe also disputed accounts concerning the 2003 presidential nomination process within the Peoples Democratic Party, PDP.

He cited former Abia State Governor, Senator Orji Kalu, who, in a video referenced by Ibe, said Atiku knelt before PDP governors to seek their support for Obasanjo’s re-election.

Ibe quoted Kalu as saying that Atiku had told the governors he did not want to betray Obasanjo, despite moves by some PDP governors at the time to support Atiku for the presidency.

The aide also revisited the controversy surrounding the Petroleum Technology Development Fund, PTDF, in the build-up to the 2007 general elections.

He said Atiku had submitted himself to investigation over allegations relating to the fund after temporarily relinquishing his immunity, insisting that the allegations were politically motivated because of his opposition to Obasanjo’s reported Third Term bid.

The statement was signed by Ibe as Media Adviser to Atiku Abubakar, presidential candidate of the ADC and former Vice President of Nigeria.

World.title: Photos: Messi arrives Argentina to bid farewell to father Jorge
World.content:
Argentine football star Lionel Messi (L) and his wife Antonela Roccuzzo arrive at the Islas Malvinas International Airport after the death of his father Jorge Messi in Rosario, Santa Fe province, Argentina on August 8, 2026. Jorge Messi, the father and agent of Lionel Messi, has died aged 68, the eight-time Ballon d’Or winner’s childhood club Newell’s Old Boys announced on August 8, 2026. (Photo by Luis ROBAYO / AFP)

Argentina football icon Lionel Messi bid farewell Sunday to his father, the global star’s emotional anchor and agent since childhood who passed away following a battle with cancer aged 68.

The eight-time Ballon d’Or winner touched down on a private flight from Miami late on Saturday with his wife Antonela Roccuzzo and their children and has remained surrounded by his close family since.

A private ceremony with a few teammates from the Argentine national squad is scheduled to take place at a cemetery in the town of Perez, adjacent to Rosario, later Sunday.

The gates of the town’s El Prado cemetery displayed handwritten messages from fans — “Stay strong, Leo, we love you” and “Stay strong, Messi family” — alongside a large floral wreath.

Messi’s teammates rallied around their captain following the announcement that Jorge Messi had passed away late Friday at a clinic in Rosario.

Argentine football star Lionel Messi (L) and his wife Antonela Roccuzzo arrive at the Islas Malvinas International Airport after the death of his father Jorge Messi in Rosario, Santa Fe province, Argentina on August 8, 2026. Jorge Messi, the father and agent of Lionel Messi, has died aged 68, the eight-time Ballon d’Or winner’s childhood club Newell’s Old Boys announced on August 8, 2026. (Photo by Luis ROBAYO / AFP)

“It will surely do him good for us to be there,” Boca Juniors midfielder Leandro Paredes told journalists after his team’s match on Saturday.

“I need to speak with a few of my teammates to see if we go now or sometime tomorrow.”

According to some media outlets midfielder Rodrigo de Paul — a close friend of Messi and his Inter Miami teammate — would travel to Argentina.

After scoring a goal in a 2-1 defeat to Monterrey in Miami on Saturday, De Paul paid tribute to his friend by taking off his shirt to reveal Messi’s number 10 jersey.

Argentine football star Lionel Messi arrives at the Islas Malvinas International Airport after the death of his father Jorge Messi in Rosario, Santa Fe province, Argentina on August 8, 2026. Jorge Messi, the father and agent of Lionel Messi, has died aged 68, the eight-time Ballon d’Or winner’s childhood club Newell’s Old Boys announced on August 8, 2026. (Photo by Luis ROBAYO / AFP)

The cause of death was not disclosed, but local media reported that Jorge Messi had been suffering from cancer.

His unusual absence from the World Cup in June had already attracted attention.

Messi’s family asked the media for “humanity” during the tournament amid persistent rumours over Jorge’s health.

After bursting into tears after scoring against Algeria, 39-year-old Messi had admitted to dealing with “a situation outside of sports”.

“I went through a few difficult, complicated days,” he later acknowledged, “but I am grateful to the entire delegation and my teammates, because they stood by me, as always.”

Immediately after the World Cup final defeat against Spain, Messi returned to spend a few days with his family in Rosario.

– Humble beginnings –

A guiding figure throughout his son’s career, Jorge Messi was his first coach who left everything behind to accompany his son to Spain.

A metalworker in Rosario, 340 km north of Buenos Aires, Jorge managed youth teams at the small local club Grandoli.

He was the one who introduced Argentina’s future captain to the game aged four on vacant lots where local kids played.

His life changed course in 2000 when Barcelona invited the young prodigy, then aged 13, to Catalonia to continue treatment for a growth hormone deficiency while playing for the club’s youth teams.

Jorge left behind his job in Argentina, his wife, and his three other children to settle in Spain with Lionel.

“When we arrived in Barcelona, I used to lock myself in my room to cry alone, and my father did the same — either without me seeing him or thinking I didn’t see him. We pretended we were both fine, but we were struggling,” Messi later said.

His father was later the agent who negotiated astronomical contracts on his behalf, from Barcelona to Paris Saint-Germain and Inter Miami.

Messages of sympathy have poured in since Saturday from the football world, including from the clubs Messi played for and the Spanish Football Federation.

The Argentine Football Association (AFA) ordered a minute of silence before matches and that black armbands be worn at games across all age groups for the week.

World.title: Why Igbo youths shun military service, says Intersociety
World.content:
By Jeff Agbodo

ENUGU — The International Society for Civil Liberties and Rule of Law, Intersociety, has attributed what it described as the reluctance of some Igbo youths to enlist in the Nigerian military to concerns over the alleged disappearance of young people in the South-East.

Intersociety, in a report jointly released with the United States-based Ekwenche Research Institute, claimed that more than 6,000 families in the South-East had been unable to establish the whereabouts of their sons and daughters who allegedly went missing in the custody of security personnel between January 2021 and July 2026.

The organisations also alleged that thousands of civilians had been abducted or killed in different parts of the country during the period under review.

The report, released on Sunday, claimed that at least 299 Christians were killed and 213 others abducted across Nigeria in July 2026.

It attributed the reported deaths and abductions to what it described as attacks by jihadist groups and actions involving state and non-state actors.

The report was signed by Emeka Umeagbalasi, Lead Researcher and Head of Intersociety Nigeria; Chidinma Evangeline Udegbunam, Head of Campaign and Publicity, Intersociety; Obianuju Joy Igboeli, Head of Civil Liberties and Rule of Law, Intersociety; Prof. Justin Akujieze, President and Chairman of the Board, Ekwenche Research Institute, USA; and Mazi Luke Nwannunu, Secretary and Chair of the Finance Committee, Ekwenche Research Institute.

According to the report, “at least 299 defenceless and peaceful Christians were killed by Islamic Jihadists in Nigeria, particularly in Benue, Plateau, Southern Kaduna, Adamawa, Niger, Taraba, among others; during which no fewer than 213 others were abducted.”

It further estimated that about 150 predominantly indigenous Hausa Muslims were killed during the month.

The organisations also claimed that at least six churches came under attack, while two Catholic seminarians were abducted in Enugu and Kogi, one Catholic priest was killed and four pastors were either killed or abducted.

A breakdown in the report indicated that Benue recorded the highest number of alleged Christian deaths, with 65 fatalities and 30 abductions.

It said Southern Kaduna recorded 58 Christian deaths and 70 abductions, while Plateau recorded 55 deaths and at least 10 abductions.

Adamawa was said to have recorded 35 Christian deaths, followed by Niger with 30, while Southern Kebbi recorded six deaths and 18 abductions.

The report also listed 20 abducted Christians each in Southern Borno, Kogi and Edo.

It claimed that at least 40 other Christian deaths occurred in different parts of the country, including the South-East.

The groups said their findings indicated an average of 10 Christian deaths and seven abductions daily during the month under review.

South-East concerns

The report also raised concerns over alleged disappearances and security operations in the South-East.

It claimed that about 11,000 families across the region had been unable to trace relatives who allegedly disappeared during security operations or amid violence.

Of the figure, the organisations estimated that about 70 per cent involved people who allegedly went missing in connection with military operations in the South-East since January 2021.

They further attributed 20 per cent of the alleged disappearances to police operations and 10 per cent to personnel of the State Security Service, SSS.

The organisations also claimed that more than 5,000 people abducted during security operations linked to pro-Biafra self-determination protests between August 2015 and July 2026 had not been traced by their families or lawyers.

The report alleged that some of the missing persons were taken to detention facilities outside the region, but did not provide independently verifiable evidence establishing the whereabouts of the alleged detainees.

It also made allegations of unlawful killings, custodial deaths and other human rights violations involving security agencies in the South-East.

The organisations claimed that more than 11,000 civilians had allegedly been killed in controversial circumstances by security personnel in the region between August 2015 and July 2026.

They cited the security operations of September 2017 in parts of Abia State as one of the incidents requiring further investigation.

According to the report, more than 180 civilians were allegedly killed during security operations between September 11 and 14, 2017, in Afara-Ukwu and other parts of Umuahia, Asa, Aba, Ogwe and Isiala-Ngwa.

It further claimed that hundreds of people were abducted and remained unaccounted for.

The organisations also alleged that security operations linked to pro-Biafra activities had contributed to distrust among some residents of the South-East.

Alleged attacks in communities

The report further claimed that at least 20 rural communities in the South-East were facing threats or attacks attributed by the organisations to armed herders.

It identified communities in Enugu, Anambra, Imo, Abia and Ebonyi states, as well as parts of neighbouring Delta State.

The organisations identified Ezeagu, Isi-Uzo, Uzo-Uwani and Nkanu East Local Government Areas of Enugu State as areas requiring particular attention.

The report alleged that several communities in Ezeagu had experienced insecurity over the years, while communities including Eha-Amufu and Mgbuji in Isi-Uzo had been affected by attacks and displacement.

It also alleged the destruction of places of worship and loss of lives in the affected communities.

In Uzo-Uwani, the organisations claimed that several communities had experienced displacement as a result of insecurity.

Intersociety and Ekwenche Research Institute said the findings underscored the need for further investigation into alleged human rights violations, disappearances and attacks in the South-East.

The organisations argued that the alleged disappearances and security-related concerns had contributed to distrust among some young people in the region towards military service.

However, as of the time of filing this report, the Nigerian military, police and other security agencies had not publicly responded to the latest allegations contained in the report.

World.title: ‘Cheap product’, Babachir Lawal mocks Atiku’s presidential bid
World.content:
Babachir Lawal

..Slams ADC, threatens legal action over Adamawa candidate substitution

By Omeiza Ajayi

ABUJA — Former Secretary to the Government of the Federation, SGF, Babachir Lawal, has criticised the presidential candidacy of former Vice President Atiku Abubakar under the African Democratic Congress, ADC, while also faulting the party’s handling of its Adamawa State governorship primary.

Lawal made the remarks in a Facebook post on Sunday titled “Kachalla Series Three,” in which he alleged that the ADC replaced Engr. Umar Suleiman, whom he said won the party’s Adamawa governorship primary, with Tukur Moddibo.

He attributed the alleged substitution to ethnic considerations and claimed that Atiku influenced the decision.

In the post, Lawal compared Atiku and the ADC’s candidate-selection process to products purchased from TEMU, an online marketplace.

He wrote: “As the story goes on the streets in the state, APC donated its gubernatorial candidate to the state having purchased him from TEMU the cheap online market place, and it appears that the ADC too has just done likewise, aside giving to the nation a presidential candidate that looks more like he too was a cheap product from TEMU.”

Lawal further alleged that the substitution of Suleiman with Moddibo was influenced by pressure from Atiku and accused the former vice president of favouring candidates on ethnic and religious grounds.

He said Suleiman was a “very competent and experienced gentleman” who, in his view, posed a strong challenge to what he described as an attempt to maintain political dominance in the state.

Lawal also alleged that the substitution violated the Electoral Act 2026, the ADC Constitution and the party’s Primary Election Guidelines.

He said he would challenge the matter in court.

“This criminal substitution which violates the Electoral Act 2026, the ADC Constitution, and the ADC Primary Elections Guidelines will be tested in the courts and it will fail woefully,” he said.

Lawal further said he believed voters in Adamawa State would reject what he described as an attempt to impose a candidate on them.

He predicted that both the ADC and the All Progressives Congress, APC, could lose the governorship election, while noting that voters had other candidates and political parties to choose from.

“The Adamawa masses trust God that both the ADC and APC will lose the gubernatorial elections in the state,” he said.
